# affectUI

> Agent-ready React UI for AI products and SaaS: 132 components, screens, blocks, illustrations and motion effects. Every item is one .tsx file with its styles inside – no Tailwind, no animation library, no other dependencies. React 19, dark mode and reduced motion built in.

40 items are free and open source (MIT). The other 92 are part of affectUI Pro, a one-time purchase (https://www.affectui.com/pricing).

## How to add an item

- Free items: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/<slug>.json` – the file lands in components/ui.
- Short names: register `"@affectui": "https://www.affectui.com/r/{name}.json"` under "registries" in components.json, then `npx shadcn@latest add @affectui/<slug>`.
- Pro items: the same commands, with the buyer's access key (AFFECTUI_TOKEN, created under https://www.affectui.com/account/downloads) sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` – set it as a header on the @affectui registry in components.json. Without a key the registry answers 401.
- Import from `@/components/ui/<slug>` and keep the component's own styles and motion; adapt only content and props.
- MCP server: https://www.affectui.com/api/mcp (Streamable HTTP) – search items, read docs and fetch source from Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Codex.


---

## Agent Checkpoints (Pro)

An agent's run as a line of checkpoints, like git for agents – rewind to any of them and a new attempt branches out of it, while the one it left fades back but stays

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-checkpoints
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-checkpoints.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-checkpoints`

### When to use

- Long agent runs where a wrong turn shouldn't cost the whole run – rewind to the last good checkpoint and let it try again
- Showing that nothing is lost: an attempt you rewound from stays visible, faded, and you can go back to it
- Coding agents, research agents, anything that saves its state step by step

### When not to use

- Steps of a plan that haven't happened yet – use Agent Plan
- How long each step took against its plan – use Plan vs Actual
- Several agents at once – use Agent Fleet

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentCheckpoints, type Checkpoint } from "@/components/ui/agent-checkpoints";

const checkpoints: Checkpoint[] = [
  { id: "c1", title: "Read the brief", at: 9_000 },
  { id: "c2", parent: "c1", title: "Built the pricing table", files: 3, at: 64_000 },
  { id: "c3", parent: "c2", title: "Tests failing – 4 of 12", status: "failed", at: 131_000 },
  // A second checkpoint after c2 starts a new attempt
  { id: "c4", parent: "c2", title: "Switched to Stripe Elements", status: "running", at: 169_000 },
];

export function Run() {
  return <AgentCheckpoints checkpoints={checkpoints} head="c4" onRewind={(c) => agent.restoreFrom(c.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| checkpoints | `Checkpoint[]` |  | { id, title, icon?, parent?, status?, at?, files?, cost? } in the order they were taken – pass them again whenever one is added or changes; icon is a small mark before the title, e.g. the logo of the tool it worked with |
| parent | `string` |  | Per checkpoint, the one it follows – a checkpoint whose parent already has a later one starts a new attempt on its own lane |
| status | `"running" \| "done" \| "failed" \| "stopped"` | `"done"` | Per checkpoint – running shimmers, failed gets a badge, stopped means you rewound away while the agent worked toward it |
| head | `string` | `the last checkpoint` | Id of the checkpoint the agent stands on – the way to it is blue, everything off it fades back |
| onRewind | `(checkpoint: Checkpoint) => void` |  | Rewind was pressed – add a new checkpoint with this one as its parent, and move head to it |
| task | `string` |  | What the run is for, next to the title |
| formatTime | `(ms: number) => string` | `0:42 / 1:05` | Formats at |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats the total in the bar on top |
| title | `string` | `"Checkpoints"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Moves between the checkpoints
- Home / End: Jumps to the first or the last checkpoint
- Enter / Space: Rewinds to the focused checkpoint

### Accessibility

- The checkpoints are an ordered list with one tab stop; the arrow keys move between them
- Every row says its title, its attempt, its status and whether it's current or left behind; the current one has aria-current="step"
- The Rewind button is a pointer shortcut – from the keyboard, Enter on the row does the same
- The count in the bar on top is announced politely when it changes
- Status is never color alone: failed has a badge, stopped says so, the current checkpoint is announced

### Motion

- A new checkpoint rises in, its dot pops and the line to it draws itself down – the card grows smoothly to make room
- A rewind bends a new lane out of the checkpoint you picked and draws it down to the new attempt; the attempt you left turns gray and fades back
- A new checkpoint's dot gets one short glint as it arrives; while the agent works toward it, its title shimmers
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything simply appears

### Responsive

- Every row has a fixed height, so nothing jumps when a checkpoint finishes or fails – Rewind takes the place of files and time
- Past fourteen checkpoints the list scrolls inside the card and keeps the current one in view
- Narrow, the task and the file counts give way first
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Never remove checkpoints after a rewind – add the new one with the rewound-to checkpoint as its parent; the old attempt stays and fades back by itself
- Mark what the agent was working on when you rewind as "stopped"
- Lanes come from parent links alone: the first child keeps its parent's lane, every later child opens a new attempt
- The rail's blue is --ui-ack-link (#82bcff), the same as Agent Tree; how far an attempt left behind fades is --ui-ack-dim

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-plan, plan-vs-actual, agent-tree, agent-ledger

---

## Agent Cursors (Pro)

Agents working in a document like teammates in a multiplayer editor – live pointers with names, suggestions typed letter by letter, images they resize, code they fix and comments beside the page

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-cursors
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-cursors.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-cursors`

### When to use

- Agents that write or edit a document, a brief or a spec while you watch – text, images, code and comments – and you want to see who is where
- Several agents on one text at once: each change stays a suggestion in its agent's color until you accept it
- Making agent work feel like working with teammates – the same pointers people know from Figma or Google Docs

### When not to use

- One agent rewriting a reply – use Writing Assistant or Inline Diff
- Changes to code or files – use Inline Diff or Change Summary
- Who started which agent – use Agent Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentCursors, acceptSuggestion } from "@/components/ui/agent-cursors";

// One shared ink for all of them – their logos tell them apart (pass color to give one its own)
const agents = [
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", avatar: <ClaudeLogo /> },
  { id: "writer", name: "Writer", avatar: <OpenAILogo /> },
];

export function Brief() {
  const [doc, setDoc] = useState({ blocks, suggestions: [] });
  // From your agents' stream: where each one is and what it does
  const cursors = {
    research: { block: "why", at: 24, select: 9, doing: "Checking the numbers" },
    writer: { block: "list", at: 31, doing: "Adding detail", typing: true },
  };

  return (
    <AgentCursors
      title="Launch brief"
      agents={agents}
      blocks={doc.blocks}
      suggestions={doc.suggestions}
      cursors={cursors}
      onAccept={(s) => setDoc((d) => acceptSuggestion(d.blocks, d.suggestions, s.id))}
      onReject={(s) => setDoc((d) => ({ ...d, suggestions: d.suggestions.filter((x) => x.id !== s.id) }))}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `CursorAgent[]` |  | { id, name, color?, avatar?, tint?, cost? } – everyone who can be in the document; without a color every agent shares one ink (near-black, light in dark mode) and the logos tell them apart |
| blocks | `DocBlock[]` |  | { id, kind?: "title" | "heading" | "paragraph" | "item" | "code" | "image", text?, … } – the document; consecutive items form one list. Images take width (0–1), ratio, float ("left" | "right" – the next text runs beside them), loading, src and alt; their text is the caption. Tables take rows of cell blocks (the first row is the header); a cell with a tone shows as a status pill |
| cursors | `Record<string, AgentCursor \| null>` |  | Per agent: { block, at?, in?, select?, point?, doing?, typing? } – where it is (a block or a comment), a selected passage or a held image, the corner or middle of an image, what it's doing (on its flag) and whether it types; null or missing means it left |
| comments | `DocComment[]` |  | { id, agent, block, at?, x?, y?, text, open? } – comment pins on the page: on a character of the block (at), or at its top edge x along the page (0–1); y moves it down; open keeps the window open (e.g. while the agent writes), otherwise a dark round pin with the agent's mark that grows into the window on hover |
| onResolveComment | `(comment: DocComment) => void` |  | The black check in a comment's window – remove it from your list |
| onReply | `(comment: DocComment, text: string) => void` |  | Shows a reply field in the window; Enter sends |
| height | `number` |  | A fixed page height in px – the rest of the document fades out towards the bottom |
| tabs / tab / onTabChange | `{ id, label }[] / string / (id) => void` |  | Tabs above the page – the open one white with a stroke; you switch the blocks and agents |
| agents[].cost | `number` |  | Per agent: what it has cost so far – a small tag on its flag, the total in the header |
| agents[].tint | `string` |  | Per agent: the fill of its face while you follow it – defaults to a light wash of its color |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats every cost |
| suggestions | `DocSuggestion[]` | `[]` | { id, agent, block, at, remove?, insert?, note? } – changes waiting for you: removed text is struck through, new text underlined, both in the agent's color |
| onAccept / onReject | `(suggestion: DocSuggestion) => void` |  | From the window that opens on a suggestion – acceptSuggestion() writes one into your blocks |
| onAcceptAll | `() => void` |  | Shows "Accept all" in the header when there is more than one suggestion |
| following / onFollowingChange | `string \| null` |  | The agent you follow, controlled or uncontrolled – the other pointers and selections fade back |
| title | `string` | `"Untitled"` | The document's name in the header |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| acceptSuggestion | `(blocks, suggestions, id) => { blocks, suggestions }` |  | Helper: writes a suggestion into the text and moves the other suggestions in that block along |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves to the faces in the header, then from suggestion to suggestion – a focused suggestion opens its window
- Enter / Space: On a face: follow that agent, or stop following
- Esc: Closes the window of a suggestion

### Accessibility

- The text is real text in headings, paragraphs and a list – pointers, carets and selections are decoration and hidden from screen readers
- Every suggestion is focusable and labelled, e.g. "Researcher suggests adding: 38%"; its window is a dialog with Accept and Reject buttons
- The faces are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) named after the agent and what it is doing; a followed face fills with its tint
- New suggestions are announced politely, with the agent's note

### Motion

- Pointers glide to their next place; a new one pops in where it lands, one that leaves fades out where it was
- Images are gray with a light shimmer running across while they load, then fade in; a held image resizes smoothly while the pointer stays on its corner handle
- A comment pin grows into its window on hover and folds back into it – the agent's mark stays and slides to the corner
- While an agent types, its caret holds still and the pointer follows every letter
- What an agent is doing slides out next to its name on the flag
- Selected passages fade in behind the text in the agent's color; new suggestions fill in softly
- While an agent is in the document, an arc in its color runs around its face, fading in from nothing – like a loader
- Switching tabs fades the new view in; table rows an agent adds slide in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything moves at once

### Responsive

- Every position is measured from the page itself, so any width, font size or zoom works – the pointers stay on their letters while the text wraps
- Comment windows open towards the bottom right – towards the left near the right edge, upwards near the bottom
- Flags always sit to the bottom right of their pointer; near the right edge they are cut off rather than moved
- Below 520px the page gets tighter margins and the suggestion count in the header gives way to the faces
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Offsets are character indexes into the block's current text – after accepting a suggestion, use the text that acceptSuggestion returns
- A cursor inside a suggestion (in: id) counts its offset in that suggestion's insert text
- Pass new cursors as your agents stream – the component animates between any two states, it doesn't need every step
- Flags and comment pins are dark cards with a pink-to-blue bottom edge (--ui-agc-flag, --ui-agc-edge); in dark mode they turn light
- The pointer is the soft, rounded arrow from the affectUI videos, filled in the agent's color

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: writing-assistant, inline-diff, agent-tree, comment-thread

---

## Agent Findings (Pro)

A swarm of agents checking something – one calm row per agent with its progress, and their findings sliding into a short feed as they're found

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-findings
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-findings.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-findings`

### When to use

- Several agents check, audit or verify something in parallel and people want to follow along without drowning in detail
- Security reviews, code audits, test runs, data checks – anything that turns up findings as it goes

### When not to use

- When it matters who started whom – use Agent Tree
- When the timeline matters – use Agent Lanes or Trace Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentFindings, type FindingAgent, type Finding } from "@/components/ui/agent-findings";

export function Run({ agents, findings }: { agents: FindingAgent[]; findings: Finding[] }) {
  return (
    <AgentFindings
      title="Verification"
      agents={agents} // { id, name, model?, avatar?, step?, done, total, status? }
      findings={findings} // { id, agentId, title, severity: "critical" | "warning" | "note", location?, at }
      onOpen={(finding) => openFinding(finding.id)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `FindingAgent[]` |  | One row each: name, current step, checks done of total; status defaults to running until done reaches total |
| findings | `Finding[]` |  | What the agents found, with severity, where and when – the newest come first in the feed |
| title | `string` | `"Verification"` | Heading in the bar |
| rows | `number` | `4` | How many findings the feed shows at most – it grows to that height as they come in |
| now | `number` |  | A clock you control for the “2m” times – without it they follow real time |
| onOpen | `(finding: Finding) => void` |  | A finding was clicked |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the agents and the findings in the feed
- Enter / Space: On an agent: shows only its findings (again: all); on a finding: opens it

### Accessibility

- The feed is a polite live region – new findings are announced as they arrive
- Every severity has a text label for screen readers, not just a color
- Agents are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) for the filter

### Responsive

- Below 480px the check counts and locations drop, so the rows keep one line
- Dark mode built in; colors are CSS variables on .ui-af

### Requirements

- React 19

---

## Agent Fleet (Pro)

Several agents side by side – each card sums up its sub-agents, and a click opens its tree to the right while the last one folds back into its card

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-fleet
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-fleet.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-fleet`

### When to use

- Several agents working at the same time – a launch, the support queue, a release – each with sub-agents of its own
- Seeing at a glance which agent needs you, which one failed and what the whole fleet costs – without every tree open at once
- A fleet overview on a dashboard: one tree open, the others folded to a single card

### When not to use

- One run with one orchestrator – use Agent Tree
- When things happened, in time order – use Agent Lanes
- Handing tasks to agents yourself – use Delegate Board

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentFleet, type FleetAgent } from "@/components/ui/agent-fleet";

const fleet: FleetAgent[] = [
  {
    id: "launch", name: "Launch lead", model: "Opus 5.5", task: "Launch the new pricing page",
    status: "running", cost: 0.42, started: Date.now() - 840_000,
    children: [
      { id: "research", name: "Researcher", task: "Compare five competitors", status: "done", cost: 0.31, started: Date.now() - 780_000, ended: Date.now() - 360_000 },
      { id: "copy", name: "Writer", task: "Write the plan copy", status: "waiting", cost: 0.18, started: Date.now() - 720_000 },
    ],
  },
  { id: "support", name: "Support lead", task: "Answer the open tickets", status: "running", cost: 0.12, started: Date.now() - 1_560_000 },
];

export function Fleet() {
  return <AgentFleet agents={fleet} onSelect={(agent) => openLog(agent.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `FleetAgent[]` |  | { id, name, task, model?, avatar?, tools?, status, steps?, cost?, started?, ended?, children? } – the main agents, each with its sub-agents; pass them again whenever something changes; tools are small marks shown as overlapping tiles before the task |
| steps | `FleetStep[]` |  | Per sub-agent, { title, status?, tool?, took? } – the tasks it worked through; a click on its card opens them in a small window |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "waiting" \| "done" \| "failed" \| "stopped"` |  | Per agent – "waiting" reads "Needs you"; queued and stopped sub-agents and their connectors are muted |
| cost | `number` |  | Per agent, its own cost – a main agent shows its whole branch, the bar the whole fleet |
| open / defaultOpen | `string \| null` | `the first agent` | Id of the main agent whose tree is open, controlled or uncontrolled – null folds them all |
| onOpenChange | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | An agent was opened – or folded with a second click |
| ask / error | `string` |  | Per sub-agent – what a waiting one needs you to decide, and what went wrong for a failed one; shown at the top of its window above Approve and Reject, or Retry and Dismiss |
| onResolve | `(agent, action: "approve" \| "reject" \| "retry" \| "dismiss") => void` |  | An answer for a sub-agent that needs you or failed – update its status in your data; without it, those cards get no Answer or Resolve button |
| onSelect | `(agent: FleetAgent) => void` |  | A click on a sub-agent – makes the sub-agent cards clickable; one with steps opens its tasks window as well |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for running times – without it the cards tick every second while an agent runs |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Agents"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Moves between the main agents
- Home / End: Jumps to the first or the last main agent
- Enter / Space: On a main agent: opens its tree, or folds it when it's open – on a sub-agent: opens or closes its tasks window
- Tab: Moves on into the open tree's cards – those with steps, an answer to give or onSelect; in an answer window, Approve or Retry has focus and Tab reaches the other
- Esc: Closes the tasks window and puts focus back on its card

### Accessibility

- Every main agent is a button with aria-expanded, pointing at the open tree with aria-controls
- The open tree is a tree labelled "Sub-agents of …"; every sub-agent is a treeitem labelled with its name and status
- The totals in the bar – agents, running, needs you, cost – are announced politely when they change
- Status is never color alone: every card spells it out, and the phrase under each main agent says what the ring shows
- The small Answer or Resolve button on a card is a pointer shortcut – keyboard users open the same window from the card itself
- A sub-agent with steps, or one that needs you or failed, has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded; its tasks window is a dialog labelled "Tasks of …", closed by Esc or a click elsewhere

### Motion

- The agent you open stays as it is while the others fade back to half – hover brings one forward again
- The open tree leaves first – bottom card first, while its connectors pull back into the card – then the new connectors draw themselves out and the cards rise in one after another
- The tree stands centered on its agent, as far as the column reaches; when it grows while open, it glides to its new place
- Costs that still climb carry a light shimmer
- A sub-agent's tasks window drops down from its card, the tasks fading in one after another
- With prefers-reduced-motion the trees switch at once

### Responsive

- Wide enough for the column, a gap and the deepest tree, the tree opens to the right of the column
- Narrower, the tree opens under its card and pushes the agents below down – and folds back up before the next one opens
- Every card has a fixed height – one line of task, one line of numbers – so nothing jumps when a status changes
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole fleet every time something changes – ids keep the cards in place, a new sub-agent rises in with a drawn connector
- cost is the agent's own spend; the component adds the sub-agents up, so don't pre-sum it
- The phrase under a main agent picks the most urgent thing: needs you, then failed, then running, then done
- The connector color is --ui-agf-link (#82bcff), the same blue as Agent Tree; how far the other agents fade is --ui-agf-dim
- The progress circle under a main agent is a ring with a pie inside, like Linear's "In progress": the pie is the share of sub-agents that are through (done, failed or stopped); it's gray, like the phrase next to it, e.g. "2/4 running"
- Steps without a status count as done and show how long they took; the others say where they stand on the right – Running (shimmering), Needs you or Failed in bold, Queued or Skipped faint
- The status glyphs are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-tree, agent-lanes, agent-monitor, delegate-board

---

## Agent Graph (Pro)

Agents and the tools they call as a living network – a pulse along the link for every call and its answer, busy links growing thicker, agents that breathe while they work and turn amber when they need you

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-graph
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-graph.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-graph`

### When to use

- A live overview of a multi-agent system: which agents run, which tools and data sources they call, and how busy each link is
- Spotting at a glance who waits for you, which call failed and where the traffic (and the cost) goes
- A hero or status view next to a log or a chat – click a node to see what it does and its latest calls

### When not to use

- Who started whom, with status and cost per sub-agent – use Agent Tree
- When things happened, in time order – use Agent Lanes
- One agent's single tool call in detail – use Tool Call Card
- Graphs with dozens of agents – the orbits are made for a handful of agents and up to a dozen tools

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentGraph, type GraphNode, type GraphCall } from "@/components/ui/agent-graph";

const nodes: GraphNode[] = [
  { id: "lead", kind: "agent", name: "Orchestrator", detail: "Opus 5.5", status: "working", lead: true },
  { id: "research", kind: "agent", name: "Researcher", detail: "Sonnet 5.5", status: "working", cost: 0.12 },
  { id: "web", kind: "tool", name: "Web search", short: "Search" },
  { id: "notion", kind: "tool", name: "Notion", icon: <NotionLogo /> },
  { id: "you", kind: "user", name: "You" },
];

// Newest last – every new id sends a pulse; when "pending" turns "ok" or "error" the answer travels back
const calls: GraphCall[] = [
  { id: "c1", from: "lead", to: "research", at: Date.now() - 4000, status: "pending", label: "Compare pricing" },
  { id: "c2", from: "research", to: "web", at: Date.now() - 900, status: "ok", ms: 820, label: "pricing linear.app" },
];

export function Live() {
  return <AgentGraph nodes={nodes} calls={calls} edges={[["you", "lead"], ["research", "notion"]]} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| nodes | `GraphNode[]` |  | { id, name, kind, short?, icon?, detail?, status?, doing?, cost?, lead? } – every agent, tool and user; pass the whole list each time, ids keep nodes in place and new ids grow in |
| kind | `"agent" \| "tool" \| "user"` |  | Per node – agents sit on the inner orbit (the lead in the middle), tools and you on the outer one, each turned towards the agents it talks to |
| status | `"idle" \| "working" \| "waiting" \| "error" \| "done"` |  | Per node – working agents breathe, waiting turns amber ("Needs you"), error red; waiting and error also show a chip in the bar |
| short | `string` |  | Per node – a shorter label for narrow containers, e.g. "Search" |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Per node – a logo or mark; defaults to the initials (a person for the user) |
| detail / doing | `string` |  | Per node – the model or what a tool is (under the agent's name and in its card), and what it is doing right now (in its card) |
| cost | `number` |  | Per node – what it has cost so far; the bar sums all nodes |
| lead | `boolean` | `first agent` | Per node – the agent in the middle |
| calls | `GraphCall[]` | `[]` | { id, from, to, at, status?, label?, ms? } – recent calls, newest last. A new id sends a pulse from → to; when its status turns "ok" the answer travels back as a hollow dot, "error" comes back red and flashes the link. Calls also create the links they need |
| edges | `[string, string][]` | `[]` | Links that are always there, even before their first call |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for calls per minute and link heat – without it the graph ticks every second |
| heatWindow | `number` | `20000` | How far back (ms) calls count towards a link's thickness – the busiest link is about 4px, a quiet one 1.25px |
| onSelect | `(node: GraphNode \| null) => void` |  | A node was clicked (its card opens) – null when the card closes |
| height | `number` | `fits the width` | Fixed height of the graph in px – by default 0.6 × the width (360–520px) when wide, 1.2 × when narrow |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Agent graph"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between the nodes (and the "needs you" / "failed" chips); a focused node lights up its neighbourhood
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes the focused node's card
- Esc: Closes the card and returns focus to its node

### Accessibility

- Every node is a button labelled with its name, kind, status, what it does and its calls in the last minute; aria-expanded tells whether its card is open
- The card is a dialog; its close button takes focus, Esc closes it
- A visually hidden list gives the same picture as text: every node, its status, whom it called how often in the last minute and its cost
- "needs you" and "failed" chips sit in a polite live region, so a waiting or failed agent is announced
- Status is never color alone: waiting and failed agents get a badge (clock, exclamation mark) and a text line under the name

### Motion

- On the first draw the lead pops in, then the agents, then the tools around the orbit – each link draws itself towards the node it reaches
- Every call sends a solid dot with a short tail along its link; the answer comes back as a hollow dot, amber for you, red for an error – the node it lands on ripples once
- Links thicken with use (stroke-width eases over 0.7s) and fade back after six quiet seconds; a link lights up while a pulse runs along it
- Working agents breathe with a soft ring, waiting ones a little quicker in amber
- When nodes come or go every node glides to its new place on a spring – a new tool slides out of the first agent it is linked to; a leaving one shrinks away while its link pulls back
- One requestAnimationFrame loop drives gliding and pulses; it pauses when the graph is off screen or the tab is hidden
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing glides or travels: a link simply lights up for each call

### Responsive

- The width is measured with a ResizeObserver and the whole layout is computed from it – orbits, node sizes and label room
- Below 520px the graph turns taller than wide, nodes get smaller, labels use their short names, the model line is left out and the card docks to the bottom of the graph
- Labels and the outer orbit always stay inside the panel – nothing is cut off and nothing scrolls sideways, down to 320px
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole nodes and calls arrays every time something changes; a call's id must stay the same while its status goes from pending to ok/error
- Calls older than four seconds when they first appear don't send a pulse – they only count towards heat and calls per minute
- Brand logos are not part of the component – pass them as icon; the UI icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT), keep the credit comment
- The link color is --ui-agg-link (#82bcff), the soft blue of Agent Tree; pulses use --ui-agg-pulse
- Keep it to a handful of agents and about a dozen outer nodes – more get crowded on the outer orbit

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-tree, agent-lanes, tool-call-card, integration-picker

---

## Agent Handoff (Pro)

A task passed from agent to agent like a relay – at every handoff what went along to the next one, and what got lost on the way

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-handoff
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-handoff.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-handoff`

### When to use

- Several agents work on tasks one after another – research, analysis, writing, review – and people need to see what each one passed on
- Debugging multi-agent pipelines: where did the context get lost?
- Letting people push a task on to a later agent and watch it travel down the relay

### When not to use

- Agents working side by side at the same time – use Agent Lanes
- Who started whom, as a hierarchy – use Agent Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentHandoff, type HandoffAgent, type Handoff } from "@/components/ui/agent-handoff";

const agents: HandoffAgent[] = [
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", model: "Opus 5.5", avatar: <ClaudeLogo /> },
  { id: "writer", name: "Writer", model: "GPT-5", avatar: <OpenAILogo /> },
];

const handoffs: Handoff[] = [
  {
    id: "launch-1", from: "research", to: "writer", task: "Launch post",
    items: [
      { id: "brief", label: "launch-brief.md", kind: "file" },
      { id: "quotes", label: "3 user quotes", kind: "note", lost: true, why: "Over the writer's context budget" },
    ],
  },
];

<AgentHandoff
  agents={agents}
  handoffs={handoffs}
  tasks={[
    { id: "launch", title: "Launch post", logo: <NotionLogo />, status: "working", agent: "writer", note: "Drafting" },
    { id: "pricing", title: "Pricing page copy", logo: <NotionLogo />, status: "todo" },
  ]}
  onAssign={(task, agent) => run(task.id, agent.id)}
  onRestore={(handoff, item) => passOn(handoff.id, item.id)}
/>
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `HandoffAgent[]` |  | In relay order: { id, name, model?, avatar?, description? } – each card shows what it's for and the task it's on, taken from tasks |
| handoffs | `Handoff[]` |  | What was handed over: { id, from, to, task, items } – each lands as a card in the column between from and to, latest on top; a new id sends light along its lines |
| items | `HandoffItem[]` |  | Per handoff: { id, label, kind?: "file" | "source" | "fact" | "decision" | "note", lost?, why? } – lost ones are struck through, why shows on hover |
| tasks | `HandoffTask[]` |  | Every task: { id, title, logo?, status: "todo" | "working" | "done" | "warning", agent?, note? } – handoffs refer to them by title for the logo and where the task is now; the first agent shows the next todo one as up next |
| onAssign | `(task, agent) => void` |  | A handoff card was dropped on an agent to the right of its column – give that task to it and keep handoffs and tasks up to date. Cards only move on down the relay, never back |
| onRestore | `(handoff, item) => void` |  | Adds "Add back" to a lost item's card – pass it on after all |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the waiting tasks, the agents (while a task is picked up) and the handed-over items
- Enter / Space: Opens a card or an agent's task; with a card picked up, gives it to the focused agent; on a lost item: shows why, and Add back

### Accessibility

- Tasks can be given to an agent without dragging: double-tap a card, then tap an agent to its right
- Each column and each handoff's items are labelled lists; cards and lost items are buttons with aria-expanded

### Motion

- At a handoff a short streak of light with a soft glow runs along the rounded line into the top of the column, the card drops in, and the light runs on out of it to the next agent
- A card opens in place to show everything that went along; a lost thing opens to say why
- A dragged card follows the pointer; an agent it can go to lifts and rings in blue, the ones it has passed step back
- Cards keep their size – an agent shows one line for its task, a handoff card three lines; the columns fade out at the bottom
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Below about 760px the status shows as an icon only; below 620px the relay stacks into one column – an agent, its handoff, the next agent 
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component draws – your code runs the relay: on onAssign, set that task to working with the agent; when it finishes, push a Handoff to the next agent and move the task on (or to done / warning at the end)
- Mark what didn't make it with lost: true and a short why – that's the point of the component

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-lanes, agent-tree, context-map, trace-waterfall

---

## Agent Inbox (Pro)

All your background agent tasks in one calm list – live clocks and status tags, filter tabs with rolling counts, rows that unfold to the last steps with Approve, Reject, Retry or Open, and glide to their new place

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-inbox
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-inbox.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-inbox`

### When to use

- Agent products where several tasks run in the background and people come back to see what finished, what failed and what waits for them
- A home screen or dashboard that collects approvals from many runs in one calm board, instead of one modal per agent
- Job queues in general – imports, syncs, evaluations – where each job has a short description, a short history and one next step

### When not to use

- One single approval in the flow of a chat – use Approval Card
- The plan of one run, step by step – use Agent Plan; for a single tool call use Tool Call Card
- Hundreds of jobs – the board is for a few dozen at most; page or search a bigger queue in a table

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentInbox } from "@/components/ui/agent-inbox";

export function Tasks() {
  return (
    <AgentInbox
      tasks={[
        {
          id: "migrate",
          title: "Migrate users table",
          description: "Split users into accounts and profiles. The dry run on staging passed.",
          agent: "Opus 5.5",
          status: "waiting",
          startedAt: Date.now() - 6 * 60_000,
          tools: 14,
          sources: 9,
          steps: [
            { label: "Dry run on staging – no errors", time: "2m ago" },
            { label: "Wants to run it on production", time: "1m ago" },
          ],
        },
        { id: "notes", title: "Release notes v2.4", agent: "Sonnet 5.5", status: "running", startedAt: Date.now() - 80_000 },
        { id: "digest", title: "Weekly metrics digest", agent: "Haiku 5.5", status: "done", elapsed: 252_000 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `AgentTask[]` |  | { id, title, description?, agent, status, startedAt?, elapsed?, tools?, sources?, steps? } – status is "running", "waiting", "done" or "failed"; steps are { label, time? }, oldest first |
| onApprove | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Approve on a waiting task. Without it the task turns running inside the board |
| onReject | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Reject on a waiting task. Without it the task turns failed |
| onRetry | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Retry on a failed task. Without it the task runs again and its clock starts over |
| onOpen | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Shows an Open button on running and done tasks |
| title | `string` | `"Agent inbox"` | Heading on the left of the bar, after "Agents /" |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | A button in the bar next to the layout switch, e.g. New task |
| view | `"board" \| "list"` |  | Controlled layout |
| defaultView | `"board" \| "list"` | `"board"` | Starting layout when uncontrolled |
| onViewChange | `(view: AgentInboxView) => void` |  | Called when Board or List is picked |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the layout switch, the cards and the buttons inside an open card
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes a card, presses Approve, Reject, Retry or Open
- Esc: Closes the open card and puts focus back on it

### Accessibility

- Each column is a labeled section; each card is a button with aria-expanded, and a closed card's details are inert
- Board / List is a radio group
- A polite live region says how many tasks need you and how many run

### Motion

- Running tasks spin a small ring and their clock ticks every second
- When a status changes, the card shows its new state in place first, then glides over to its new column (FLIP)
- Cards open in place to the last steps as a tiny timeline and the buttons for what you can do now
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Three columns from about 620px; narrower containers always get the list and hide the switch – it works down to 300px
- Touch screens: taller cards and buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass startedAt for running and waiting tasks so the clock ticks; pass elapsed for finished ones
- Columns: Needs you holds waiting and failed tasks, then Running and Done; inside a column the cards keep your order
- Keep the description to one or two sentences on what the task is about or where it stands – it is clamped to two lines
- With a handler the board never changes a status by itself – update the task in your state and the card follows

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: approval-card, agent-plan, tool-call-card, decision-inbox

## Agent Lanes (Pro)

Where every agent is right now – a live timeline with a lane per agent, tasks growing into “now”, hand-offs drawn between agents and approvals right on the block

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-lanes
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-lanes.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-lanes`

### When to use

- A team of agents works in parallel and people want to see at a glance who is doing what, and since when
- Multi-agent pipelines where work moves from one agent to the next (research → writing → review)
- A control room for agents: spot the one that waits for a decision, or failed, without opening each run

### When not to use

- A list of background tasks grouped by state – use Agent Inbox
- The steps of one single run – use Agent Plan or Agent Steering
- Scheduling future work on a calendar – the lanes show the last half hour, not the week ahead

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentLanes, type LaneAgent, type LaneTask } from "@/components/ui/agent-lanes";

const agents: LaneAgent[] = [
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", model: "Opus 5.5" },
  { id: "writer", name: "Writer", model: "Sonnet 5.5" },
];

export function AgentRoom({ tasks }: { tasks: LaneTask[] }) {
  return (
    <AgentLanes
      agents={agents}
      tasks={tasks} // { id, agentId, title, status, start, end?, handoffTo?, ask? }
      onApprove={(task) => api.approve(task.id)}
      onReject={(task) => api.reject(task.id)}
      onOpen={(task) => router.push(`/runs/${task.id}`)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `LaneAgent[]` |  | One lane each: { id, name, model?, avatar? }. A logo as avatar sits on a white tile; without one the initials show. Free agents get an Idle tag, waiting ones Needs you |
| tasks | `LaneTask[]` |  | { id, agentId, title, status: "done" | "running" | "waiting" | "failed", start, end?, handoffTo?, ask?, summary?, tools? }. No end: the block reaches "now" |
| span | `number` | `30 minutes` | How much time the lanes show, in ms |
| now | `number` |  | A clock you control, e.g. a faster one for a demo. Without it the lanes follow real time, every second |
| onApprove / onReject | `(task: LaneTask) => void` |  | Approve or Reject on a waiting task. Without handlers the lanes change the status themselves |
| onOpen | `(task: LaneTask) => void` |  | Shows an Open link in the tooltip of a block that doesn't wait |
| title | `string` | `"Agents"` | Heading in the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves from block to block, lane by lane
- Enter: Opens a block's tooltip (what got done), or the decision on a waiting one
- Esc: Closes the decision and returns to its block

### Accessibility

- Every lane is a list labelled with the agent's name; every block is a button that names the agent, task, state and time
- A waiting block controls its decision popover (aria-expanded), which is a labelled dialog with Approve focused
- How many tasks need someone is announced politely when it changes

### Motion

- The window slides with the clock: blocks and hand-off curves are drawn from the same time, so they move together; at the left edge blocks slide out and fade
- Running blocks shimmer, a live hand-off curve flows towards the next agent, waiting flags pulse
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything stays still and only updates

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 760px
- Below 520px the names column shrinks to the avatars
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component draws what it gets – update tasks from your agent events (status, end) and the lanes follow
- Give a waiting task an ask (one sentence on what needs deciding); it shows above Approve / Reject
- Give any task a summary – two or three short points on what got done – for the dark tooltip a click opens
- tools takes up to three small logos (React nodes) of the apps a task works in; they sit on white tiles before the title
- Use handoffTo on the task that hands over, pointing at the id of the next agent's task

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-inbox, agent-plan, agent-steering, approval-card

## Agent Ledger (Pro)

Everything an agent changed in your systems, each change with an undo – before and after per row, and pointing at Undo shows what builds on it: what would be undone too, and what can't be taken back

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-ledger
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-ledger.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-ledger`

### When to use

- An agent works in real systems – code, payments, CRM, docs, chat – and people need to see what it changed and take it back
- An audit trail next to a run, with before and after for every change
- Anywhere undo needs to be honest about consequences: what goes with it, and what can't be undone

### When not to use

- Approving a change before it happens – use Approval Card or Review Center
- Where the time of one run goes – use Trace Waterfall
- A single decision the agent can't take alone – use Decision Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentLedger, type LedgerEntry } from "@/components/ui/agent-ledger";

const entries: LedgerEntry[] = [
  { id: "price", action: "Changed price", target: "Pro plan", system: "Stripe", at: Date.now() - 120000,
    change: ["$29 / month", "$34 / month"] },
  { id: "deals", action: "Updated 212 deals", target: "Renewals in Q4", system: "HubSpot", at: Date.now() - 60000,
    change: ["$29 per seat", "$34 per seat"], dependsOn: ["price"] },
  { id: "email", action: "Sent email", target: "3,812 customers", system: "HubSpot", at: Date.now(),
    detail: "New price and the code LAUNCH20", dependsOn: ["price"], reversible: false },
];

export function Changes() {
  return <AgentLedger entries={entries} agent="Launch agent" onUndo={(ids) => revert(ids)} onRedo={(ids) => reapply(ids)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entries | `LedgerEntry[]` |  | { id, action, target?, system, icon?, at, change?, detail?, reversible?, dependsOn? } – every change, any order; newest shows first |
| change | `[before, after]` |  | Per entry – shown as before (struck) → after; or pass detail for a single line |
| dependsOn | `string[]` |  | Per entry – the changes it builds on; undoing one of those undoes this one too, if it can be |
| reversible | `boolean` | `true` | Per entry – false for things that can't be taken back (a sent email, a payout): no Undo, and "Can't undo" when something it builds on is undone |
| agent | `string` |  | Who made the changes, next to the title |
| now | `number` |  | The clock for "2m ago" (epoch ms) – defaults to now, kept fresh |
| undone / defaultUndone | `string[]` |  | Ids of undone changes, controlled or not |
| onUndo / onRedo | `(ids: string[]) => void` |  | The change and its reversible dependents – revert or reapply them |
| pointAt | `string \| null` |  | Lights up a change and what builds on it, as if its Undo were pointed at – for a walkthrough |
| title | `string` | `"Ledger"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the Undo and Redo buttons; focusing Undo shows what goes with it
- Enter / Space: Undoes or redoes the focused change

### Accessibility

- The ledger is an ordered list labelled with its title, newest first
- Undo is labelled with the change and how many changes build on it; Redo with the change
- Before → after is plain text; the arrow is read as "to"

### Motion

- New changes open their row at the top – the panel grows smoothly – and then fade in
- Pointing at Undo lights up the change and everything built on it – "Also undone" in blue, "Can't undo" in amber
- Undo draws a line across each row, down the chain a beat after each other; the rows go quiet and their logos gray
- Rows never change height – the time, Undo, Redo and the flags all share one slot
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: under 480px the numbers move to a line of their own, the time drops the system's name and Undo / Redo shrink to round icon buttons
- On touch screens Undo and Redo show on every row, in place of the time
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every change every time – ids keep rows in place, new ids slide in
- at is epoch ms; pass now to drive "2m ago" yourself
- Undo calls onUndo with the ids to revert – actually reverting them in Stripe, GitHub etc. is up to you
- Mark irreversible changes with reversible: false – honesty about what can't be undone is the point
- Colors are variables on .ui-al, e.g. --ui-al-also-bg / --ui-al-kept-bg
- The undo, redo and lock icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: approval-card, review-center, trace-waterfall, decision-tree

---

## Agent Monitor (Pro)

One agent at work, as a card – its current step with a clock and the bill so far, a time strip and the finished steps with the logo of each tool, a click on any of them for the details; the exact command when it needs your OK; folds into a small bar with the tools it has used

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-monitor
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-monitor.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-monitor`

### When to use

- A dashboard tile or side panel that keeps one agent in view while people do other work – its current step, the clock and the bill so far
- Agents that must ask before they touch something real – a deploy, a release, a refund: the card shows the exact command and takes Allow or Decline from the keyboard
- Runs where it matters which tool the time went to – the time strip and the logos answer that without opening a log

### When not to use

- You need every tool call with its input and output – use Trace Waterfall
- More than one agent works at once – use Agent Lanes or Agent Tree
- Only a single "thinking…" line is needed – a shimmering label is enough

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentMonitor } from "@/components/ui/agent-monitor";

<AgentMonitor
  state={run.state}                  // "idle" | "running" | "waiting" | "paused" | "finished" | "failed" | "cancelled"
  agent={{ name: "Claude Opus 5.5", role: "Release agent", mark: <ClaudeLogo /> }}
  since={run.since}
  pausedFor={run.pausedFor}
  cost={run.cost}
  steps={[
    { id: "issues", label: "Collected 14 issues", icon: <LinearLogo />, state: "done", took: 1700 },
    { id: "notes", label: "Drafting the release notes", icon: <NotionLogo />, state: "running", since: run.stepSince },
    { id: "build", label: "Build the preview", kind: "run", state: "queued" },
  ]}
  ask={{ title: "Ready to ship", command: "gh release create v3.2.0 --latest", icon: <GitHubLogo /> }}
  outcome={{ note: "v3.2.0 is live · 14 changes" }}
  onPause={() => runs.pause(run.id)}
  onResume={() => runs.resume(run.id)}
  onCancel={() => runs.cancel(run.id)}
  onAllow={() => runs.allow(run.id)}
  onDecline={() => runs.decline(run.id)}
  onRetry={() => runs.retry(run.id)}
  onOpenLog={() => openLog(run.id)}
/>
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| state | `"idle" \| "running" \| "waiting" \| "paused" \| "finished" \| "failed" \| "cancelled"` | `"idle"` | Where the run is – a small pill next to the cost: blue Running, amber Needs you, green Finished, red Failed |
| agent | `{ name: string; role?: string; mark?: ReactNode }` | `{ name: "Agent" }` | Who's working: a name, a role or model, and a 16px logo – without one, the name's first letter |
| steps | `AgentRunStep[]` |  | Every step, oldest first: { id, label, kind?, icon?, state: "queued" | "running" | "done" | "failed", since?, took? } – the running one fills the well, finished ones become bars and rows (three rows tall, the rest scroll), queued ones count toward "3/6" |
| icon (step) | `ReactNode` |  | The logo of the tool the step used – GitHub, Linear, Slack, Notion… – shown in its row and in the well |
| tool / detail / output (step) | `string` |  | Fill the step's info card: the tool's name, a sentence on what happened, and the command it ran or the place it touched – a click on the row or its bar opens it |
| kind (step) | `"read" \| "search" \| "edit" \| "run" \| "think" \| "web"` |  | A plain icon for steps without a logo |
| current | `{ label: string; kind?; icon? }` |  | Overrides what the well says while running – by default it's the running step |
| since / until | `number` |  | When the run began and ended (ms) – the clock counts between them |
| pausedFor | `number` | `0` | Time spent paused (ms), left out of the clock so it picks up where it stopped |
| cost | `number` |  | USD spent so far – shimmers while the agent is busy |
| ask | `{ title: string; command?: string; icon?: ReactNode }` |  | While waiting: a short title, the exact command as code, and the logo of the tool it's about to use |
| outcome | `{ added?; removed?; files?; note? }` |  | Once finished: lines added and removed, files touched, or a short note – after "Finished in 19s" |
| error | `string` |  | Once failed: what went wrong, in a few words |
| onAllow / onDecline | `() => void` |  | Allow and Decline while waiting – Enter and Escape do the same while the card has the focus |
| onPause / onResume / onCancel | `() => void` |  | Steer a running or paused run – Pause or Resume and Cancel sit side by side as two small buttons; paused, the clock and the running bar stand still |
| onRetry | `() => void` |  | Try again after a failure |
| onOpenLog | `() => void` |  | Shows Log, to jump to the full trace |
| defaultFolded | `boolean` | `false` | Start folded, as the small bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Fold away, the step list when it scrolls, then the controls at the foot
- ↑ / ↓: On the focused step list: scroll through the finished steps
- Enter: Waiting, with the card focused: Allow
- Escape: Waiting, with the card focused: Decline – with an info card open, it closes the info card and puts the focus back on its row
- Enter / Space: On a step row: open or close its info card, the focus moving to its close button – on the folded bar: open the card, the focus landing on Fold away

### Accessibility

- The card is a labelled region naming the agent, its state and its current step; the folded bar is a button with the same name
- The time strip is one image whose label lists each step with its time; the rows are a list, and the logos are decoration
- Cost and time are labelled in words for screen readers
- Each row is a button with aria-expanded; the info card is a labelled dialog, and a press outside it closes it

### Motion

- A new step rolls into the well from below; the state pill rolls the same way
- A finished step drops into the top of the list and pushes the others down; past three rows the list scrolls, with a soft fade at the edge that has more
- Folded, each tool the agent picks up slides into the stack of logos – the one in use in full color, the earlier ones faded back; point at one and it lifts, with a small label above naming its last step and how long it took
- The running bar grows live with a soft sheen; when waiting, a short amber bar breathes at the end; finished, the strip turns green
- A click on a row or a bar opens the step's info card under it, with a small drop-in; the pair stays lit while it's open
- Point at a bar or a row and its partner lights up while the rest fade back – a bar whose row has scrolled away scrolls it back into view
- Every change of state is a soft swap: the old content fades and shrinks away while the new one fades in, and the room between them eases to the new width – the folded bar's clock and its Needs you, ✓ and Failed tags, and the controls on the tray alike
- Folded, the running clock carries the same soft shimmer as the cost
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- 372px wide (a white card on a gray tray, the controls on the tray), or narrower with its container – long steps and commands end in an ellipsis
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component only draws – update state, steps, since, pausedFor and cost from your agent's events
- Fill tool, detail and output on each step – a click on it should answer what it did, with what, and how long it took
- Give each step the logo of the tool it calls; steps that only think or edit can go without and get a plain icon
- Rename the running step once it's done ("Drafting the notes" → "Drafted the notes") so rows read as a record

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: trace-waterfall, agent-lanes, permission-request, tool-call-card

## Agent Plan (Pro)

An agent's step-by-step plan to review before it runs – rename, drag to reorder, remove or add steps, then watch each one run with live timers and retry from a failed step

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-plan
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-plan.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-plan`

### When to use

- An agent is about to do several things in a row and people should agree to the plan first
- Long or expensive runs (tool calls, emails, writes) where a wrong order or an extra step costs real time
- Showing the same plan as it executes – which step is running, how long each took, where it failed

### When not to use

- A single action that needs a yes or no – use Approval Card
- Model reasoning without editable steps – use Thinking State
- A user's own onboarding checklist – use Progress Tracker

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { AgentPlan, type PlanStep } from "@/components/ui/agent-plan";

export function PlanReview({ plan }: { plan: PlanStep[] }) {
  const [steps, setSteps] = useState(plan);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"draft" | "running" | "done">("draft");

  return (
    <AgentPlan
      title="Prepare the Q3 board update"
      estimate="~2 min"
      steps={steps}
      status={status}
      onChange={setSteps}
      onRun={(final) => {
        setStatus("running");
        agent.run(final); // stream step updates back into setSteps
      }}
      onCancel={() => agent.discard()}
      onRetry={(id) => agent.retryFrom(id)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `PlanStep[]` |  | Controlled steps: { id, title, detail?, tool?, status?, duration?, error? }. Pair with onChange |
| defaultSteps | `PlanStep[]` | `[]` | Initial steps when uncontrolled – edits are kept inside the component |
| status | `"draft" \| "running" \| "done"` | `"draft"` | Review and edit, executing, or finished. Editing is only possible in draft |
| onChange | `(steps: PlanStep[]) => void` |  | Every edit during review: rename, remove, reorder, add |
| onRun | `(steps: PlanStep[]) => void` |  | "Run plan" pressed – gets the steps in their final order. Set status to "running" here. Also shows "Run again" on the tray once done |
| onCancel | `() => void` |  | Shows a Cancel button next to Run plan |
| onRetry | `(stepId: string) => void` |  | Shows "Retry from here" under failed steps |
| title | `string` |  | The goal of the plan, shown as the heading and used as the list's label |
| estimate | `string` |  | Estimated run time shown in review, e.g. "~2 min" |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between steps, their remove buttons, the Add step field and the actions
- ↑ / ↓: Moves focus to the previous or next step
- Alt / ↑ / ↓: Moves the focused step up or down
- Enter: Renames the focused step; Enter again saves. In Add step: adds the step at the end and keeps the field ready for the next one
- Esc: Cancels a rename
- Delete: Removes the focused step

### Accessibility

- The steps are an ordered list labelled with the plan's title; each step is focusable in review and describes its shortcuts
- Moves, renames, removals and additions are announced in a polite live region ("Moved 'Draft the board memo' to position 3 of 5")
- While running, each step carries its status as text, the active one has aria-current="step", and finished or failed steps are announced
- The drag grip is pointer-only; Alt+arrow keys do the same from the keyboard
- Icon buttons are labelled, focus rings show on keyboard focus only, and the folded-away Add step is inert while running

### Motion

- Reordering is live: the dragged step follows the pointer, the others slide aside, and everything settles with a FLIP glide – also for keyboard moves and order changes from props
- Removed steps collapse and the list closes the gap; added steps fade up into place
- Numbers in a hairline ring turn into a ray spinner, then into a check on a light gray fill that draws itself; the progress line fills segment by segment
- Add step folds away when the plan starts, and the tray below the card swaps its actions for the run's status – "Running · 2 of 5" with the elapsed time, then "Done in 14s"
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and the spinner stands still

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 460px; titles and details wrap, tool chips stay on one line
- Below 400px the footer hint drops away, below 340px gutters tighten – works down to 320px
- On touch screens the grip and remove button are always visible
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every step a stable id – reorder animations, timers and announcements follow the id, not the index
- Leave duration out to have it measured from when a step turned active; pass it when your agent reports its own timing
- On retry, reset the failed step and everything after it to "pending" and keep status "running"
- Run the steps onRun hands you, not the original proposal – the user may have renamed, removed or reordered them

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: progress-tracker, tool-call-card, approval-card, thinking-state

## Agent Queue (Pro)

The work waiting for your agents, and how fast it moves – jobs drop into a live queue, glide into free worker slots as growing bars and land in Done or Failed, while a depth chart shows the backlog build up when a rate limit pauses the workers and drain when they resume

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-queue
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-queue.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-queue`

### When to use

- A job queue in an agent product – how many tasks wait, which worker runs what, and how fast the backlog moves
- Watching backpressure live: a provider rate-limits, the workers pause, the queue builds up and drains again
- An ops view next to your agents where people can pause the queue, add or remove workers, or move a job to the front

### When not to use

- Several agents side by side over time – use Agent Lanes
- Handing work to a specific agent by hand – use Delegate Board
- A list of background tasks with their results – use Agent Inbox
- Where the time and money of one run go – use Trace Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentQueue, type QueueJob, type QueueWorker } from "@/components/ui/agent-queue";

const workers: QueueWorker[] = [
  { id: "w1", name: "Sonnet 5.5" },
  { id: "w2", name: "GPT-6 Sol" },
];

const jobs: QueueJob[] = [
  { id: "j1", name: "Summarize ticket #4821", kind: "llm", status: "running", worker: "w1",
    enqueuedAt: t0, startedAt: t0 + 1200, progress: 0.4 },
  { id: "j2", name: "Embed 240 docs", kind: "tool", status: "queued", enqueuedAt: t0 + 800 },
  { id: "j3", name: "Draft reply – Acme", kind: "llm", status: "queued", priority: "high", enqueuedAt: t0 + 2100 },
];

export function Jobs() {
  // Times are on one clock (epoch ms here) – without now, the component ticks Date.now while there is work
  return <AgentQueue jobs={jobs} workers={workers} backpressure={20} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| jobs | `QueueJob[]` |  | { id, name, kind, status, enqueuedAt, priority?, startedAt?, endedAt?, worker?, progress?, estimate?, attempt?, maxAttempts?, detail?, icon?, error? } – waiting, running and recently finished jobs |
| kind | `"llm" \| "tool" \| "agent" \| "human"` |  | Per job – picks its tint: LLM calls violet, tool calls teal, sub-agents slate, human review blue |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per job – a job that goes from running back to queued with a higher attempt shows as a retry |
| priority | `"high" \| "normal" \| "low"` | `"normal"` | Per job – a high one glides past the others to the front |
| progress / estimate | `number` |  | Per job – 0–1 while it runs, or the expected run time in ms to estimate it |
| workers | `QueueWorker[]` |  | { id, name, detail?, icon? } – the slots; their number is the concurrency |
| now | `number` |  | The clock, on the same scale as the job times – without it, the component keeps its own (Date.now) |
| rateLimits | `{ from, until, label? }[]` |  | Stretches when the provider rate-limits – while one is active the running jobs pause in amber with a countdown |
| paused / onPausedChange | `boolean / (paused) => void` |  | The queue is paused; the handler shows a Pause/Resume button |
| onConcurrencyChange | `(workers: number) => void` |  | Shows a – N + stepper for the number of workers |
| minConcurrency / maxConcurrency | `number` | `1 / 8` | The stepper's range |
| backpressure | `number` |  | A depth that means trouble – a dashed line on the chart; above it Waiting turns amber |
| window | `number` | `120000` | How far back the depth chart looks, in ms |
| totals | `{ done?, failed? }` |  | Counts since the start, when jobs only holds the recent ones |
| openId / defaultOpenId | `string \| null` | `null` | The job whose card is pinned, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(id: string \| null, job?: QueueJob) => void` |  | A job's card was pinned or closed |
| onPromote / onCancel | `(job: QueueJob) => void` |  | Show "Move to front" and "Cancel" in a pinned card |
| title / name | `string` | `"Queue"` | Heading, and the queue's name muted next to it |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves into the jobs (one job is in the tab order), then to the card's buttons
- ArrowUp / ArrowDown / ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: Walks through the running jobs, slot by slot, then the queue from the front; Home and End jump to the ends
- Enter / Space: Pins or closes the focused job's card
- Esc: Closes the card

### Accessibility

- Every job is a real button, labelled with its name, kind, how long it waited or ran, its place in line, priority and attempt
- Roving focus – only one job is in the tab order, so the flow is a single stop
- The pinned card is a dialog with a close button; Esc closes it and returns focus to the job
- Rate limits, their end, failures, retries and crossing the backpressure line are announced in a polite live region
- The chart is an image with a text summary: how many wait now, the peak, the average and the rate-limited stretches
- Pause is a toggle button with aria-pressed; the stepper's buttons say what they do and the count is announced

### Motion

- New jobs drop in at the back of the queue; a high-priority job lands at the back first, then glides past the others
- The front job moves into a free worker and becomes a bar that grows with its progress, with a sheen and a glowing front edge
- A finished job turns green for a beat and flies into Done; a failed one shakes red and goes to Failed – or slides back into the queue with a retry badge
- During a rate limit the bars stop and turn amber, a countdown runs out; the chart line climbs, then falls as the queue drains
- The numbers ease to their new value and the chart's scale glides when it changes – one frame loop that sleeps when nothing moves or the queue is off-screen
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears in place

### Responsive

- Built on a container query and the measured width: wide, the flow runs left to right – queue, workers, Done and Failed
- Under 600px the flow stacks: queue on top, the workers below (just their marks, the rail gets the room), Done and Failed side by side
- The four numbers wrap to two columns; under 440px Pause and the stepper get a row of their own
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole list every time something changes – ids keep jobs in place and every change glides
- All times are on one clock – epoch ms, or your own (then pass now)
- A retry is the same id going back to "queued" with attempt + 1, a new enqueuedAt and no startedAt or worker
- The chart is computed from the jobs: keep finished jobs for as long as window, or pass totals and accept a shorter history
- Pass progress while a job runs for honest bars; otherwise give an estimate
- Colors are variables on .ui-agq, e.g. --ui-agq-llm-bg / --ui-agq-llm-edge for LLM calls
- The icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-lanes, delegate-board, agent-inbox, trace-waterfall

## Agent Recap (Pro)

What the agents did while you were away – the night as a small chart with a peak per event, then a board of what needs you, what failed and what's done, acted on right on the card

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-recap
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-recap.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-recap`

### When to use

- The first thing people see when they come back to agents that kept working – in the morning, after a meeting, after a weekend
- A catch-up where the few things that need a decision come first and can be decided right there
- Showing that the agents were busy without making people read every step

### When not to use

- A live feed of what agents are doing right now – use Agent Monitor or Agent Lanes
- A full log with undo for every change – use Agent Ledger
- Decisions without the rest of the night – use Decision Inbox

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentRecap, type RecapEvent } from "@/components/ui/agent-recap";

const events: RecapEvent[] = [
  { id: "refund", kind: "needs", at: "2026-10-30T02:14", title: "Refund $240 to Acme Corp",
    detail: "Over the $200 auto-approve limit", action: "Approve", doneLabel: "Approved" },
  { id: "sync", kind: "failed", at: "2026-10-30T03:02", title: "Contact sync to the CRM",
    detail: "Token expired after 1,284 of 3,900 contacts" },
  { id: "tickets", kind: "done", at: "2026-10-29T19:05", title: "Answered support tickets", count: 38 },
];

export function Morning() {
  return <AgentRecap events={events} since={lastSeenAt} onAction={(e, a) => handle(e, a)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| events | `RecapEvent[]` |  | { id, at, kind, title, detail?, logo?, count?, action?, doneLabel? } – everything that happened, any order |
| kind | `"needs" \| "failed" \| "done"` |  | Per event – needs you (with its action), failed (with Retry) or done |
| since / until | `Date \| string \| number` |  | When the person left, and now – the chart runs between them; until defaults to the time it renders |
| onAction | `(event, action: "primary" \| "review") => void \| Promise` |  | The main action (Approve, Retry …) or Review. Return a promise and the row shows it working until it settles – a rejected one puts the row back |
| onUndo / onRedo | `(event) => void` |  | Undo on a card that was acted on or on something an agent did (a done card), and Redo after that |
| limit | `number` | `3` | Cards per lane at most – every lane keeps room for this many, so the three stay the same height however full they are |
| replay | `number` | `1800` | How long the night replays when it opens, in ms – 0 shows everything at once |
| title | `string` | `"While you were away"` | Heading |
| locale | `string` |  | For the times and counts |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the actions card by card – Review, then the main action (or Undo / Redo)
- Enter / Space: Runs the focused action; focus then moves to Undo, and back to the action after Undo

### Accessibility

- A section named by its heading; each lane has a heading with its count – of everything in it, also beyond the limit
- Every button says what it does to which task – "Approve: Refund $240 to Acme Corp" – so a screen reader never hears three bare Approves
- When an action finishes, a polite live region says so – "Approved: Refund $240 to Acme Corp" – and focus moves to Undo, so it never drops to the page
- Focusing anything in a card lights up its dot on the chart, the same as pointing at it; the chart itself is decorative and hidden from screen readers – everything on it is in the cards
- Every time is a <time> with the full date; empty lanes say so in words

### Motion

- The night is a small line chart with a peak per event and an area fading out below; when it opens, the line draws itself from left to right, each dot pops onto its peak as it's passed, its card fades in and the counts count along
- Pointing at the chart draws a line through its whole height; close to an event it snaps there, the dot grows, its card lights up and a tip says what it was – pointing at a card lights up its dot
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything shows at once

### Responsive

- Every card is the same height and ends in the same line – a state tag (Done, Fixed, Approved) and the buttons – so acting on one never moves anything
- Under 640px the three lanes stack
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every event a unique id – Undo, focus and the chart keep track of cards by it
- Events without a readable time are left out; ones before since or after until sit at the chart's edges
- A lane shows up to limit cards – keep the rest for a full view and link to it from your page
- since is when the person was last active – store it when they leave or go idle
- Merge many small done events into one card with a count (38 tickets) instead of 38 cards – the count also makes its peak taller
- Give needs cards a doneLabel in the past tense of their action – Approve → Approved, Send → Sent
- Colors are variables on .ui-ar, e.g. --ui-ar-needs or --ui-ar-failed

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: decision-inbox, agent-inbox, agent-ledger, notification-stack
