## Decision Tree (Pro)

An agent stuck on a decision lays out its options as a tree – the consequences of each branch, the risky ones marked, its own pick highlighted – and you choose a path or write your own

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/decision-tree
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/decision-tree.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/decision-tree`

### When to use

- An agent hits a fork it shouldn't take alone – it asks how to proceed and shows what each way would change
- Backend calls without much to look at: data cleanups, refunds, rollouts, escalations – the consequences are the content
- When the agent has a preference but a person decides – its pick is marked, the other ways stay one click away

### When not to use

- Reviewing finished work – a diff, an email, a refund – one item after another: use Review Center
- One action that only needs a yes or no, with a countdown – use Approval Card
- A few quick questions with two answers each – use Decision Inbox
- An agent asking for access to a tool or scope – use Permission Request

### Usage

```tsx
import { DecisionTree, type Decision } from "@/components/ui/decision-tree";

const decisions: Decision[] = [
  {
    id: "dupes",
    question: "3 customers have two active subscriptions – how should I proceed?",
    context: "All three signed up twice during the checkout outage.",
    agent: "Billing agent", model: "Sonnet 5.5", risk: "high",
    options: [
      { label: "Cancel the newer ones", pick: true, effects: ["Cancels 3 subscriptions · reversible", "Sends 3 emails"] },
      // A flagged part: marked in the leaf, its note shows on hover or with F
      { label: "Refund the newer ones", effects: [["Refunds ", { text: "$147 · not reversible", note: "One charge is two cycles old." }]] },
      { label: "Ask the customers", effects: ["Sends 3 emails · waits for answers"] },
    ],
  },
];

export function Decisions() {
  return (
    <DecisionTree
      decisions={decisions}
      onChoose={async (decision, choice) => {
        if ("other" in choice) return await agent.instruct(decision.id, choice.other); // its answer shows under your branch
        await agent.resume(decision.id, choice.option.label);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| decisions | `Decision[]` |  | { id, question, context?, agent, model?, icon?, risk?, options } – everything waiting for a call; decided ones leave, new ids join at the end |
| options | `DecisionOption[]` |  | Per decision, two to four – { label, effects?, pick? }; effects are what the branch leads to, one line each; pick marks the agent's own preference |
| effects | `DecisionText[]` |  | Per option – a string, or an array of strings and { text, note, source? } flags; flags are marked and explain themselves on hover, focus or F |
| risk | `"high" \| "medium" \| "low"` |  | Per decision – high and medium show as a small tag next to the agent |
| onChoose | `(decision, choice) => string \| void \| Promise<string \| void>` |  | A branch was picked ({ index, option }) or an instruction written ({ other }) – for an instruction, return the agent's short answer |
| allowOther | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the "Other…" branch for your own instruction |
| ref | `Ref<DecisionTreeHandle>` |  | hover, choose, setOther, send, next, previous, peek |
| title | `string` | `"Decisions"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: Picks a branch; the number after the last option opens "Other…"
- Enter: In "Other…": sends your instruction – Shift+Enter starts a new line
- ArrowRight / ArrowLeft: Next and previous decision (J and K too)
- F: Shows the agent's note on the next flagged consequence
- Esc: Closes "Other…" or a note

### Accessibility

- Every branch is a real button labelled with its option and, where it applies, "the agent's pick"; shortcuts are set with aria-keyshortcuts
- Flagged consequences are focusable and point to their note with aria-describedby (role tooltip)
- The "Other…" field is a labelled textarea; it has no focus ring of its own – its outline darkens instead, so focus stays visible
- Picks, instructions and the agent's answers are announced in a polite live region
- The lines are decoration and hidden from assistive tech

### Motion

- A new decision grows in: the question first, then its branches and their consequences, each line drawing itself out a beat after the other
- Pointing at a branch lights its path and lets the others step back
- A pick fades the other branches away; the chosen path draws on to its outcome – "Approved · running" or the agent's answer – then the tree fades and the next one grows
- "Other…" opens as a two-line field and glides taller as you write, up to three lines; its line stays put while it grows
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: wide, the tree runs left to right – question, branches, consequences
- Under 640px it runs top to bottom – the branches hang off a rail under the question, each with its consequences below it; nothing scrolls sideways
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Ask a real question in one sentence and give two to four options – the label says what to do, the effects say what changes
- Write effects as plain consequences with numbers ("Refunds $147 · not reversible"); flag only the part that worries the agent, with a one-line note and, if you have it, a source
- Mark at most one option as pick – the agent's honest preference
- For "Other…", treat the text as a new instruction for the agent and return its short answer from onChoose
- Colors are variables on .ui-dct, e.g. --ui-dct-link / --ui-dct-link-pick for the lines
- The icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: review-center, approval-card, decision-inbox, agent-tree

---

## Delegate Board (Pro)

Hand work to your agents by dragging it onto them – each agent previews its new “busy until” time, or switch to Auto and every new task goes to whoever is free first

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/delegate-board
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/delegate-board.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/delegate-board`

### When to use

- People hand tasks to a team of agents and want to see who is free and how long each one is busy
- Re-balancing work between agents: move a queued task to someone with more room
- Showing an automatic routing suggestion before it happens (suggestion prop)
- Weighing time against money: a fast, pricey model or a slower, cheaper one (rate on each agent)

### When not to use

- Watching what agents are doing right now over time – use Agent Lanes
- Approving single results – use Approval Card or Agent Inbox
- Assigning people in a project tool – this one is about agents, their models and queues

### Usage

```tsx
import { DelegateBoard, type DelegateAgent, type DelegateTask } from "@/components/ui/delegate-board";

export function Dispatch({ agents, tasks }: { agents: DelegateAgent[]; tasks: DelegateTask[] }) {
  return (
    <DelegateBoard
      agents={agents} // { id, name, model?, avatar?, current? }
      tasks={tasks} // { id, title, estimate, tools?, agentId? } – no agentId: unassigned
      onAssign={(taskId, agentId) => api.assign(taskId, agentId)} // agentId null: back to unassigned
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `DelegateAgent[]` |  | { id, name, model?, avatar?, current?, rate? } – current: minutes left on the task it runs now, for the Busy until time; rate: cost per minute of work, shown after the model, as the price of a hand-off and as the total in the queues |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.60"` | Formats every cost – swap in your currency or credits |
| tasks | `DelegateTask[]` |  | { id, title, estimate (minutes), tools?, agentId? }. In each queue the first task is the running one; past three, a +N chip lists the rest in a tooltip on hover or focus |
| onAssign | `(taskId: string, agentId: string \| null) => void` |  | A drop, a keyboard pick or Auto. null means back to Unassigned. Without it the board moves tasks itself |
| mode / defaultMode | `"auto" \| "manual"` | `"manual"` | Auto hands every unassigned task to the least busy agent, about one a second; Manual waits for a drag. The Auto switch sits in the bar |
| onModeChange | `(mode: DelegateMode) => void` |  | The Auto switch was turned on or off |
| suggestion | `{ taskId, agentId } \| null` |  | A proposed hand-off: the agent lights up and previews its new time, the task is marked |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for the Busy until times |
| title | `string` | `"Delegate"` | Heading in the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Picks up the focused task; Enter again hands it to the highlighted agent
- ↑ / ↓: Chooses the agent while a task is picked up
- 1–9: Hands the focused task to that agent at once (the numbers show next to the names)
- Esc: Puts a picked-up task back

### Accessibility

- Unassigned and Agents are labelled sections; every queue is a list named after its agent
- Tasks are buttons described by how to move them; every hand-off is announced politely ("Write release notes → Writer")
- Dragging is never the only way: keyboard pick-up, number keys and Auto do the same; Auto is a switch (role switch) labelled by its word

### Motion

- The dragged card lifts, tilts a little and follows the pointer; the agent under it lights up with its new time
- On drop the card glides and shrinks into the agent's queue; queued chips glide when they move between agents
- In Auto the next task goes out about every second, so each hand-off can be followed
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything moves at once, without glides

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 720px; below 560px the pile sits above the agents
- Works with touch: cards and chips can be dragged with a finger
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- estimate is in minutes; Busy until adds the agent's current (or its first task's estimate) and every queued task's estimate to now
- To route automatically, set suggestion first so people see it, then call your own assign

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-lanes, agent-inbox, agent-steering, autonomy-dial

---

## Dropzone (Pro)

Drag files in and watch them upload – fanning documents, colored type badges, progress with time left, errors with retry

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/dropzone
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/dropzone.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/dropzone`

### When to use

- Uploading documents, images or media – attachments, imports, asset libraries, onboarding
- Several files at once, where people want to see what's done, what's still running and what failed

### When not to use

- A single avatar or logo – a simple picker with a preview is lighter
- Huge uploads that run in the background for minutes – show them in a separate transfer panel

### Usage

```tsx
import { Dropzone } from "@/components/ui/dropzone";

export function Attachments() {
  return (
    <Dropzone
      accept={[".pdf", ".png", ".jpg", ".xlsx"]}
      maxSize={25 * 1024 * 1024}
      onUpload={(file, onProgress) =>
        new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
          const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
          xhr.upload.onprogress = (e) => onProgress(e.loaded / e.total);
          xhr.onload = () => (xhr.status < 300 ? resolve() : reject(new Error("Upload failed")));
          xhr.onerror = () => reject(new Error("Upload failed – connection lost"));
          xhr.open("POST", "/api/upload");
          xhr.send(file);
        })
      }
      onChange={(items) => setAttachments(items.filter((i) => i.status === "done"))}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| accept | `string[]` |  | Allowed extensions, e.g. [".pdf", ".png"]; any file when left out. Other files get a row with an error |
| maxSize | `number` | `25 MB` | Largest file in bytes; bigger files get a "Too large" row |
| onUpload | `(file: File, onProgress: (p: number) => void) => Promise<void>` |  | Uploads one file and reports progress from 0 to 1; reject to mark it as failed (the message is shown, Retry calls it again). Simulated when left out |
| onChange | `(items: UploadItem[]) => void` |  | Every change of the list: { id, name, size, status, progress, error?, file? } |
| hint | `string` |  | Text under the title; defaults to the accepted types and the size limit |
| autoplay | `boolean` | `false` | Plays a sample drop of four files – for previews and landing pages |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Reaches the drop area, then Retry and Remove in every row
- ↵: On the drop area: opens the file picker (Space works too)

### Accessibility

- The drop area is a button that opens the file picker, described by the accepted types and size
- Every row has a progress bar with its value; Retry and Remove are named after the file
- Finished, failed and rejected files are announced in a polite live region

### Motion

- Dragging files over the area fans the three little documents out, the outline turns solid blue and the title counts the files
- Rows grow in one after another; the bar fills in one solid color, a small check pops in when a file is done
- A failed row gives a short shake and its bar turns red; removed rows fold away
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 520px; long file names are cut with an ellipsis
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: chat-composer, ai-answer, glass-folder

## Email Draft (Free)

Agent-written email for review – switch recipient and tone, edit inline, remove the attachment, send or discard with undo

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/email-draft
- Section: Components · Cards
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/email-draft.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/email-draft`

### When to use

- Human-in-the-loop flows where an agent drafts an email and someone approves it – renewals, reminders, follow-ups
- Inboxes or task lists of pending outreach, one card per record

### When not to use

- Writing long emails from scratch – use a full editor
- Messages that go out without review – then a simple activity row is enough

### Usage

```tsx
import { EmailDraft } from "@/components/ui/email-draft";

export function RenewalReview() {
  return (
    <EmailDraft
      reference="SUB-1182"
      account="Northwind Logistics"
      amount="$8,900"
      status="Renews in 5 days"
      agent="Renewal agent"
      contacts={[{ name: "Jonas Weber", email: "jonas@northwind.io" }]}
      attachment="Renewal-quote.pdf"
      link={{ label: "Review quote", href: "/quotes/1182" }}
      onSend={(email) => api.send(email)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reference | `string` | `"SUB-1182"` | Reference of the record the email is about |
| account | `string` | `"Northwind Logistics"` | Account or company under the reference |
| amount | `string` | `"$8,900"` | Amount on the right |
| status | `string` | `"Renews in 5 days"` | Status chip next to the reference |
| agent | `string` | `"Renewal agent"` | Who wrote the draft, shown in the footer |
| contacts | `DraftContact[]` |  | People the email can go to – the first is preselected |
| attachment | `string \| null` |  | File name of the attachment; it can be removed and added back |
| tones | `DraftTone[]` |  | Text variants { id, label, body(contact) } – Friendly, Short and Formal by default |
| link | `{ label, href }` |  | Link appended to the email text |
| onSend | `({ to, body, attachment }) => void` |  | Called after Send with the final email |
| onDiscard | `() => void` |  | Called when the draft is discarded |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ⌘ / Enter: Sends the email while editing
- Esc: Leaves editing, or closes the recipient menu

### Accessibility

- The recipient is a button that opens a listbox; tones are toggle buttons with aria-pressed
- The text is a plain paragraph; clicking it or the pencil swaps in a labelled text field
- Sent and discarded states are announced as a status with an Undo button

### Motion

- Switching tone fades the new text in; the recipient menu scales in from its corner
- Sending shows a spinner, then the card folds into a one-line receipt – the height glides between them
- With prefers-reduced-motion changes happen instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 520px; on narrow screens the email address and the shortcut hint hide
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Experiment Card (Pro)

An A/B test in two lines that quietly unfolds on hover – variants linked to a tiny chart, a metric switch with rolling numbers, and a winner you pick with a click

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/experiment-card
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/experiment-card.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/experiment-card`

### When to use

- A/B tests, prompt or model comparisons, pricing experiments – anything with a few variants measured the same way
- Lists of running experiments where the result should be one hover away
- When people should not only read the result but act on it: pick the winner and ship it

### When not to use

- More than about five variants – the head chart and the rows get crowded; use a table
- Results over time – a line chart shows when a variant pulled ahead; this card shows where things stand
- A single number without variants – use KPI Chart or Compact Breakdown

### Usage

```tsx
import { ExperimentCard } from "@/components/ui/experiment-card";

export function SignupCopyTest() {
  return (
    <ExperimentCard
      title="Signup button copy"
      status={{ label: "Running", tone: "green" }}
      note="Day 9 of 14"
      metrics={[
        { id: "conversion", label: "Conversion", format: (n) => `${n.toFixed(1)}%` },
        { id: "revenue", label: "Revenue", format: (n) => `$${n.toFixed(2)}` },
      ]}
      variants={[
        { id: "a", key: "A", name: "Start free trial", control: true, visitors: 4790, values: { conversion: 4.2, revenue: 18.4 } },
        { id: "b", key: "B", name: "Try it free", visitors: 4812, values: { conversion: 4.7, revenue: 19.1 }, confidence: { conversion: 96, revenue: 81 } },
      ]}
      action={{ label: (v) => `Ship ${v.key}`, onClick: (v) => ship(v.id) }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | Name of the experiment |
| variants | `ExperimentVariant[]` |  | { id, key, name, values, control?, visitors?, confidence?, color? } – values and confidence hold one number per metric id; key is the short letter in the badge |
| metrics | `ExperimentMetric[]` |  | { id, label, format?, lowerIsBetter? } – the switch above the rows; no switch with a single metric |
| metric | `string` |  | Controlled metric id |
| defaultMetric | `string` | `first metric` | Starting metric when uncontrolled |
| onMetricChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new metric |
| winner | `string \| null` |  | Controlled id of the picked variant |
| defaultWinner | `string \| null` | `null` | Picked variant when uncontrolled |
| onWinnerChange | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | Called when a variant is picked, or null when the pick is taken back |
| status | `{ label: string; tone?: ExperimentTone }` |  | The tag under the title – tone is red, amber, green, blue, violet or gray |
| note | `string` |  | Short text next to the status, e.g. "Day 9 of 14" |
| action | `{ label: string \| (variant) => string; onClick: (variant) => void }` |  | The button that appears on the tray once a winner is picked |
| hint | `ReactNode` | `"Pick a winner"` | The line on the tray while nothing is hovered or picked |
| trigger | `"hover" \| "click"` | `"hover"` | Hover opens under the mouse; taps and the keyboard always toggle |
| open | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Starts open when uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the card opens or closes |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the card: opens or closes it
- ← / →: In the metric switch: previous or next metric (wraps around)
- Tab: Through the metric switch, the variants and the action
- Space: On a variant: picks it as the winner, or takes the pick back
- Esc: Closes the card and returns focus to it

### Accessibility

- The head is one button with aria-expanded; its name carries the status and who is ahead
- The metric switch and the variants are radio groups; every variant's name includes its value and its change against the baseline
- The small chart in the head is decorative – everything it shows is in the rows
- While the card is closed, everything inside is inert; the line on the tray is announced politely

### Motion

- Nothing travels: the head stays where it is and the comparison unfolds below it while it fades in
- Switching the metric rolls every number in one shared tween while bars and columns glide to their new size; the pill of the switch slides along
- Hovering a variant widens its column in the head and fades the others – and the other way round
- Picking a winner turns its badge into a check and pops the action onto the tray
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 340px; below 300px the note next to the status goes and the chips tighten
- Touch screens: a tap opens, a tap outside closes, rows and the metric switch are taller
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Changes are measured against the control (the variant with control: true, else the first). With lowerIsBetter a drop is shown as it is (−7.5%) but colored green and counted as the lead
- Pass raw numbers and do the formatting in the metric's format, so the rolling values stay smooth
- The card does not compute confidence – pass what your stats engine gives you

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: project-card, compact-breakdown, kpi-chart

## Fallback Chain (Pro)

One request finding a model that answers, as a small flow diagram – the request branches out to each model in its fallback order, a light runs to the one being tried, failed branches break red, and the one that answers runs on to the response

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/fallback-chain
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/fallback-chain.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/fallback-chain`

### When to use

- A request can go to several models, providers or regions and people should see which one answered – and why the others didn't
- Model routers, LLM gateways, retries across providers, uptime and incident views

### When not to use

- When several models answer the same prompt at once and you compare them – use Parallel Attempts
- When the full timeline of one run matters – use Trace Waterfall

### Usage

```tsx
import { FallbackChain, type FallbackAttempt } from "@/components/ui/fallback-chain";

export function Route({ attempts }: { attempts: FallbackAttempt[] }) {
  return (
    <FallbackChain
      title="Summarize support ticket"
      route="openrouter/auto"
      attempts={attempts} // { id, model, provider?, providerLogo?, region?, logo?, status, startedAt?, duration?, timeout?, cost? (USD), reason?, note?, details? }
      request={{ name: "HubSpot · Ticket #4821", logo: <HubSpotLogo />, text: prompt }}
      response={{ name: "Slack · #support", logo: <SlackLogo />, text: answer }}
      onRetry={() => resend()}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attempts | `FallbackAttempt[]` |  | The models in the order they're tried, each with its status: waiting, trying, failed, answered or skipped |
| title | `string` | `"Request"` | What was asked, above the diagram next to the attempt and the running time and cost |
| route | `string` |  | The route on the request node, e.g. "openrouter/auto" |
| request | `ChainEnd` |  | Where the request came from – { name, logo, text, details } for its hover card: the source, a preview of the prompt and extra lines |
| response | `ChainEnd` |  | Where the answer goes – { name, logo, text, details } for its hover card; the preview shows once a model answered |
| now | `number` |  | A clock you control for the live timer – without it it follows real time |
| onRetry | `() => void` |  | Shows a Retry button once every model failed |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the request, each model and the response – each opens its hover card while focused; then the Retry button once every model failed

### Accessibility

- The summary on top is a status region – “Attempt 2 of 4”, “Answered in 8.5s” and failures are announced
- The branches are decoration – the models are an ordered list with each one's provider, status and time
- Hover cards are tooltips tied to their element (aria-describedby), so they're read on focus too
- Every state is written out (“Rate limited · 429”, “Not needed”), not only shown by color
- The running light and the drawing branches stop with reduced motion

### Responsive

- Below 680px the provider moves into the model's hover card; below 520px the diagram turns into a tree – the request on top, the models branching off one line, the result stays in the line above
- Dark mode built in; colors are CSS variables on .ui-fc

### Requirements

- React 19

---

## Fan-out Grid (Pro)

One agent hands a big job to many workers – every task a cell on a live grid that fills in as they get through it, with retries, failures, cost and the time left, and the details of any task on hover

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/fan-out-grid
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/fan-out-grid.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/fan-out-grid`

### When to use

- An agent fans one job out to many workers – enriching leads, translating pages, labelling tickets, running evals – and you want to watch it fill in
- Batch runs with hundreds of tasks, where retries and failures matter more than any single step
- A live overview next to a run's log: how far it is, what it costs, how long is left

### When not to use

- A handful of agents and who started whom – use Agent Tree
- Where the time of one run goes, step by step – use Trace Waterfall
- Several agents side by side over time – use Agent Lanes

### Usage

```tsx
import { FanoutGrid, type FanoutTask } from "@/components/ui/fan-out-grid";

const tasks: FanoutTask[] = leads.map((lead) => ({
  id: lead.id,
  label: lead.domain,
  status: lead.status, // "queued" | "running" | "retrying" | "done" | "failed"
  worker: lead.worker,
  start: lead.startedMs, end: lead.endedMs,
  cost: lead.cost, attempts: lead.attempts,
  result: lead.summary, error: lead.error,
}));

export function Enrichment({ elapsed }: { elapsed: number }) {
  return <FanoutGrid tasks={tasks} job="Enrich 240 leads" workers={16} now={elapsed} onRetry={(ids) => retry(ids)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `FanoutTask[]` |  | { id, label, status, worker?, start?, end?, cost?, attempts?, result?, error? } – one per task, in the order the cells should show |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "retrying" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per task – picks the cell's tint: gray, blue with a shine, amber, green, red |
| start / end | `number` |  | Per task, in ms from the start of the job – used for its duration and the time left |
| attempts | `number` |  | Per task – 2 and more show in its details |
| job | `string` |  | What the whole job does, next to the title – e.g. "Enrich 240 leads" |
| workers | `number` |  | How many workers run at once – the time left is worked out from it (defaults to the tasks running now) |
| now | `number` | `0` | The clock, in ms from the start of the job |
| onRetry | `(ids: string[]) => void` |  | Shows "Retry failed" while tasks have failed, and gets their ids |
| onSelect | `(task \| null) => void` |  | A task was picked (click or Enter) – null when it's let go |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Fan-out"` | Heading of the bar |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | A small mark before the title, e.g. the agent's logo |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves into the grid (one stop) and on to the counts on the tray and Retry
- ArrowLeft / ArrowRight / ArrowUp / ArrowDown: Walks the cells and shows each one's details; Home and End jump to the first and the last
- Enter / Space: Keeps the details open, or lets them go
- Esc: Lets go of the details

### Accessibility

- The grid is a single tab stop; the details of the cell you're on are its description
- The counts on the tray under the card are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) that show only one state
- The run's progress is announced politely in steps of ten percent, and once more when it's finished

### Motion

- Cells appear in a quick wave; running ones carry a shine that sweeps across, each a little out of step
- Retrying cells breathe in amber; done and failed cells pop once when they land
- The details window opens with a soft scale and fade from its cell
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: the grid fills whatever width it gets, the cells wrap into rows
- Under 520px the cells get smaller and the numbers move to a line of their own
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every task every time something changes – ids keep cells in place, and a cell animates when its status changes
- start and end are ms from the job's start, not timestamps
- The time left needs at least three finished tasks; pass workers for an honest estimate
- A retried task keeps its id – raise attempts and set status back to running
- Colors are variables on .ui-fog, e.g. --ui-fog-done-bg / --ui-fog-done-edge
- The retry icon is Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-tree, trace-waterfall, agent-lanes, agent-queue

## Filter Menu (Free)

Grouped filters with removable chips, collapsible checkbox groups, Clear all and full keyboard control

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/filter-menu
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/filter-menu.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/filter-menu`

### When to use

- Filtering a list, table or board by a few groups of options – stage, owner, region and the like
- Side panels or popovers where people pick several filters and want to see them all at a glance

### When not to use

- A single choice from a short list – use a select or segmented control
- Free-text search or numeric ranges with a slider – this menu works with predefined options

### Usage

```tsx
import { FilterMenu } from "@/components/ui/filter-menu";

const groups = [
  { id: "stage", label: "Stage", options: [{ id: "new", label: "New lead" }, { id: "won", label: "Won" }] },
  { id: "size", label: "Deal size", chipPrefix: "Deal: ", options: [{ id: "s", label: "Under $5k" }, { id: "l", label: "Over $50k" }] },
];

export function DealFilters() {
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState({});
  return <FilterMenu groups={groups} value={filters} onChange={setFilters} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| groups | `FilterGroup[]` |  | Required. Each { id, label, options: { id, label }[], chipPrefix? } |
| value | `Record<string, string[]>` |  | Picked option ids per group – makes it controlled |
| defaultValue | `Record<string, string[]>` | `{}` | Starting filters when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(value) => void` |  | Called with the new filters after every change |
| defaultOpen | `string[]` | `the first group` | Groups that start open |
| title | `string` | `"Filters"` | Heading on top |
| hints | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the keyboard hints on the tray |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Moves through group headers and the options of open groups
- Enter / Space: Picks or unpicks an option, or opens and closes a group
- → / ←: Opens a group, or closes it and jumps back to its header
- Home / End: Jumps to the first or last row

### Accessibility

- Group headers are buttons with aria-expanded; options are role=checkbox with aria-checked
- One roving tab stop for the list, so Tab moves past it in one step
- Each chip has a remove button labelled with the filter; changes to the chips are announced politely

### Motion

- Groups open and close by animating their height; the chevron turns along
- Chips pop in, and their box glides to its new height when a row of chips appears or goes
- Checkmarks draw themselves in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 420px wide; chips wrap onto new lines
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Inline Diff (Pro)

AI edits to prose shown inline – struck and added words you accept or reject one by one, with keys, a popover and undo

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/inline-diff
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/inline-diff.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/inline-diff`

### When to use

- An AI rewrote a piece of prose – an email, a paragraph, a product description – and people should approve each edit
- "Make it shorter", "fix the tone", "fix grammar" actions where most edits are small and scattered through the text
- Review steps in an agent flow where the result should only change with an explicit yes

### When not to use

- Code or line-based text – use a line diff with gutters instead
- Full rewrites where almost every word changes – show the new version next to the old one
- Live typing suggestions inside an editor – this reviews a finished suggestion, it isn't a text field

### Usage

```tsx
import { InlineDiff } from "@/components/ui/inline-diff";

export function ReviewRewrite({ draft, rewrite }: { draft: string; rewrite: string }) {
  return (
    <InlineDiff
      label="Suggested by AI · Make it shorter"
      original={draft}
      suggested={rewrite}
      onChange={(text) => saveDraft(text)}
      onDone={(text) => setFinal(text)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| original | `string` | `""` | The text as it is now |
| suggested | `string` | `""` | The text the AI suggests – diffed word by word against original |
| changes | `DiffSegment[]` |  | Pre-computed segments ({ type: "equal", text } or { type: "change", remove, insert }) instead of original and suggested |
| onChange | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called on every decision and undo with the text so far – pending changes keep the original words |
| onDone | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called when the last pending change is decided, with the final text |
| label | `string` |  | Small line on the gray tray above the card, e.g. "Suggested by AI · Make it shorter" |
| ref | `Ref<InlineDiffHandle>` |  | highlight(index | null), accept(index), reject(index), acceptAll(), rejectAll(), undo(), reset() |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab / Shift+Tab: Move between pending changes
- ‹ / ›: Toolbar arrows: highlight the previous / next pending change (wrapping around) and open its popover
- Y / Enter: Accept the focused change and move to the next one
- N / Backspace: Reject the focused change and move to the next one
- Esc: Leave the change or clear the arrow highlight

### Accessibility

- Every pending change is a focusable button labelled like "Suggestion 2 of 4: replace “available” with “live”. Press Y to accept, N to reject"
- Removed words are a <del>, new words an <ins>; the side that was dropped is hidden from screen readers once decided
- Each decision, Accept all, Reject all and Undo are announced in a polite live region with the number left
- After the last decision focus moves to Undo, so the keyboard is never stranded; the hidden toolbar is inert
- Popover buttons are labelled and keep focus on the change; visible focus rings throughout
- The prev/next arrows never steal focus: a focused change hands focus to the next one, otherwise the change is highlighted while focus stays on the arrow
- Deleted words are red and struck, added words green – color is never the only cue (strike-through, <del> and <ins>)

### Motion

- Accepting shrinks the struck words to nothing while the green tint fades and the new words settle into the text
- Rejecting does the opposite – the new words shrink away, the strike-through and red tint fade
- The popover fades up above a change and glides from one change to the next
- The arrows only scroll the page when the next change is out of view (smoothly, or instantly with reduced motion)
- The toolbar cross-fades into "All changes reviewed" and the check draws itself
- With prefers-reduced-motion every change happens instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container; the paragraph wraps freely and changes wrap across lines with their tints
- The popover stays inside the card horizontally, down to 320px wide
- Below 400px the prev/next arrows step aside; on touch screens the popover buttons grow and drop the key hints
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the user's text as original and the model's rewrite as suggested – diffWords groups adjacent removals and insertions into one change
- Ask the model for a rewrite that keeps unchanged sentences verbatim; the fewer stray edits, the easier the review
- Write the result back with onDone (or onChange for drafts); undecided changes keep the original words
- diffWords is exported, so you can count edits or build the same segments on the server

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: writing-assistant, change-summary, approval-card

---

## Integration Picker (Pro)

Integrations page of a command menu – search, a list of services and the picked one with its connection on two tiles

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/integration-picker
- Section: Components · Navigation
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-picker.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-picker`

### When to use

- The integrations step of a command menu or settings dialog
- Letting people find a service quickly and switch it on without leaving what they're doing

### When not to use

- A full marketplace with categories and many details per app – use a page instead
- Two or three integrations – a simple list with switches is enough

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationPicker } from "@/components/ui/integration-picker";

export function Integrations() {
  return (
    <IntegrationPicker
      appName="affectUI"
      onToggle={(id, connected) => saveIntegration(id, connected)}
      onExplore={(id) => router.push(`/integrations/${id}`)}
      onBack={() => setPage("root")}
      onClose={closeMenu}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| integrations | `Integration[]` | `10 sample services` | Each { id, name, domain, category, description, features, path + color or icon, connected } |
| appName | `string` | `"affectUI"` | Your product's name in the title, e.g. “affectUI + Linear” |
| appIcon | `ReactNode` | `the affectUI mark` | Your product's mark on the black tile |
| defaultSelected | `string` | `the first item` | Id of the integration that is picked first |
| onToggle | `(id: string, connected: boolean) => void` |  | Called when an integration is switched on or off |
| onExplore | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called by “Explore integration” |
| onBack | `() => void` |  | Shows the back button and runs on ← in an empty search |
| onClose | `() => void` |  | Runs on Esc in an empty search |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Move through the list
- ↵: Switch the picked integration on or off
- Esc: Clear the search, then close
- ←: Back to the parent page when the search is empty
- ⌘ / /: Jump into the search from anywhere (Ctrl / on Windows)

### Accessibility

- The search is a combobox that controls the list; the picked row is announced as the active option
- The connection switch is a real switch with a label that says what it will do
- Details update in a polite live region when the pick changes

### Motion

- The gray highlight glides from row to row, also across the Connected and Available groups
- The service tile swaps in with a short blur and lift; the arrows between the tiles turn once when connected
- While connected, a ring keeps spreading out from the tiles – paused when the picker is off screen
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Follows its own width: below 560px the list sits above the details; the illustration and capabilities are left out
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Integration Settings (Pro)

Settings card for a connected service – on/off switch, API key, validated site address, time zone and a save bar

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/integration-settings
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-settings.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-settings`

### When to use

- The settings of one connected service – a store, an ad account, a data source
- Forms that should only save when someone confirms, with a clear way to discard

### When not to use

- Long settings pages with many sections – split them into separate cards or pages

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationSettings } from "@/components/ui/integration-settings";

export function Store() {
  return (
    <IntegrationSettings
      name="Shopify store"
      logo={<ShopifyLogo />}
      count={128}
      meta="Connected on March 4, 2026"
      defaultValues={{ siteUrl: "lumen-studio.com", timeZone: "(GMT +01:00) Berlin" }}
      onGenerateKey={() => api.createKey()}
      onSave={(values) => api.saveSettings(values)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` |  | Name of the service |
| logo | `ReactNode` |  | Logo in the white tile |
| count | `number` |  | Small number next to the name |
| meta | `string` |  | Line under the name; switching off shows a paused note instead |
| defaultValues | `Partial<IntegrationValues>` |  | enabled, siteUrl, timeZone and apiKey to start with |
| siteHint | `string` |  | Helper text under the address field |
| timeZones | `string[]` |  | Choices in the time zone picker |
| onGenerateKey | `() => string \| Promise<string>` |  | Creates a key – a random demo key without it |
| onSave | `(values) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Called with all values from the save bar |
| onToggle | `(enabled: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the switch changes |

### Keyboard

- Space: Toggle the switch
- Tab: Move through the key actions, the address and the time zone
- Escape: Close the time zone picker

### Accessibility

- The toggle is a real switch; the address field reports invalid input and points to its hint
- A new key is announced together with the reminder to copy it

### Motion

- Switching off folds the settings away, the save bar slides open on changes – reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: app-directory, data-table

## KPI Chart (Pro)

Metric card with a multi-line chart and a tooltip that follows the pointer

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/kpi-chart
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/kpi-chart.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/kpi-chart`

### When to use

- Dashboards that show one headline number and how its parts moved over a short period
- Comparing a handful of channels, pages or plans day by day

### When not to use

- More than about six lines – the chart and the tooltip get hard to read
- Long time ranges with hundreds of points – use a chart library with zoom and sampling

### Usage

```tsx
import { KpiChart } from "@/components/ui/kpi-chart";

export function Revenue() {
  return (
    <KpiChart
      title="Revenue"
      value="$96.4k"
      delta={7900}
      format={(n) => `$${(n / 1000).toFixed(1)}k`}
      labels={["Mar 3", "Mar 4", "Mar 5"]}
      series={[
        { label: "Organic", color: "#2f6bff", values: [4600, 4900, 5200] },
        { label: "Paid ads", color: "#ec4899", values: [3100, 3400, 3200] },
      ]}
      footer="Top channels"
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | Label above the number |
| value | `string` |  | Headline value, already formatted |
| delta | `number` |  | Change against the previous period – green when positive, red when negative |
| labels | `string[]` |  | One label per point; first, middle and last are shown on the axis |
| tooltipLabels | `string[]` |  | Longer labels for the tooltip header, falls back to labels |
| series | `KpiSeries[]` |  | Lines with a label, a color and one value per label |
| format | `(n: number) => string` | `compact, e.g. 1.2k` | Formats axis, tooltip and delta values |
| footer | `string` |  | Line under the chart |
| defaultIndex | `number` |  | Point that stays highlighted while nobody hovers |
| emptyText | `string` | `"No data yet"` | Quiet text in the plot when there are no values, or only zeros (0% on a percent axis still draws) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focus the chart
- ← / →: Move to the previous or next point
- Esc: Close the tooltip

### Accessibility

- The chart is focusable and readable with the arrow keys
- The tooltip is a polite live region, so screen readers announce the values of the current point

### Motion

- Lines draw in from the left on mount
- Guide, dots and tooltip glide between points; reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- The card fills its container up to 460px; the plot scales, line widths stay crisp
- Touch works too – tap or drag across the chart
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: progress-tracker

## Memory Panel (Pro)

What the assistant remembers about you, grouped and editable – a master switch, category filters, and on every memory edit in place, pause or forget with Undo on the tray

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/memory-panel
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/memory-panel.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/memory-panel`

### When to use

- Assistants and agents that remember things across chats – the place where people see, correct and remove what was kept
- Settings or a side panel next to the chat, so a wrong memory can be fixed the moment it shows up in an answer
- Products that need a clear off switch for personalization without losing what was saved

### When not to use

- What the model has in mind right now, inside one conversation – use Context Window
- Hundreds of entries with sorting and bulk actions – a Data Table handles that better
- Account settings that are not about what the assistant learned – a plain settings list says that with less

### Usage

```tsx
import { MemoryPanel } from "@/components/ui/memory-panel";

export function AssistantMemory() {
  return (
    <MemoryPanel
      memories={[
        { id: "ts", text: "Prefers TypeScript examples over plain JavaScript", category: "Preferences", source: "From chat", date: "Oct 12" },
        { id: "role", text: "Product designer and front-end developer", category: "Work", source: "From chat", date: "Sep 28" },
        { id: "fintech", text: "Redesigning a fintech onboarding flow, due Oct 24", category: "Projects", source: "From chat", date: "Oct 11" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| memories | `Memory[]` |  | { id, text, category, source?, date?, paused? } – source and date are shown as given, e.g. "From chat" and "Oct 12" |
| onChange | `(memories: Memory[]) => void` |  | Called with the full list after any change. With it the panel shows exactly the memories you pass; without it the changes live inside the panel |
| onAdd | `(memory: Memory) => void` |  | A memory was added with New memory |
| onEdit | `(id: string, text: string) => void` |  | The text of a memory was edited and saved |
| onPause | `(id: string, paused: boolean) => void` |  | A memory was paused or resumed |
| onForget | `(id: string) => void` |  | A memory was forgotten – it can still come back with Undo |
| onRestore | `(memory: Memory) => void` |  | A forgotten memory was brought back with Undo, at its old place |
| enabled | `boolean` |  | The Use memory switch, controlled |
| defaultEnabled | `boolean` | `true` | Start state of the switch when it is not controlled |
| onEnabledChange | `(enabled: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the switch is flipped |
| categories | `string[]` |  | Order of the groups and the choices for new memories – defaults to the categories in the order they appear |
| title | `string` | `"Memory"` | Heading of the panel |
| maxHeight | `number` | `360` | Height of the list in px before it scrolls |
| undoFor | `number` | `5000` | How long Undo stays on the tray after forgetting, in ms |
| addedSource | `string` | `"You added"` | Source given to memories added in the panel; their date is today |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | A button on the tray – Undo takes its place for a moment after forgetting |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Switch, the selected category chip, search, then each memory's Edit, Pause and Forget, New memory and the tray button
- ← / →: Move between category chips (and between categories of a new memory)
- Enter: Saves an edited or new memory (Shift + Enter for a line break)
- Esc: Cancels editing, closes New memory or the search field

### Accessibility

- A group named by its title; Use memory is a switch with aria-checked and controls the note that unfolds
- Category chips are a radiogroup with arrow keys and one tab stop; each group of memories is a labelled section
- Every action button is named after its memory, e.g. "Forget “Prefers TypeScript…”"; actions also show on keyboard focus
- Rows that are filtered out or folding away are inert, so the keyboard never lands on something hidden
- The tray line is announced politely: counts, the forgotten memory with Undo, and editing hints

### Motion

- Filtering folds the rows that don't match closed and fades them – nothing slides across the list
- Forgetting folds the row away with a soft blur; Undo unfolds it at its old place and scrolls it into view
- Pausing greys the text and a Paused tag fades in; the pause icon swaps to play
- Counts on the head and the tray roll to their new value; changing tray text crossfades
- Turning memory off dims the list and unfolds a short note; New memory unfolds into the editor in place of the button
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 380px; works from 300px wide. Below 340px the chips drop their counts, below 320px the switch keeps only its track
- Category chips scroll sideways when they don't fit, with a soft fade at the edge
- Touch screens: the actions are always visible and every button gets a taller hit area
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass source and date already formatted – the panel shows them as they are
- Forgetting calls onForget right after the row folds away; keep the item around (soft delete) until undoFor has passed if your backend can't restore it
- Paused memories stay in the list and count in the total; filter them out yourself before sending memories to the model
- Without onChange the panel copies memories once on mount – give it a new key to reset it

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: context-window, chat-composer, integration-settings, filter-menu

---

## Message Actions (Free)

The quiet bar under an AI message – copy turns into a check, regenerate spins and unfolds a version switcher, thumbs pop and ask why, read aloud becomes a tiny equalizer

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/message-actions
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/message-actions.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/message-actions`

### When to use

- Under every assistant message in a chat – copy, try again, rate and listen without leaving the conversation
- Wherever a model can answer more than once and people should be able to flip between the answers
- When you collect feedback on answers and want a reason, not just a thumb

### When not to use

- Under the user's own messages – edit and delete fit there better than regenerate and rating
- For a long list of actions – keep it to the four; put the rest in a menu
- When the answer is still streaming – show a stop button instead and bring the bar in once it is done

### Usage

```tsx
import { MessageActions, MessageText } from "@/components/ui/message-actions";

export function AssistantMessage({ message }) {
  const [version, setVersion] = useState(message.versions.length - 1);
  const text = message.versions[version];

  return (
    // data-ui-message lets the bar light up while the whole message is hovered
    <div data-ui-message>
      <MessageText version={version}>{text}</MessageText>
      <MessageActions
        text={text}
        versions={message.versions}
        version={version}
        onVersionChange={setVersion}
        onRegenerate={() => regenerate(message.id)}
        onFeedback={(kind, reason) => saveFeedback(message.id, version, kind, reason)}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | `string` |  | The message text – Copy writes it to the clipboard, and an uncontrolled read aloud is timed by its length |
| actions | `MessageActionKey[]` | `["copy", "regenerate", "feedback", "speak"]` | Which actions to show and in what order. feedback is the thumbs up and down |
| versions | `number \| string[]` | `1` | All versions of the message, or just how many there are. From two on the "‹ 2 / 3 ›" switcher unfolds next to Regenerate |
| version | `number` |  | Controlled version, 0-based |
| defaultVersion | `number` | `newest` | Starting version when uncontrolled. Uncontrolled, the switcher jumps to a version as soon as it is added |
| onVersionChange | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called with the version picked in the switcher |
| onCopy | `(text?: string) => void` |  | Called after Copy, with text |
| onRegenerate | `() => void` |  | Called when Regenerate is pressed – add a version to versions and it shows up in the switcher |
| regenerating | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the arrow spinning and the bar lit while a new version is written |
| onFeedback | `(kind: "up" \| "down" \| null, reason?: string) => void` |  | Called with the vote right away, with null when it is taken back, and once more with "down" and a reason when the feedback row is sent. A new version starts without a vote |
| reasons | `string[]` | `Not accurate, Too long, Didn't follow instructions, Other` | Quick reasons in the feedback row. "Other" unfolds a small text field whose words are sent as the reason |
| onSpeak | `(playing: boolean) => void` |  | Called with true when Read aloud starts and false when it stops |
| speaking | `boolean` |  | Controlled playing state – tie it to your speech player. Without it the bar plays for speakDuration and stops on its own |
| speakDuration | `number` | `from text, at least 2600` | How long an uncontrolled read aloud plays, in ms |
| quiet | `boolean` | `true` | Faded until the message (an ancestor with data-ui-message) or the bar is hovered or focused. Touch screens always show it fully |
| label | `string` | `"Message actions"` | Accessible name of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the actions, the version arrows and – when it is open – the reasons and Send
- Enter / Space: Presses an action, picks or drops a reason, sends
- Enter: In the "Other" text field: sends
- Esc: Closes the feedback row and puts focus back on thumbs down

### Accessibility

- Each action is a button with its own name; the thumbs and Read aloud are toggle buttons with aria-pressed, thumbs down has aria-expanded for the feedback row
- Tooltips repeat the button names, so they are hidden from screen readers; they also show on keyboard focus
- Copied, the version you switched to, Reading aloud and Thanks are announced through a polite live region
- The version arrows are disabled at either end, and the count is read as "Version 2 of 3"
- While closed, the feedback row is inert – nothing hidden can be focused

### Motion

- Copy blurs into a check that draws itself; it turns back after a moment
- Regenerate spins once per press, and keeps spinning while regenerating is true
- A vote fills the thumb with a small pop; the feedback row unfolds below the bar and folds away after Thanks
- The version switcher unfolds sideways from Regenerate; its number crossfades, and MessageText crossfades the message while its height eases
- Read aloud swaps the speaker for four bouncing bars
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement and the bars stand still

### Responsive

- The bar is about 230px wide with the switcher; the feedback row fills its container up to 440px and its reasons wrap
- Below 320px the Send button takes its own line under the reasons
- Touch screens: 38px buttons, taller reasons, no hover tooltips (only "Copied"), and the bar is never faded
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Put data-ui-message on the element that wraps the message and the bar – that is what lights the quiet bar up on hover
- Keep versions per message in your state and pass version + onVersionChange; after a regenerate, set version to the new last index
- onFeedback fires twice for a thumbs down with a reason – once with only the vote, once with the reason. Upsert by message and version instead of inserting rows
- The bar does not speak by itself – pass speaking and onSpeak and drive speechSynthesis or your TTS from there

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: ai-answer, reaction-bar, chat-composer, thinking-state

---

## Model Picker (Pro)

The model menu of an AI chat – point at a model and its speed, quality and cost bars fill, switch on extended thinking and its effort unfolds, while the tray rolls the first-token time and price

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/model-picker
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/model-picker.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/model-picker`

### When to use

- The model switch in the toolbar of a chat composer – the place people decide between fast, cheap and smart
- Products with a few models that differ in speed, quality and price, and settings that ride along with the model: thinking, effort, web search
- When people should see what a choice costs them before they send – the tray shows first-token time and price

### When not to use

- Dozens of models from many providers – use Combobox or Command Menu, where people can type to search
- A setting page that lists every parameter – this menu is for the two or three things people change between messages
- A plain two-way choice – Segmented Control says it with less

### Usage

```tsx
import { ModelPicker } from "@/components/ui/model-picker";

const models = [
  { id: "opus", name: "Opus 5.5", description: "Hardest problems", speed: 2, quality: 5, cost: 5, latencyMs: 2100, pricePerM: 25 },
  { id: "sonnet", name: "Sonnet 5.5", description: "Everyday work", speed: 4, quality: 4, cost: 3, latencyMs: 900, pricePerM: 15 },
  { id: "haiku", name: "Haiku 5.5", description: "Quick and light", speed: 5, quality: 3, cost: 1, latencyMs: 400, pricePerM: 4 },
];

export function ComposerToolbar() {
  return (
    <div className="toolbar">
      <ModelPicker models={models} defaultValue="sonnet" />
      <SendButton />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| models | `PickerModel[]` |  | { id, name, description?, icon?, speed?, quality?, cost?, latencyMs?, pricePerM? } – strengths go from 1 to 5 (cost 5 is the most expensive); leave all three out for a router like Auto and the row says "Varies" |
| value | `string` |  | Id of the chosen model (controlled) |
| defaultValue | `string` | `first model` | Chosen model when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the picked model's id |
| thinking | `boolean` |  | Extended thinking switch (controlled) |
| defaultThinking | `boolean` | `false` | Starting state of the thinking switch |
| onThinkingChange | `(on: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the thinking switch flips |
| webSearch | `boolean` |  | Web search switch (controlled) |
| defaultWebSearch | `boolean` | `false` | Starting state of the web search switch |
| onWebSearchChange | `(on: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the web search switch flips |
| effort | `"low" \| "medium" \| "high"` |  | Thinking effort (controlled) – the control only shows while thinking is on |
| defaultEffort | `"low" \| "medium" \| "high"` | `"medium"` | Starting effort |
| onEffortChange | `(effort) => void` |  | Called with the new effort |
| open | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state of the menu |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Starts open when uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the menu opens or closes |
| align | `"start" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with |
| side | `"bottom" \| "top"` | `"bottom"` | Opens below or above the trigger – use top for a composer at the bottom of the screen |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space / ↓: On the trigger: opens the menu and moves into the model list
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: In the list: moves between models – the tray follows
- Enter / Space: In the list: picks the model and closes the menu
- Tab: From the list to Extended thinking, Effort and Web search
- ← / →: In Effort: Low, Medium, High
- Esc: Closes the menu and returns to the trigger

### Accessibility

- The trigger has aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls; its name carries the model and whether thinking is on
- Models are a listbox with options and aria-activedescendant, so focus stays on the list while the arrows move
- Thinking and web search are switches, Effort is a radio group with one tab stop
- While closed the menu is inert; the tray's numbers are announced politely once, not while they roll

### Motion

- The menu opens with a short fade and a soft scale from the corner of the trigger, and closes the same way
- Pointing at a model fills its bars segment by segment and steps the other rows back
- Effort unfolds under the thinking switch; its white thumb slides to the chosen level
- First-token time and price roll to their new values; the model name in the trigger crossfades and a small bulb unfolds next to it while thinking is on
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- The menu is 320px wide and never wider than the screen minus 32px. Below 300px the row glyphs and key hints give way and the bars move closer
- Touch screens: taller trigger, rows, switches and effort buttons; the key hints are hidden
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The menu is positioned absolutely from the trigger – keep the composer's overflow visible, or the menu gets cut
- Pick side="top" when the composer sits at the bottom of the viewport, and align="end" when the trigger is on the right
- latencyMs is the time without thinking; the tray multiplies it by the effort (×1.6, ×2.5, ×4) while thinking is on
- Keep descriptions to two or three words – the row has room for one short line next to the bars

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: chat-composer, combobox, segmented-control, context-window

## Notification Stack (Free)

Notice cards stacked behind each other – dismiss the front one to reveal the next

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/notification-stack
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/notification-stack.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/notification-stack`

### When to use

- A few announcements or notices in a corner of an app – releases, maintenance, invites
- Toast-style messages that stay until someone dismisses them

### When not to use

- Messages that need an answer before people continue – use a dialog
- Many notifications at once – past three or four, use an inbox or activity list

### Usage

```tsx
import { NotificationStack } from "@/components/ui/notification-stack";

const notices = [
  {
    id: "maintenance",
    badge: "Notice",
    title: "Scheduled maintenance",
    text: "We'll be offline on Sunday from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.",
    action: { label: "View status", href: "/status", external: true },
    pattern: "grid",
  },
];

export function Notices() {
  return <NotificationStack notices={notices} onDismiss={(n) => markRead(n.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| notices | `Notice[]` |  | id, badge, title, text, action ({ label, href, onClick, external }) and pattern |
| onDismiss | `(notice: Notice) => void` |  | Called when a notice is dismissed with its close button |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the stack |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move through the front card's buttons
- Enter / Space: Run the action or dismiss the notice

### Accessibility

- The stack is a labelled region; each card is an article named by its title
- Only the front card is read out and focusable; the next one takes its place after a dismiss

### Motion

- A dismissed card slides away and the next one moves up into its place; reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: decision-inbox, tips-panel

## OTP Input (Free)

The verification code field done right – a gliding focus ring, paste and SMS autofill, a calm shake on errors and a morph into Verified

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/otp-input
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/otp-input.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/otp-input`

### When to use

- Two-step sign-in, email or phone verification, confirming a sensitive action with a one-time code
- Any short code people copy from an email or SMS – paste and autofill fill every box at once

### When not to use

- Codes longer than about 8 characters or with free-form text – a plain text field is easier to read and correct
- Passwords or PINs that must stay hidden – the boxes show what's typed

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { OtpInput, type OtpStatus } from "@/components/ui/otp-input";

export function VerifyEmail() {
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<OtpStatus>("idle");
  const [triesLeft, setTriesLeft] = useState(3);

  async function verify(value: string) {
    setStatus("verifying");
    const res = await fetch("/api/verify", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ code: value }) });
    if (res.ok) {
      setStatus("success");
      router.push("/dashboard");
    } else {
      setTriesLeft((n) => n - 1);
      setStatus("error");
    }
  }

  return (
    <OtpInput
      value={code}
      onChange={(next) => {
        setCode(next);
        if (status === "error" && next) setStatus("idle");
      }}
      onComplete={verify}
      status={status}
      errorMessage={`That code didn't work. ${triesLeft} tries left.`}
      separator
      autoFocus
      onResend={() => fetch("/api/send-code", { method: "POST" })}
      resendIn={30}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| length | `number` | `6` | Number of boxes |
| separator | `boolean \| number` | `false` | A small dash between the boxes – true puts it in the middle, a number after that many boxes |
| numeric | `boolean` | `true` | Digits only with the numeric keyboard on phones; false allows letters too, shown in capitals |
| value | `string` |  | The code – makes the field controlled |
| defaultValue | `string` | `""` | Starting code when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(code: string) => void` |  | Every change: typing, Backspace, paste, autofill and the clearing after an error |
| onComplete | `(code: string) => void` |  | Called once the last box is filled by the user – the place to start verifying |
| status | `"idle" \| "verifying" \| "error" \| "success"` | `"idle"` | Verifying shimmers and locks the field, error shakes and shows the message, success morphs into the pill |
| errorMessage | `ReactNode` | `"That code didn't work. Try again."` | Shown below the boxes after an error, until the user types again |
| clearOnError | `boolean` | `true` | Clears the boxes shortly after the shake, ready for the next try |
| successLabel | `string` | `"Verified"` | Text in the pill on success |
| onResend | `() => void` |  | Shows "Didn't get a code?" below the boxes with a countdown that becomes a Resend button; clicking restarts the countdown |
| resendIn | `number` | `30` | Seconds until the code can be resent |
| align | `"start" \| "center"` | `"start"` | Where the boxes and the lines below them sit |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Dims the field and ignores input |
| autoFocus | `boolean` | `false` | Focuses the field on mount (without scrolling) |
| label | `string` | `"Verification code"` | Accessible name; the number of digits is added |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- 0–9: Fills the active box and moves on; typing on a filled box replaces it
- ⌫: Clears the box and goes back one
- ← / →: Moves between the filled boxes and the next empty one
- Home / End: Jumps to the first box, or to the next empty one
- ⌘ / V: Pastes a whole code – spaces and dashes are ignored

### Accessibility

- One real text input carries the whole code, so screen readers hear one field ("Verification code, 6 digits") instead of six
- autocomplete="one-time-code" lets iOS and Android offer the code from an SMS; inputMode="numeric" opens the number pad
- Errors set aria-invalid and point to the message with aria-describedby; verifying, errors, success and resend are announced in a polite live region

### Motion

- A single focus ring glides from box to box with a softly blinking caret; digits pop in out of a short blur
- Pasted or autofilled codes fill the boxes one after another
- Verifying: a soft light passes over the boxes. Error: a calm shake, red borders, the message grows in below and the code fades out for the next try
- Success: the boxes slide together while one frame morphs its width into a "Verified" pill and the check draws in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Container query: the boxes shrink to fit their container – six boxes with a separator fit a 320px phone
- Inputs use 16px text under the hood, so iOS doesn't zoom in on focus
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: combobox, segmented-control, button, toaster

---

## Parallel Attempts (Pro)

An agent tries the same task several ways at once and the best one wins – every attempt races as a row with its model, approach and live bar, then gets a score; the best is marked and picked, and you can switch to another

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/parallel-attempts
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/parallel-attempts.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/parallel-attempts`

### When to use

- An agent tries a task several ways at once – different models, prompts or approaches – and the best result wins
- Best-of-N runs, where you want to see them race, compare their scores and keep the say in which one is used
- Code fixes, drafts or plans that are cheap to try in parallel and easy to score

### When not to use

- One run and where its time goes – use Trace Waterfall
- Many small tasks spread over workers – use Fan-out Grid
- A single decision the agent can't take alone – use Decision Tree

### Usage

```tsx
import { ParallelAttempts, type Attempt } from "@/components/ui/parallel-attempts";

const attempts: Attempt[] = [
  { id: "a", name: "Opus 5.5", approach: "Add a retry with backoff",
    status: "running", progress: 0.6, step: "Running tests 12/20" },
  { id: "b", name: "GPT-6 Sol", approach: "Mock the payment API",
    status: "done", score: 94, note: "20/20 runs green", took: 125000, cost: 0.27 },
];

export function Fix() {
  return <ParallelAttempts attempts={attempts} task="Fix the flaky checkout test" onPick={(a) => apply(a.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| attempts | `Attempt[]` |  | { id, name, approach, model?, icon?, status, progress?, step?, score?, note?, took?, cost? } – one per attempt, in the order the rows should show; name is usually the model, icon its logo (on a small tile before the name) |
| status | `"running" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per attempt – picks the bar's tint: blue with a shine, green, red |
| progress | `number` |  | Per attempt, 0 to 1 – the bar's length while it runs (and where a failed one stopped) |
| step | `string` |  | Per attempt – what it does right now, shown on the right while it runs |
| score | `number` |  | Per attempt, 0–100 once done – the highest is marked Best and picked unless you pick another |
| note | `string` |  | Per attempt – one line about the outcome, or the error |
| task | `string` |  | What all of them try to do, next to the title |
| picked | `string \| null` |  | Controlled pick – leave it out and the best finished attempt is picked on its own |
| onPick | `(attempt) => void` |  | Another attempt was picked with "Use this one" |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Best of N"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves to the finished attempts' "Use this one" buttons
- Enter / Space: Uses the focused attempt

### Accessibility

- The rows are a radiogroup labelled with the title; each finished attempt's button is a radio with its name and score
- Bars are decoration – what they show is in the text beside them

### Motion

- Rows come in a beat after each other
- Running bars grow with a shine sweeping over them and a soft glow at their leading edge
- When an attempt finishes its bar turns green or red; the line under its name turns into the outcome in place – cards never change height
- The best one gets a Best tag; the one in use a soft green wash, while the others step back – pointing at one brings it forward again
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: wide, name, bar and score sit in one line
- Under 560px the bar moves under the name, the approach drops out and the score sits beside the name
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass every attempt every time something changes – ids keep rows in place
- progress is 0–1; a failed attempt keeps the progress where it stopped
- Scores are yours to define (tests passed, an eval, a judge) – only their order matters for Best
- Colors are variables on .ui-pa, e.g. --ui-pa-best-bg / --ui-pa-best-edge
- The tick icon is Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: fan-out-grid, agent-lanes, trace-waterfall, decision-tree
