## Trace Waterfall (Pro)

Where the time and money of an agent run go – every LLM call, tool call and sub-agent as a bar on a live timeline, with tokens and cost per step, the slowest call marked and branches that fold into their parent

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/trace-waterfall
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/trace-waterfall.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/trace-waterfall`

### When to use

- Debugging an agent run: how long each step took, where the time and the money went, which call is slow
- A run view next to a chat or a log – every LLM call, tool call and sub-agent as a bar on one timeline
- Live runs, where you want to watch spans start, grow and finish while the agent works

### When not to use

- Who started whom, at a glance – use Agent Tree
- Several agents side by side over the last half hour – use Agent Lanes
- One agent's plan as a checklist – use Agent Plan

### Usage

```tsx
import { TraceWaterfall, type TraceSpan } from "@/components/ui/trace-waterfall";

const run: TraceSpan = {
  id: "run", name: "Orchestrator", kind: "agent", status: "running", start: 0,
  input: "Launch the new pricing page",
  children: [
    { id: "plan", name: "Plan the launch", kind: "llm", model: "Opus 5.5", detail: "Opus 5.5", status: "done",
      start: 900, end: 7800, tokensIn: 3240, tokensOut: 880, cost: 0.115 },
    { id: "search", name: "web_search", kind: "tool", detail: "Linear pricing", status: "running", start: 8100 },
  ],
};

export function Run({ startedAt }: { startedAt: number }) {
  // Times are ms from the start of the run; with startedAt the component keeps its own clock while it runs
  return <TraceWaterfall root={run} startedAt={startedAt} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| root | `TraceSpan` |  | { id, name, kind, status, start, end?, detail?, icon?, model?, tokensIn?, tokensOut?, cost?, input?, output?, error?, children? } – the whole run as a tree, rebuilt as it goes on |
| kind | `"agent" \| "subagent" \| "llm" \| "tool"` |  | Per span – picks the bar's tint: agents slate, LLM calls violet, tool calls teal; failed spans are red |
| status | `"running" \| "done" \| "failed"` |  | Per span – a running span has no end yet and grows into "now" |
| start / end | `number` |  | Per span, in ms from the start of the run; leave end out while it runs |
| detail | `string` |  | Per span – a few muted words after the name, e.g. the model or the query |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Per span – a small mark, e.g. the model maker's or the tool's logo; defaults to a swatch in the kind's color |
| cost / tokensIn / tokensOut | `number` |  | Per span, its own – agents add up their children, so don't pre-sum |
| input / output / error | `string` |  | Per span – short previews shown in the details window |
| now | `number` |  | The clock in ms from the start of the run – e.g. a faster one for a demo or a replay |
| startedAt | `number` |  | When the run started (epoch ms) – without now, the component ticks its own clock from here while a span runs |
| collapsed / defaultCollapsed | `string[]` | `[]` | Ids of folded spans, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onCollapsedChange | `(collapsed: string[]) => void` |  | A span was folded or opened |
| openId / defaultOpenId | `string \| null` | `null` | The span whose details are open, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(id: string \| null, span?: TraceSpan) => void` |  | Details opened (with the span) or closed |
| markSlowest | `boolean` | `true` | Marks the slowest finished LLM or tool call with a small "Slowest" tag |
| minRange | `number` | `10000` | The shortest time the axis shows, in ms – it grows in round steps as the run gets longer |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.042"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Trace"` | Heading of the bar; next to it the root's input (or name) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves into the waterfall (one row is in the tab order) and on to the details window
- ArrowUp / ArrowDown: Moves between the rows; Home and End jump to the first and the last
- ArrowRight: Opens a folded span, or moves to its first child
- ArrowLeft: Folds an open span, or moves to its parent
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes the details of the focused span
- Esc: Closes the details

### Accessibility

- The rows are a tree: every span is a treeitem with its level, labelled with name, kind, status, duration and cost; aria-expanded on spans with children
- Roving focus – only one row is in the tab order, so the waterfall is a single stop
- The details window is a dialog labelled with the span's name, with a close button; Esc closes it and returns focus to the row
- The run's state in the bar (Live, Done, Failed) is announced politely when it changes
- Ticks, grid lines and the "now" line are decoration and hidden from assistive tech

### Motion

- New spans slide in as rows and their bars grow from their start point
- A running span grows live, with a sheen and a soft glow at its leading edge; a "now" line moves across
- When the run outgrows the axis, the range glides to the next round value – ticks fade in and out where they are, bars rescale with it, nothing jumps
- Folding closes the children's rows smoothly and shows their calls as small marks on the parent bar; the chevron turns
- Rows that leave – a new run, removed data – close up a beat after each other, bottom first
- The details window opens with a soft scale and fade from the row's bar, and closes the same way
- Numbers that still climb – the duration, cost and tokens of a live run – carry a light shimmer
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- Built on a container query: wide, the span tree sits on the left and the timeline on the right
- Under 560px each row stacks – name, duration and cost on one line, the bar across the whole width under it; the numbers wrap to three columns
- Under 360px the muted detail after each name drops out, so names keep their room
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole tree every time something changes – ids keep rows in place, new ids slide in and grow
- start and end are ms from the run's start, not timestamps – subtract the run's start time from your span times
- cost and tokens are the span's own; agents and sub-agents add their children up
- A retried call is a new span with its own id – keep the failed one, it tells the story
- For a live run pass startedAt (the component ticks) or drive now yourself; once nothing runs, the axis settles on the last end
- Colors are variables on .ui-tw, e.g. --ui-tw-llm-bg / --ui-tw-llm-edge for LLM calls
- The chevron, warning and close icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-tree, agent-lanes, agent-plan, agent-steering

---

## Usage Meter (Pro)

Plan usage and AI credits – a stacked credits meter by category, daily sparkline, limits and a button that speaks up near the limit

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/usage-meter
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/usage-meter.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/usage-meter`

### When to use

- The usage or billing page of a SaaS or AI product – credits, tokens, minutes or messages per billing cycle
- Showing what the usage went into (chat, search, images, API) next to plan limits like seats and storage
- Nudging people to top up or upgrade right where they see they're running out

### When not to use

- Long-term trends over many months – a line chart like the KPI Chart reads better
- More than about five categories – the bar gets too thin; group the small ones into "Other"

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { UsageMeter } from "@/components/ui/usage-meter";

export function Usage({ usage }) {
  const [period, setPeriod] = useState("month");
  const data = usage[period]; // { used, limits, daily } per period from your API

  return (
    <UsageMeter
      title="Acme AI"
      plan="Pro plan"
      total={10000}
      used={data.used} // [{ label: "Chat", value: 3980 }, { label: "Search", value: 1640 }, …]
      limits={[
        { label: "Seats", used: 8, total: 10 },
        { label: "Storage", used: 3.2, total: 5, unit: "GB" },
        { label: "Projects", used: 12, total: null }, // unlimited
      ]}
      daily={data.daily} // [{ label: "Oct 1", value: 312 }, …, { label: "Oct 17", value: null }]
      periods={[
        { id: "month", label: "This month" },
        { id: "last", label: "Last month" },
        { id: "7d", label: "7 days" },
      ]}
      period={period}
      onPeriodChange={setPeriod}
      resetAt="2026-10-17"
      onUpgrade={(state) => (state === "ok" ? openPlans() : openTopUp())}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| total | `number` |  | Credits included in the plan – the bar's full width |
| used | `{ label: string; value: number; color?: string }[]` |  | What the credits went into in the shown period. Without colors the parts get shades of the accent, then grays; each label keeps its shade |
| limits | `{ label; used; total?: number \| null; unit?; decimals? }[]` |  | Thin meters below, e.g. seats and storage. Leave total out (or null) for unlimited – shown as "of ∞" on a striped track |
| periods | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | Options of the period switch; no switch when left out |
| period | `string` |  | Controlled period id – pass the matching used, limits and daily with it |
| defaultPeriod | `string` |  | Starting period when uncontrolled; defaults to the first option |
| onPeriodChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called when a period is picked |
| resetAt | `Date \| string \| number` |  | When the credits reset – shown as "Resets in 9 days", the date on hover |
| daily | `{ label: string; value: number \| null }[]` |  | Usage per day for the sparkline; null for days still to come, shown as flat stubs |
| onUpgrade | `(state: "ok" \| "warn" \| "limit") => void` |  | Called by the button with the current state |
| title | `string` | `"Usage"` | Card title, e.g. the workspace or product name |
| plan | `string` |  | Plan name in front of the reset date |
| unit | `string` | `"credits"` | Unit of the main meter |
| warnAt | `number` | `0.8` | Share (0–1) from which the meter and the limits warn |
| upgradeLabel | `string` | `"Upgrade"` | Button text while there is room left (a quiet button) |
| topUpLabel | `string` | `"Add credits"` | Button text near and at the limit (a solid button) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Reaches the period switch, the bar, the sparkline and the button
- ← / →: Switch: picks the previous or next period. Bar: steps through the categories. Sparkline: steps through the days
- Esc: Hides the category or day readout

### Accessibility

- A section labelled by its title; the bar and every limit are meters with their value as text ("7,420 of 10,000 credits")
- The period switch is a radio group with a roving tab stop
- The category tooltip is a polite live region, so stepping through the bar reads each part
- Running low and reaching the limit are announced in a polite live region; amber is never the only signal – the text says it too

### Motion

- On first view the bar fills from zero and every number counts up, in one frame loop so numbers and widths stay in step
- Switching periods: the white pill glides to the new option, numbers roll to their new values and the parts glide to their new widths
- A category that drops out shrinks to nothing on the bar while its legend row folds away; the card glides to its new height
- Hovering a part dims the others and highlights its legend row; the tooltip glides along the bar
- Near the limit a small amber dot pops in and the button turns solid with a gentle nudge, its width gliding to the new label
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 460px; at 400px and below the switch gets its own row and the limits stack as rows
- Works down to 320px wide; long labels end with an ellipsis, numbers and units never split
- Touch: tapping a part or a legend row shows its value, targets grow to 36–38px
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: kpi-chart, breakdown-chart, billing-schedule, progress-tracker

## Writing Assistant (Pro)

AI chat card with a soft gradient glow, suggestions, streaming replies and live voice dictation

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/writing-assistant
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/writing-assistant.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/writing-assistant`

### When to use

- A small AI helper inside an editor, CRM or sidebar – rewrite, shorten, translate or draft
- Landing pages that should show an assistant you can actually try, including voice input

### When not to use

- Long conversations with files, tools and model settings – use the Chat Composer or the AI Workspace block
- When you can't send voice to the browser's speech service – set speech="simulate" or hide the mic

### Usage

```tsx
import { WritingAssistant } from "@/components/ui/writing-assistant";

export function Helper() {
  return (
    <WritingAssistant
      name="Quill"
      tagline="Your writing companion."
      respond={async (message) => {
        const res = await fetch("/api/write", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ message }) });
        return (await res.json()).text;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | `"Quill"` | Assistant name on top |
| tagline | `string` | `"Your writing companion."` | Line under the name |
| greeting | `string` | `"What should we write?"` | Big line on the welcome screen |
| suggestions | `string[]` |  | Chips that send themselves as a message |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Ask anything…"` | Placeholder of the prompt field |
| respond | `(message) => string \| Promise<string>` |  | Your answer for a message; a sample writer is used by default |
| speech | `"auto" \| "simulate"` | `"auto"` | auto uses the browser's speech recognition when available, simulate always plays a sample take |
| dictation | `string` |  | Sentence used for simulated dictation |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Sends what's in the prompt field
- Shift / Enter: Starts a new line – the field grows up to four lines, then scrolls
- Tab: Moves through the suggestions, the field, Send, the mic and New chat

### Accessibility

- The mic is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label that says what it does next
- New messages are announced politely; the typing dots carry a label
- Everything works with the keyboard; dictation is optional

### Motion

- The glow keeps drifting in the lower half; the welcome view hands over to the chat with a short rise
- While listening, the mic turns dark with three calm bars and a soft ring breathing outwards; words appear live in the field
- When you stop speaking, the finished sentence moves into the chat as your message; replies stream in word by word
- With prefers-reduced-motion the glow stands still and replies appear at once

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 380px wide
- Dictation uses the Web Speech API (Chrome, Edge, Safari) with the page language; elsewhere a short simulated take plays
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Agent Run (Pro)

One autonomous agent run: the plan ticking through its steps, the tool calls, an approval it waits on and the draft it wrote

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-run
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-run.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-run`

### When to use

- The detail view of one autonomous agent run – a background task, a scheduled job, a long workflow
- Runs that pause for a human before they send, pay or publish something

### When not to use

- Back-and-forth conversations with the agent – use Agent Chat
- A list of many runs – use a table with a status column

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentRunScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-run";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <AgentRunScreen
      title="Prepare the Q3 board update"
      steps={run.steps}
      draft={{ original: memo.before, suggested: memo.after, label: "Board memo – Q3" }}
      onApprove={(stepId) => api.approve(run.id, stepId)}
      onDeny={(stepId) => api.deny(run.id, stepId)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` | `"Prepare the Q3 board update"` | Goal of the run, in the header and above the plan |
| steps | `RunStep[]` | `defaultRunSteps` | Steps with id, title, detail, tool, their tool calls ({ name, summary, icon?, args?, result?, duration }) and an optional approval ({ title, description, risk, details }) the run waits on |
| draft | `{ original: string; suggested: string; label?: string }` | `defaultRunDraft` | Text the agent wrote, shown as an inline diff in the side panel |
| agent | `string` | `"Board prep"` | Name of the agent in the run details |
| autoRun | `boolean` | `true` | Plays the built-in simulation on mount – turn off and drive the steps from your own events |
| onApprove | `(stepId: string) => void` |  | An approval was given; the run carries on |
| onDeny | `(stepId: string) => void` |  | An approval was denied; the run stops at that step |
| onStop | `() => void` |  | Stop run pressed |
| onDone | `() => void` |  | Every step is done |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name in the sidebar |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, the run actions and the panel toggle are real buttons with labels
- The plan marks the current step with aria-current and announces progress; tool calls and approvals announce their status
- Approve and deny work from the keyboard (⌘↵ / Esc), the diff with Tab, Y and N
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app; the run and the side panel scroll on their own
- Below 1000px of main area the side panel becomes a layer that slides in from the right
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell Inset, Agent Plan, Tool Call Card, Approval Card, Inline Diff, Thinking Loader and Button (installed with it)

---

## Analytics (Pro)

Revenue dashboard: key figures, revenue by channel, breakdown, top products and weekly trends

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/analytics
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/analytics.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/analytics`

### When to use

- Revenue, product or marketing dashboards
- Overview pages that combine key figures and charts

### When not to use

- Live monitoring with many changing values – use a denser layout

### Usage

```tsx
import { AnalyticsScreen } from "@/components/ui/analytics";

export default function Page() {
  return <AnalyticsScreen workspace="Acme" user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }} onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name in the sidebar |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| stats | `{ label: string; value: string; delta: string; bars: number[]; good?: "up" \| "down" }[]` |  | Key figures on top – shown as given; good says which way of the delta is good news |
| breakdown | `{ label: string; value: string; spark: number[]; tone?: "up" \| "down" \| "flat" }[]` |  | Lines of the revenue breakdown |
| products | `{ label: string; value: string; share: number }[]` |  | Top products, share in % of the best one |
| channels | `KpiSeries[]` |  | Lines of the revenue chart, one value per day |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, tabs and toolbar actions are real buttons with labels
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, KPI Chart and Button (installed with it)

## App Shell Flat (Pro)

The App Shell laid flat – gray sidebar and an edge-to-edge page, split by a single hairline

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/app-shell-flat
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/app-shell-flat.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/app-shell-flat`

### When to use

- Tools and dashboards that should feel calm and edge to edge, like Linear or Notion
- Dense screens – tables, boards, editors – that want every pixel instead of a framed panel

### When not to use

- When the page should read as a card on a gray page – use App Shell Inset
- Marketing pages – use a block or a plain layout

### Usage

```tsx
import { AppShellFlat } from "@/components/ui/app-shell-flat";

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <AppShellFlat active="New chat" workspace="Acme" user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }} onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}>
      <div className="ui-as-page">{children}</div>
    </AppShellFlat>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| header | `{ title: ReactNode; actions?: ReactNode } \| false` | `the open page's name, share and more` | The header across the app – sidebar toggle and search, the page's title and actions; false for none |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The page shown next to the sidebar |
| active | `string` |  | Label of the menu item or project that is open |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a menu item or project when it is clicked |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name; its first letter becomes the logo |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom; without an avatar it shows initials |
| nav | `ShellNavItem[]` | `New chat, Folders, Integrations` | Menu items, each { label, icon } |
| projects | `string[]` |  | Project list under the menu |
| groups | `ShellGroup[]` |  | Lists under the menu instead of Projects, e.g. Tools or Pipelines |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, projects and the collapse toggle are real buttons with labels
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Below 900px the sidebar becomes a drawer that slides in over the page
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Same props and the same page classes (.ui-as-page, .ui-as-page-title) as App Shell Inset – swap one for the other without touching the screens inside

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell Inset (installed with it)

Related: app-shell

---

## App Shell Inset (Pro)

Collapsible sidebar with workspace, menu, projects and account – the frame every screen sits in

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/app-shell
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/app-shell.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/app-shell`

### When to use

- The base of an AI assistant, internal tool or SaaS dashboard
- Building your own screens on the same frame as the other affectUI screens

### When not to use

- Marketing pages – use a block or a plain layout
- Apps with deep, multi-level navigation trees

### Usage

```tsx
import { AppShell } from "@/components/ui/app-shell";

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <AppShell active="New chat" workspace="Acme" user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }} onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}>
      <div className="ui-as-page">{children}</div>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The page shown next to the sidebar |
| active | `string` |  | Label of the menu item or project that is open |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a menu item or project when it is clicked |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name; its first letter becomes the logo |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom; without an avatar it shows initials |
| nav | `ShellNavItem[]` | `New chat, Folders, Integrations` | Menu items, each { label, icon } |
| projects | `string[]` |  | Project list under the menu |
| sidebarWidth | `{ default?: number; min?: number; max?: number }` | `{ default: 272, min: 220, max: 380 }` | Sidebar width in px – drag its edge between min and max, double-click the edge for the default |
| header | `{ title: ReactNode; actions?: ReactNode } \| false` |  | A header across the whole app, like Claude's – sidebar toggle and search, the page's title (BarTitle) and actions, the work area's title; one line under it |
| panel | `ReactNode` |  | A work area on the right of the page (tools, a preview, files) – resizable and collapsible like the sidebar |
| panelTitle | `string` | `"Workspace"` | Heading of the work area on the right |
| panelWidth | `{ default?: number; min?: number; max?: number }` | `{ default: 360, min: 280, max: 560 }` | Width of the work area in px, like sidebarWidth |
| layout | `"inset" \| "flat"` | `"inset"` | Inset: the page as a rounded panel on the gray page. Flat: edge to edge next to the sidebar, split by a hairline. Without it, data-shell="flat" on an ancestor (e.g. <html>) makes every App Shell flat |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, projects and the collapse toggle are real buttons with labels
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers
- The edges are separators you can focus: arrow keys resize (Shift for bigger steps), Home and End jump to the minimum and maximum

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as
- Inset or flat for a whole app at once: data-shell="flat" on <html> – every screen built on App Shell follows

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons

---

## App Shell Workspace Flat (Pro)

The flat App Shell with a resizable work area on the right – sidebar, page and tools, each split by a hairline

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/app-shell-workspace-flat
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/app-shell-workspace-flat.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/app-shell-workspace-flat`

### When to use

- AI assistants and agent tools that keep a terminal, browser or sources next to the conversation
- Editors and dashboards with a detail or preview pane beside the page

### When not to use

- When the page needs the full width – use App Shell Flat without the work area
- Marketing pages – use a block or a plain layout

### Usage

```tsx
import { AppShellWorkspaceFlat } from "@/components/ui/app-shell-workspace-flat";

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <AppShellWorkspaceFlat active="New chat" onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])} onOpen={(id) => openTool(id)}>
      <div className="ui-as-page">{children}</div>
    </AppShellWorkspaceFlat>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The page shown between the sidebar and the work area |
| tools | `WorkspaceTool[]` | `Terminal, Browser, Notes` | Rows under Tools, each { id, label, icon, shortcut? } |
| sources | `WorkspaceSource[]` |  | Rows under Suggested, each { id, title, source, mark? } |
| onOpen | `(id: string) => void` |  | A tool or a suggestion was clicked |
| panel | `ReactNode` |  | Your own content for the work area instead of tools and suggestions |
| panelTitle | `string` | `"Workspace"` | Heading of the work area |
| panelWidth | `{ default?: number; min?: number; max?: number }` | `{ default: 360, min: 280, max: 560 }` | Work area width in px – drag its edge between min and max |
| sidebarWidth | `{ default?: number; min?: number; max?: number }` | `{ default: 272, min: 220, max: 380 }` | Sidebar width in px, the same way |
| … | `AppShellProps` |  | Everything App Shell takes: active, onNavigate, workspace, user, nav, projects, groups, setup, className |

### Accessibility

- Both edges are separators you can focus: arrow keys resize (Shift for bigger steps), Home and End jump to the minimum and maximum, double-click resets
- The work area is a labelled landmark; while it's folded away it's inert, and its icon in the top right brings it back

### Responsive

- Below 900px the work area becomes a drawer from the right, like the sidebar from the left; Escape or a tap beside it closes it
- Dark mode built in, from the App Shell tokens

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell Inset, App Shell Flat and App Shell Workspace Inset (installed with it)

---

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell (installed with it)

## Onboarding (Pro)

First-run flow of an AI workspace: workspace setup, tool connections, team invites and a first agent, with a getting-started checklist

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/onboarding
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/onboarding.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/onboarding`

### When to use

- The first minutes after sign-up in a workspace or AI product
- Guided setup that people can skip and pick up again later

### When not to use

- Long forms with many required fields – use the Stepper Form
- A single setting – show it inline instead of a whole flow

### Usage

```tsx
import { OnboardingScreen } from "@/components/ui/onboarding";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <OnboardingScreen
      workspace="Acme"
      user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }}
      defaultStep={1}
      onComplete={(values) => api.finishOnboarding(values)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| defaultStep | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `2` | Step shown first; the steps before it count as done |
| defaultInvites | `string[]` | `["jamie@acme.com"]` | Addresses already in the invite field, e.g. from the sign-up form |
| onComplete | `(values: OnboardingValues) => void` |  | Called after Create agent (or skipping the last step) with workspace, slug, team size, tools, invites, role and template |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item or a next step (Chat, Integrations, Analytics) |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name in the sidebar, the greeting and the first field |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar; the first name is used in the greeting |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Each step is a form: Enter continues, the primary button submits
- Progress is a progressbar with the step name as its value text; the checklist marks the current step with aria-current
- Tool toggles are switches, templates a radio group; email chips can be removed with their button or Backspace
- Step transitions and checkmarks turn off with prefers-reduced-motion

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- The checklist sits beside the step card on wide panels and moves below it on narrow ones
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, Segmented Control and Button (installed with it)

## AI Workspace (Pro)

Complete assistant app – sidebar, welcome, streaming chat and projects, built on the Chat Composer

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/ai-workspace
- Section: Blocks · Productivity
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/ai-workspace.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/ai-workspace`

### When to use

- The main screen of an AI assistant or copilot inside your product
- Internal tools where people chat with your data and group work into projects

### When not to use

- A small chat widget in a corner – use the Chat Composer on its own

### Usage

```tsx
import { AiWorkspace } from "@/components/ui/ai-workspace";

export function Assistant() {
  return (
    <AiWorkspace
      userName="Lena"
      respond={async (message, history) => {
        const res = await fetch("/api/chat", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ message, history }) });
        return (await res.json()).answer;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| respond | `(message, history) => Promise<string>` |  | Your model call – the answer streams in word by word. Demo answers without it |
| userName | `string` | `"Lena"` | Shown in the greeting and the sidebar |
| userAvatar | `string` |  | Image for the sidebar footer |
| workspace | `ReactNode` | `"N"` | Initial or logo in the top-left tile |
| pinned | `string[]` |  | Pinned assistants in the sidebar – pinned projects are added automatically |
| conversations | `Conversation[]` |  | Recent chats with their messages |
| projects | `Project[]` |  | Projects with name, description, days since update and pinned |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Send a message in the composer
- Escape: Close menus and the create-project dialog
- Tab: Move through sidebar, header, chat and projects

### Accessibility

- Menus are real menus with radio items, the dialog is modal and labelled, the collapsed sidebar is inert
- New answers are announced politely while they stream in

### Motion

- The sidebar collapses smoothly, answers stream in, views fade in, menus drop in
- Reduced motion turns these off

### Responsive

- Below 720px of width the sidebar becomes an overlay and the project grid turns into one column
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
- Chat Composer – installed automatically with the CLI

Related: chat-composer, thinking-state, comments-panel

```tsx
import { ClientContext } from "@/components/ui/client-context";

export function ClientPage() {
  return (
    <ClientContext
      me={{ name: "Lena Hart", avatar: "/avatars/lena.jpg" }}

      onCreateClient={(name) => api.createClient(name)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| context entries | `ContextEntry[]` |  | note ("@Report name" becomes a mention), report, files (type pdf · xlsx · csv · doc) or integration { app, connected } |
| me | `{ name, avatar? }` |  | Author of new context |
| onAddContext | `(clientId, text, files) => void` |  | Called when context is added |
| onCreateClient | `(name) => void` |  | Called when a client is created from the switcher |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ⌘ / Enter: Adds the context you typed
- @: Suggests the client's reports – Enter or Tab inserts the first
- Esc: Closes the switcher, the filter and the mention suggestions
- Tab: Moves through the switcher, tabs, search, filter and composer

### Accessibility

- Tabs are a tablist with a labelled panel; the client switcher, filter and mention suggestions are listboxes
- KPI cards and financial rows are toggle buttons; reports are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded
- Search, composer and attachment buttons are labelled; settings are switches

### Motion

- KPI cards rise in one after another and their sparklines draw in; new context slides in at the top
- The tab thumb glides with a little spring, reports fold open, menus pop from their button, sync icons spin while working
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Follows its own width: below 680px the KPIs wrap into two rows, the tabs stretch and search moves below them
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

## Invoice & Credit Note (Pro)

An invoice and its credit note stacked like paper – switch between them, pick lines to credit, adjust amounts and issue

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/invoice-credit
- Section: Blocks · Billing
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/invoice-credit.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/invoice-credit`

### When to use

- Billing portals and admin tools that show an invoice and let a team credit it
- Product pages for invoicing software – a document that looks real and can be tried

### When not to use

- Printing or PDF generation – render a dedicated print layout instead
- Invoices with dozens of lines – the credit tray is built for a handful

### Usage

```tsx
import { InvoiceCredit } from "@/components/ui/invoice-credit";

export function Billing() {
  return (
    <InvoiceCredit
      invoiceNo="INV-2041"
      creditNo="CN-0117"
      lines={[
        { id: "plan", name: "Growth plan", qty: 1, rate: 1250, tax: 0.2 },
        { id: "api", name: "API calls (per 1k)", qty: 18420, rate: 0.42, tax: 0.2, group: "Metered usage" },
      ]}
      onIssue={(credits, total) => api.issueCreditNote(credits, total)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| seller / buyer | `{ name, lines: string[] }` |  | From and To blocks on the invoice |
| invoiceNo / creditNo | `string` |  | Document numbers shown under Terms |
| invoiceDate / dueDate / period | `string` |  | Dates shown on both documents; an empty one leaves its line out |
| lines | `InvoiceLine[]` |  | Each { id, name, qty, rate, tax, group? } – lines with a group are listed under a heading. A negative rate is a discount; a rate that is not a number shows — and counts as 0 |
| currency | `string` | `"$"` | A symbol shown in front of amounts ("$", "£"), or an ISO code ("EUR", "JPY") formatted with Intl – the code is also shown after the applied total |
| onIssue | `(credits, total) => void` |  | Called when the credit note is issued, with the credited amount per line and the total incl. tax |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the switch, the actions, every line and amount
- Enter: Confirms an amount

### Accessibility

- The switch is a tablist; the sheet in the back is hidden from screen readers and can't be focused
- Credit lines are checkboxes with labels; amounts are labelled per line and stay within the line total

### Motion

- Switching slides the sheets: the chosen one comes forward, the other tucks behind it with only its top edge showing
- Checkmarks draw in; the segmented thumb glides between Invoice and Credit note
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Follows its own width: below 560px the parties stack, the rate and tax columns hide and the credit tray drops the total column
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## KPI Board (Pro)

The top of a dashboard – three trend cards, an overview chart that compares this period with the last, and a focus card; hover shows any day's value and every number rolls when the range changes

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/kpi-board
- Section: Blocks · Analytics
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/kpi-board.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/kpi-board`

### When to use

- The top of a dashboard: a few headline numbers with their trend, one chart that compares this period with the last, and one product or plan in focus
- Sales, growth and usage overviews of a SaaS or AI product, above a table or a list
- When the charts belong together – same range, same filter – and should react as one

### When not to use

- One metric in depth – use KPI Chart or Breakdown Chart
- Parts of a whole (shares, funnels, rankings) – the board only draws trends over time
- Reports that are printed or exported – this is built for pointing and switching

### Usage

```tsx
import { KpiBoard, type KpiBoardData } from "@/components/ui/kpi-board";

const ranges = [
  { id: "7d", label: "Last 7 days" },
  { id: "30d", label: "Last 30 days" },
];

export function Overview({ data }: { data: Record<string, KpiBoardData> }) {
  // data["30d"] = { stats, overview, focus }
  return <KpiBoard data={data} ranges={ranges} defaultRange="30d" compareLabel="vs. last month" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | `Record<string, KpiBoardData>` |  | One data set per range id: { stats, overview, focus } |
| ranges | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | Options of the date range picker |
| range | `string` |  | Controlled range id |
| defaultRange | `string` | `first range` | Starting range when uncontrolled |
| onRangeChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new range |
| segments | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | A filter inside the overview card, e.g. All items / Pro / Team – it only switches that card's lines; no filter when left out |
| segment | `string` |  | Controlled segment id |
| defaultSegment | `string` | `first segment` | Starting segment when uncontrolled |
| onSegmentChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new segment |
| compareLabel | `string` | `"vs. last period"` | Words after every change |
| currentLabel | `string` | `"This period"` | Name of the main line in the tooltip and the focus card |
| previousLabel | `string` | `"Last period"` | Name of the comparison line |
| formatMoney | `(value: number) => string` | `$1,234.00` | Formats money values |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Icon in the focus card |
| title | `string` |  | Heading on the left of the bar above the cards |
| setup | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | The small button at the top right of the focus card, e.g. Set up |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | The button at the bottom of the focus card |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the pickers and the action
- Enter / Space / ↓: On a picker: opens its menu
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: In an open menu: moves through the choices
- Enter: Picks the highlighted choice
- Esc: Closes the menu without changing anything

### Accessibility

- Every card is a labelled region with its numbers as text; the charts themselves are decorative
- The pickers are comboboxes with a listbox: the open state, the highlighted and the chosen option are announced
- Changes carry an arrow or a sign next to the color, and the color follows whether the change is good news (lowerIsBetter)

### Motion

- On first view the cards rise in one after another and every line draws itself in from the left
- Switching the range rolls every number in one shared tween while every line is drawn in again from the left
- The filter inside the overview does the same for that card only – the other cards stay still
- Hovering a small card marks the day under the pointer with a dot, its value in a tag and the date on the axis
- Hovering the overview shows a dark tooltip that compares this period with the last at that day
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- The date range sits above the cards on the right. Three small cards over a wide overview and the focus card; below 820px of container width the two lower cards take a full row each, below 600px everything stacks
- It follows its container, not the window
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Series may have different numbers of points per range (7 days, 30 days, 13 weeks) – each range is drawn in fresh
- A stat's value is the sum of its series; `previous` is the total of the period before and drives the change on the right
- Points that are not a number count as 0 and show as — on hover; a previous total of 0 leaves the change out instead of showing +0%
- focus.unitOne is the word after a count of exactly 1 – without it the unit loses its plural s ("1 license"), so only irregular words like person need it; long labels end in an ellipsis with the full text in a tooltip, numbers are never cut
- The date range sits in the bar above the cards because it changes all of them; the picker inside the overview is the segment and only switches the overview's own lines (overview.segments)

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: metrics-dashboard, kpi-chart, usage-meter

---

## Logo Marquee (Free)

The endless “Trusted by” strip – a seamless loop that eases to a stop on hover, scrubs with inertia and lifts the hovered logo to colour

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/logo-marquee
- Section: Blocks · Social proof
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/logo-marquee.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/logo-marquee`

### When to use

- A “Trusted by” or “Used by teams at” strip under a hero or above pricing
- Showing more customer, partner or integration logos than fit in one static row

### When not to use

- Three to five logos – a static, centred row reads calmer and needs no motion
- Logos people need to compare or click through – use a grid; a moving target is hard to hit

### Usage

```tsx
import { LogoMarquee } from "@/components/ui/logo-marquee";
import { VercelMark, LinearMark, StripeMark, FigmaMark, NotionMark, GitHubMark } from "./marks";

const logos = [
  { name: "Vercel", svg: <VercelMark />, scale: 0.86 },
  { name: "Linear", svg: <LinearMark />, color: "#5E6AD2" },
  { name: "Stripe", svg: <StripeMark />, color: "#635BFF", href: "/customers/stripe" },
  { name: "Figma", svg: <FigmaMark />, color: "#F24E1E" },
  { name: "Notion", svg: <NotionMark /> },
  { name: "GitHub", svg: <GitHubMark /> },
];

export function TrustedBy() {
  return (
    <section className="py-16">
      <p className="mb-6 text-center text-sm text-neutral-500">Trusted by teams at</p>
      <LogoMarquee logos={logos} rows={2} speed={36} labels="beside" />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| logos | `{ name, svg?, src?, color?, scale?, href? }[]` |  | The logos. svg is a ReactNode – use fill="currentColor" so it follows the muted colour; src takes an image instead. color is the brand colour it lifts to on hover, scale corrects optical size, href makes it a link |
| speed | `number` | `40` | Pixels per second – the same pace on any width |
| direction | `"left" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Which way the first row runs |
| rows | `1 \| 2` | `1` | Two rows split the logos alternately and run in opposite directions |
| gap | `number` | `56` | Space between logos in px; about 60 % of it on narrow containers |
| pauseOnHover | `boolean` | `true` | Ease to a stop while hovered or focused with the keyboard, and speed back up on leave |
| grayscale | `boolean` | `true` | Muted, colourless logos; the hovered one lifts to its brand colour. Off shows full colour and dims the others on hover |
| labels | `"none" \| "below" \| "beside"` | `"none"` | Show the brand name as a small caption under the mark, or beside it like a wordmark |
| label | `string` | `"Logos of companies using the product"` | Accessible name of the strip |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through linked logos; the strip stops and the focused logo is nudged into view

### Accessibility

- A labelled region; each name is read once – the repeated copies that make the loop are aria-hidden and inert
- Keyboard focus stops the strip so a logo never runs away from the focus ring
- Hover and focus stop it too, which covers the WCAG pause requirement for moving content
- Reduced motion shows every logo in a static, wrapping row
- A logo without svg or src, or whose image fails to load, shows a letter tile (or just its name when labels are on); an empty list renders nothing

### Motion

- The loop repeats a measured set and wraps by exactly its width – no gap, no jump
- One requestAnimationFrame loop eases a velocity per row: hover slows it to a stop, leaving winds it back up
- Drag or swipe to scrub; letting go flings it with inertia before it settles back into its own pace
- Only runs while on screen; edges fade out with a mask

### Responsive

- Container queries make logos and gaps smaller in narrow containers, down to 320px without page overflow
- Touch: horizontal swipes scrub the strip, vertical swipes still scroll the page
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: logo-cluster, text-reveal, gradient-text

---

## Metrics Dashboard (Pro)

Sales overview – KPI cards pick the metric, one chart switches between dotted line and bars, with top products and channels

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/metrics-dashboard
- Section: Blocks · Analytics
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/metrics-dashboard.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/metrics-dashboard`

### When to use

- A compact sales or business overview with a handful of headline metrics
- Dashboards where one chart, picked by KPI cards and shown as a line or as bars, says more than a grid of small charts

### When not to use

- Large data sets or drill-downs – the chart shows up to 30 points per period
- A single number – use a KPI card instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { MetricsDashboard } from "@/components/ui/metrics-dashboard";

export function Overview({ days, products, channels }) {
  return (
    <MetricsDashboard
      title="Sales"
      site="Northwind Store"
      data={days} // [{ date, revenue, orders, refunded }, …] oldest first
      products={products} // [{ name: "Linen overshirt", share: 0.22 }, …]
      channels={channels}
      currency="USD"
      defaultRange="30d"
      onExport={(range, metric) => console.log("export", range, metric)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` | `"Sales"` | Title in the bar on top |
| site | `string` | `"Northwind Store"` | Site or workspace shown under the title |
| defaultRange | `"7d" \| "30d" \| "90d"` | `"30d"` | Period to start on – shown as Week, Month and Quarter |
| defaultMetric | `"revenue" \| "orders" \| "aov" \| "refunds"` | `"revenue"` | Metric to start on |
| onExport | `(range, metric) => void` |  | Called when Export is pressed; the button confirms locally either way |
| data | `{ date: Date; revenue; orders; refunded }[]` | `sample data` | One entry per day, oldest first; 180 days give every range a previous period. Days missing a number count as 0; without a previous period the change chips stay empty |
| products | `{ name: string; share: number }[]` | `sample products` | Rows of Top products with their share of revenue (0–1); bars are relative to the largest share. An empty list shows a short note |
| channels | `{ name: string; share: number }[]` | `sample channels` | Rows of Channels, like products |
| currency | `string` | `"USD"` | ISO currency code for revenue, average order and the axis |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the period switch, Export, the KPI cards, the chart type, Compare and the chart
- ← / →: With the chart focused, moves the inspected point
- Home / End: Jumps to the first or last point

### Accessibility

- Period and chart-type buttons use aria-pressed; the KPI cards are tabs with aria-selected
- The chart has a text label with the range and values; the inspected point is announced through a status tooltip
- Deltas say up or down in text, not only with color – and a falling refund rate counts as good

### Motion

- KPI values and list counts count to their new amounts with tabular numerals
- The chosen KPI card turns fully opaque while the others dim; the line draws in with its dots popping on, bars grow up one after another
- With prefers-reduced-motion values and views switch instantly

### Responsive

- Follows the block's own width with container queries: below 640px the KPI cards form a 2 × 2 grid and the lists stack
- Below 460px the period switch fills the width, figures shrink and the chart is 168px tall
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

---

## Pricing Plans (Pro)

Pricing section with a monthly / yearly switch, three plan cards and collapsible details

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/pricing-plans

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/pricing-plans.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/pricing-plans`

### When to use

- A pricing page or section with up to three plans and a monthly / yearly choice
- Plans that differ in a few limits plus a longer list of features

### When not to use

- One-time purchases – drop the billing switch or use a simpler card
- More than three or four plans – use a comparison table instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { PricingPlans } from "@/components/ui/pricing-plans";

export function Pricing() {
  return <PricingPlans plans={plans} defaultBilling="yearly" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plans | `Plan[]` |  | Name, monthly and yearly price, limits, sync chip, features and an onSelect callback. One to three plans sit side by side, four two by two; a price that is not a number reads “Custom”; none shows a short empty note |
| title | `string` | `"Choose your plan"` | Section heading |
| subtitle | `string` |  | Line under the heading |
| defaultBilling | `"monthly" \| "yearly"` | `"yearly"` | Billing period shown first |
| currency | `string` | `"$"` | Symbol in front of the prices, or a three-letter code like "EUR" to format them as that currency (cents only when a price has them) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the section |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between the switch, the buttons and the detail toggles
- Enter / Space: Switch the billing period, start a plan or show / hide details

### Accessibility

- The billing switch is a radio group
- Details toggles use aria-expanded; hidden details are inert
- Features that are not included are announced as such

### Motion

- The switch thumb slides; prices roll digit by digit after a switch
- Details fold open and closed; reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Three columns on wide screens, one column below 860px
- Long plan names, badges, limit labels, sync chips and button labels stay on one line with an ellipsis and show in full on hover; feature labels wrap
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Task Board (Pro)

Kanban board with drag and drop, quick add, a detail panel, search, label filters and a compact view

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/task-board
- Section: Blocks · Productivity
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/task-board.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/task-board`

### When to use

- Sprint and project boards in a product, with tasks moving through a few statuses
- Internal tools where people sort work by dragging it

### When not to use

- Thousands of tasks – each column shows 50 cards and grows with Show more; beyond that, page and filter on the server
- Touch-first apps – native drag and drop needs a mouse; offer the detail panel's status buttons instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { TaskBoard } from "@/components/ui/task-board";

export function Sprint({ tasks }) {
  return (
    <TaskBoard
      tasks={tasks}
      statuses={statuses}
      labels={labels}
      people={people}
      path={["Northwind", "Launch", "Sprint 12"]}
      onChange={save}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `Task[]` |  | key, title, status, priority (0–4), estimate, labels, assignee, dueIn, subtasks, pullRequest, created |
| statuses | `TaskStatus[]` |  | Columns in order: id, label and icon |
| labels | `TaskLabel[]` |  | id, label and color – used on cards, in the filter and in the panel |
| people | `TaskPerson[]` |  | id, name and avatar for assignees |
| path | `string[]` |  | Breadcrumb above the board |
| onChange | `(tasks: Task[]) => void` |  | Called with all tasks after every move, edit, add or delete |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move through the toolbar, columns and cards
- Enter / Space: Open the focused card in the detail panel
- Escape: Close the detail panel or cancel a new task

### Accessibility

- Every card is focusable and opens a panel where status, priority, labels and assignee are plain toggle buttons – no dragging needed
- The star, compact view and filter are pressed or checked toggles; the breadcrumb marks the current page

### Motion

- Cards fade in, a blue line shows where a dragged card lands, the panel slides in from the right
- Reduced motion turns these off

### Responsive

- Columns keep a minimum width and the board scrolls sideways on narrow screens
- Long titles stop at three lines (full title in the panel); keys, labels, column names and the breadcrumb end in an ellipsis and show in full on hover; more than three labels fold into +N; column counts above 999 read 999+
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Testimonial Wall (Free)

The landing-page wall of quotes – columns that scroll endlessly in opposite directions, ease to a stop on hover and scrub with inertia

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/testimonial-wall
- Section: Blocks · Social proof
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/testimonial-wall.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/testimonial-wall`

### When to use

- A “Loved by” section on a landing or pricing page with eight or more quotes
- Social proof that should feel alive without asking for attention – it runs slowly and stops the moment someone reads

### When not to use

- Two or three quotes – show them side by side; a loop of three repeats too obviously
- A single hero quote or a case study – it deserves a static, larger layout
- Reviews people need to search or filter – use a list or grid

### Usage

```tsx
import { TestimonialWall } from "@/components/ui/testimonial-wall";

const items = [
  {
    quote: "We replaced three half-finished internal kits with it in a sprint.",
    name: "Lena Hartmann",
    role: "Design Lead",
    company: "Fieldnote",
    avatar: "/avatars/lena.jpg",
    rating: 5,
  },
  {
    quote: "The motion is the part nobody notices – which is exactly the point.",
    name: "Jonas Weber",
    role: "Staff Engineer",
    company: "Ledgerline",
    verified: true,
  },
  // … at least two quotes per column, ideally four or more
];

export function Testimonials() {
  return (
    <section className="py-24">
      <p className="text-center text-sm text-neutral-500">Testimonials</p>
      <h2 className="mb-10 text-center text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight">Loved by product teams</h2>
      <TestimonialWall items={items} speed={26} className="[--ui-tw-height:640px]" />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `{ quote, name, role?, company?, avatar?, rating?, verified? }[]` |  | The quotes. avatar is a photo URL – without one, or when it fails to load, the initials sit on a soft gray circle. rating (1–5) adds a small gray star row, verified a gray check beside the name. Quotes keep their line breaks and stop at ten lines; role and company wrap once, then end in an ellipsis. Fewer quotes than columns use fewer columns; none shows a short empty note |
| columns | `1 \| 2 \| 3` | `3` | Most columns on a wide container; the wall itself drops to 2 below 740px and 1 below 480px of its own width |
| speed | `number` | `28` | Pixels per second of the first column; the others run about 15 % slower and faster, in alternating directions |
| pauseOnHover | `boolean` | `true` | Ease the hovered column to a stop and wind it back up on leave. Keyboard focus always stops its column |
| label | `string` | `"What customers say"` | Accessible name of the wall |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper. Set the height with --ui-tw-height (600px by default) and the edge fade with --ui-tw-fade (96px) |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the quotes; the focused card's column stops and the card is nudged into view
- Shift / Tab: Moves back; leaving the wall lets the columns run again

### Accessibility

- A labelled region; every quote is a figure with a blockquote and a figcaption, read out once – the copies that make the loop are aria-hidden and inert
- Keyboard focus stops the column, so a card never runs away from the focus ring
- Hover, focus and press-and-hold all stop the motion, which covers the WCAG pause requirement for moving content
- Star ratings are an image with a text label (“Rated 5 out of 5”), the check is labelled “Verified customer”
- Reduced motion shows every quote once in a static masonry grid

### Motion

- Each column repeats a measured set and wraps by exactly its height – no gap, no jump
- Columns alternate up and down at slightly different speeds and start at different points, so rows never line up
- One requestAnimationFrame loop eases a velocity per column: hover slows it to a stop over about a third of a second, leaving winds it back up
- Drag a column with the mouse to scrub it; letting go flings it with inertia before it settles back into its own pace
- The hovered card lifts 3px with a soft shadow while the rest of the wall dims a little
- Only runs while on screen; top and bottom edges fade out with a mask

### Responsive

- Columns follow the wall's own width (3 / 2 / 1), so it works in a sidebar as well as full width
- One column on phones with 15px quotes; names win over role and company when space is tight – down to 320px without overflow
- Touch: vertical swipes keep scrolling the page (no scroll trap); pressing and holding a column pauses it to read
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: logo-marquee, tilt-card, text-reveal

## Agent Team (Free)

A prompt types itself and branches out into three agents, each with a role and overlapping tool logos

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/agent-team
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-team.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-team`

### When to use

- AI and automation products where one prompt sets up several agents or roles
- Feature cards about teams, delegation or workflows that span several tools

### When not to use

- Real org charts or live agent status – the scene is decorative and loops on its own
- More than three agents – the layout is built for exactly three

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentTeam } from "@/components/ui/agent-team";

export function FeatureCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 560 }}>
      <AgentTeam
        prompt="Build a team to work my inbound pipeline"
        members={[
          { role: "Lead Researcher", avatar: "/team/lena.jpg", tools: ["linkedin", "hubspot"] },
          { role: "Inbound Qualifier", avatar: "/team/theo.jpg", tools: ["hubspot", "slack"] },
          { role: "Outbound SDR", avatar: "/team/noah.jpg", tools: ["gmail", "salesforce"] },
        ]}
      />
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prompt | `string` | `"Build a team to work my inbound pipeline"` | Text that types itself into the prompt pill |
| members | `[AgentTeamMember, AgentTeamMember, AgentTeamMember]` |  | Required. Three agents, left to right – { role, avatar, tools? } with up to two of linkedin, hubspot, slack, gmail, salesforce |
| label | `string` |  | Accessible description – by default built from the prompt and the roles |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a label built from the prompt and the roles; everything inside is hidden from screen readers
- Nothing in the scene is interactive

### Motion

- The prompt types itself, the send button presses and a soft pink-to-violet glow blooms behind it, dashed lines draw down and the three agents pop in one after another – then it starts over
- Each status dot pops in last; the tool circles overlap slightly
- With prefers-reduced-motion it shows the finished team and stays still

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – text and shapes are sized in container units
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Cover Flow (Free)

Browse covers in 3D – drag, flick or scrub the row, it springs to the nearest cover; images drift in their frames over a soft reflection

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/cover-flow
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/cover-flow.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/cover-flow`

### When to use

- Six to twenty visual items where looking at one at a time is the point – albums, places, products, case studies, templates
- A showcase row that should feel physical: drag, flick, sideways trackpad scroll

### When not to use

- Text-heavy slides or many items to compare side by side – use a plain carousel or a grid
- Large libraries – a grid with a lightbox scales better

### Usage

```tsx
import { CoverFlow } from "@/components/ui/cover-flow";

export function Albums() {
  return (
    <CoverFlow
      aria-label="New releases"
      items={[
        { id: 1, title: "Low Tide", subtitle: "Mara Lind", image: "/covers/low-tide.jpg" },
        { id: 2, title: "Night Drive", subtitle: "Okto", image: "/covers/night-drive.jpg" },
        { id: 3, title: "Paper Moon", subtitle: "Ilse & June", image: "/covers/paper-moon.jpg" },
      ]}
      onSelect={(item) => openAlbum(item.id)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `CoverFlowItem[]` |  | { id, title?, subtitle?, image?, alt?, cover? } – pass an image URL or any ReactNode as cover |
| index | `number` |  | Controlled front cover – pair with onIndexChange |
| defaultIndex | `number` | `middle cover` | Starting cover when uncontrolled |
| onIndexChange | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called whenever a different cover reaches the front, also while dragging |
| onSelect | `(item, index) => void` |  | Clicking the front cover or pressing Enter – e.g. open a detail view |
| itemWidth | `number` | `280` | Cover width in px – the whole row scales down in narrow containers (to half at most) |
| itemHeight | `number` | `280` | Cover height in px |
| angle | `number` | `50` | How far the side covers turn away, in degrees |
| reflection | `boolean` | `true` | Mirror the covers on the floor |
| caption | `boolean` | `true` | Title and subtitle of the front cover |
| renderCaption | `(item, index) => ReactNode` |  | Replaces the default caption |
| controls | `boolean` | `true` | Previous and next buttons beside the caption |
| ticks | `boolean` | `true` | Small position ticks under the caption – clicking one jumps there |
| sound | `boolean` | `false` | A soft click each time a new cover reaches the front (Web Audio, no file) |
| aria-label | `string` | `"Cover flow"` | Names the carousel |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: Previous or next cover while the row has focus
- Home / End: First or last cover
- ↵: Selects the front cover (calls onSelect)

### Accessibility

- A region with aria-roledescription="carousel"; each cover is a group with aria-roledescription="slide" and a label like "3 of 10: Alpenglow"
- Covers away from the front are aria-hidden; the reflections are aria-hidden and inert
- The caption is a polite live region, so the new front cover is announced
- Previous / next are real buttons; the ticks are labelled "Show <title>" with aria-current and stay out of the tab order

### Motion

- A spring carries the row: drag 1:1, flick and it travels with your speed, then lands on a cover – a quick flick always moves at least one
- Sideways trackpad scrolling scrubs the row and settles in the direction of the swipe; vertical scrolling stays with the page
- Covers turn, recede, scale down and dim with distance; a light sheen sits on the side facing the center and each image drifts inside its frame
- The ends rubber-band; the caption rises in from the direction of travel
- With prefers-reduced-motion covers jump into place and the drift is off

### Responsive

- Scales with its container down to half size; touch-action pan-y keeps vertical swipes scrolling the page
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: tilt-card, logo-marquee, segmented-control

## DACH Region (Free)

DACH map with fading neighbours and a pastel band along the border, switchable to the US, China, India, Brazil or Japan

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/region-dach
- Section: Illustrations · Maps
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/region-dach.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/region-dach`

### When to use

- Showing a service area, sales territory or market focus in Germany, Austria and Switzerland
- Sections about regional exclusivity or local presence in one of the larger markets (US, China, India, Brazil, Japan), next to a short text

### When not to use

- Maps that need cities, regions or exact borders – the shapes are simplified and there are no labels

### Usage

```tsx
import { RegionDach } from "@/components/ui/region-dach";

export function TerritorySection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 420 }}>
      <RegionDach />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| region | `"dach" \| "us" \| "cn" \| "in" \| "br" \| "jp"` |  | Shown region (controlled). Pair it with onRegionChange to keep the menu working |
| defaultRegion | `Region` | `"dach"` | Region shown first when region is not set |
| onRegionChange | `(region: Region) => void` |  | Called when the viewer picks a region in the menu |
| showSwitcher | `boolean` | `true` | Show the region menu in the top-left corner |
| label | `string \| ((region: Region) => string)` | `"Map of the DACH region: Germany, Austria and Switzerland" / "Map of Japan" …` | Accessible description of the map; by default it follows the current region |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the menu button: open the region list. In the list: pick the highlighted region
- ArrowDown / ArrowUp: On the menu button: open the list. In the list: move through the regions
- Home / End: Jump to the first or last region
- Escape: Close the list and return focus to the menu button
- Tab: Close the list and move on

### Accessibility

- The map is one image whose label names the current region; the shapes inside are hidden from screen readers
- The menu button reports the current region and its expanded state; the list is a listbox with options, the selected one marked with aria-selected

### Motion

- A soft pastel band travels along the outer border in a continuous 14-second loop: a blurred glow that only spreads outwards, with three sharp layers on top
- Switching regions fades and slightly grows the old map away while the new one settles in from slightly smaller; the band starts anew
- The menu morphs open out of its button, and the hover fill glides between rows
- With prefers-reduced-motion the band stays still, regions swap instantly and the menu opens without the morph

### Responsive

- Transparent background; the neighbouring countries fade out towards the edges, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 540 : 440 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – set a width or max-width via className
- The menu scales down with the illustration (to about 60 %) so it still fits in small previews
- The file embeds the map data for all six regions (about 155 KB)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

export function FeatureCard() {

### Accessibility

### Motion

- The placeholder lines shimmer softly and the colored glow under the front card breathes
- Hover the front card to lift and tilt it; hover a back card to slide it further out
- With prefers-reduced-motion the shimmer and glow stop and hover changes happen instantly

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – set a width or max-width via className
- Drawn on a 320 × 240 viewBox, so text and cards scale crisply at any size
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
