## Frost Cloud (Free)

A frosted white cloud with eyes cut out of it, on a red-orange or blue sky – it floats, turns to look around, blinks, follows the pointer and bounces with a wink when clicked

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/frost-cloud
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/frost-cloud.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/frost-cloud`

### When to use

- A friendly face for an assistant, an AI feature or a cloud product – as an app icon, an empty state or a feature card
- Landing pages that want a calm, living mascot instead of a static logo

### When not to use

- Tiny sizes below ~48px – the glow and the eyes get lost
- Brands far from blue or orange – the colors are part of the look

### Usage

```tsx
import { FrostCloud } from "@/components/ui/frost-cloud";

export function AssistantCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 320 }}>
      <FrostCloud color="blue" />
      <h3>Meet your assistant</h3>
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| color | `"blue" \| "orange"` | `"orange"` | Blue-to-cyan or red-to-orange sky; the cloud's colors follow |
| background | `boolean` | `true` | Fill the whole box with the sky gradient; false leaves the cloud on a transparent background with a soft colored edge |
| followPointer | `boolean` | `true` | The eyes follow the pointer while it's over the illustration |
| label | `string` |  | Accessible description of the illustration |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label
- Clicking only plays an animation – nothing else happens

### Motion

- Frosted white and a little see-through, the sky shining through softly towards the bottom, eyes cut out of it
- The cloud floats and breathes; its shadow shrinks and fades as it rises
- Every few seconds it glances left, right, up or down: the body tilts a little, the eyes move further and the shine slides the other way, so it seems to turn
- It blinks at random moments, sometimes twice
- The eyes follow the pointer; a click gives a squishy bounce and a wink
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion it keeps still and only reacts to clicks

### Responsive

- Square by default; give it a height and the sky fills the whole box while the cloud stays centered, up to 320px wide
- Light and dark mode via a .dark class or data-theme="dark": a deeper sky in dark mode

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: glow-cloud, model-wheel

---

## Ghosted Chat (Free)

Unanswered chat messages marked as read, with a thumbs-down reply on hover

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/ghosted-chat
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/ghosted-chat.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/ghosted-chat`

### When to use

- A problem card about cold outreach that gets ignored or messages left on read
- Bento grids and feature cards that need a small illustration above the text

### When not to use

- A real chat UI – the bubbles are a fixed, decorative scene
- Very small sizes below ~220px wide, where the bubble text gets hard to read

### Usage

```tsx
import { GhostedChat } from "@/components/ui/ghosted-chat";

export function FeatureCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <GhostedChat />
      <h3>Card title</h3>
      <p>Short description of the problem or step.</p>
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` | `"A chat with three unanswered messages…"` | Accessible description of the illustration |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the messages inside are hidden from screen readers
- The hover reply is purely decorative, nothing needs to be reached with the keyboard

### Motion

- A red shine sweeps through the last message every few seconds; the last bubble has a soft colored glow
- On hover the status texts fade out, the messages move up and a blue thumbs-down reply pops in with a small bounce
- With prefers-reduced-motion the shine stops and hover changes happen instantly

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Laid out on a fixed 360 × 240 artboard and scaled to the width of its container with a ResizeObserver, so the bubbles never reflow
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

## Glow Keyboard (Pro)

AI chat input that types itself over a glass keyboard – every key press sends a wave up the gradient floor

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/glow-keyboard
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/glow-keyboard.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/glow-keyboard`

### When to use

- Hero sections for AI assistants, chat or writing tools – the prompt types itself and invites people to try
- Landing pages that want an interactive scene instead of a video

### When not to use

- As your real chat input – it is a showcase; use Chat Composer for a working input
- Small cards on mobile – the keyboard legends get tiny below ~360px width

### Usage

```tsx
import { GlowKeyboard } from "@/components/ui/glow-keyboard";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 1100, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <GlowKeyboard />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prompts | `string[]` | `three hiking prompts` | Prompts the demo types one after another; each one is sent with Enter |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Ask AI anything..."` | Placeholder of the chat input |
| onSubmit | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called when a prompt is sent with Enter – by the demo or the user |
| label | `string` | `"AI chat input above a glass keyboard…"` | Accessible name of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Click: Anywhere on the scene puts the cursor into the input and stops the demo
- Any key: Types and lights up the same key on the drawn keyboard
- Enter: Sends the prompt and clears the input

### Accessibility

- The input is a real text field with a label; the drawn keyboard and the floor are hidden from screen readers
- The demo stops as soon as the input gets focus, so it never types over the user

### Motion

- The demo types each prompt with an uneven, human rhythm, holds Shift for capitals and corrects one typo
- Every key press: the key sinks in, a wave rises out of the gradient below it and the input glow flashes at the same spot
- The floor's two layers – colour and white plus-lighter – drift and morph slowly
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion the scene stays still and the demo does not type, typing yourself still works

### Responsive

- Keeps an 11 : 6 frame and scales to the width of its container – every detail is sized in container units
- Set the background with --ui-gk-bg (default #fafafa, #111113 in dark mode)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: gradient-floor, chat-composer

---

## Integration Beam (Free)

Your product between the tools it connects – light pulses flow along curved beams, hover to focus a tool, click to pause it

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/integration-beam
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-beam.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-beam`

### When to use

- A hero or integrations section that shows your product sitting between the tools a team already uses
- Landing pages where a calm, self-playing data flow explains “we connect to X and Y” faster than a logo wall

### When not to use

- A real integration settings page – pausing a tool here is only part of the scene, nothing is saved
- More than four tools per side – the beams get crowded; use Integration Grid or Logo Cluster for long lists

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationBeam } from "@/components/ui/integration-beam";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <IntegrationBeam />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| left | `{ name: string; logo: ReactNode }[]` | `Slack, Notion, Gmail` | Tools that send data in – on the left, or above the hub on narrow widths. The logo fills a 28 × 28 box |
| right | `{ name: string; logo: ReactNode }[]` | `HubSpot, Linear, Google Drive` | Tools that receive data – on the right, or below the hub on narrow widths |
| center | `{ name: string; logo?: ReactNode }` | `{ name: "Acme" }` | Your product. The logo is drawn white into a 36 × 36 box on the dark tile (currentColor); a neutral flower mark when left out |
| label | `string` | `"Acme connected to Slack, Notion, …"` | Accessible name of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between the tool tiles; the focused tool's beam comes forward and its name shows
- Enter / Space: Pauses or reconnects the focused tool

### Accessibility

- The scene is a labelled group; every tool is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a name like “Slack, connected”
- Pausing or reconnecting is announced in a polite live region, with the new count (“5 of 6 connected”)
- The beams, pulses and logos are decorative and hidden from screen readers
- Visible focus ring on the tiles; the tooltip also shows on keyboard focus

### Motion

- Sync cycles: pulses leave the left tools 280 ms apart, travel 1.5 s along their beam and, as they land, the hub glows and the next wave leaves for the right tools
- Each pulse is a short gradient – clear tail, accent body, pale tip – with a soft blurred glow; one accent color only
- The status chip under the hub slides between “Syncing…” and “6 connected”, and its width glides with the text
- When the layout switches between side by side and stacked, the tiles glide to their new spots and the curves morph with them (460 ms)
- The loop only runs while the scene is on screen (IntersectionObserver)
- With prefers-reduced-motion the beams are drawn as static lines – no pulses, no glides; hover, focus and pausing still work

### Responsive

- The beams are measured from the real tile positions (ResizeObserver), so the scene reflows with its container
- Below 460px of container width the senders stack above the hub and the receivers below, with vertical beams; fits 320px screens
- On touch screens a tap pauses a tool and shows its name for a moment instead of a hover tooltip
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: integration-grid, integration-flow, logo-cluster, agent-team

---

## Integration Flow (Pro)

Integration pills rotating along a dashed arc, each beaming its data into a central analysis hub

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/integration-flow
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-flow.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-flow`

### When to use

- A hero or feature section that shows your product pulling data in from the tools teams already use
- Integration or data-platform pages where a short, self-playing loop explains the idea better than a logo wall

### When not to use

- A real list of connected integrations – the pills are decorative, not interactive
- Very small spaces below ~320px wide, where the pill text gets hard to read
- Brands that clash with the warm coral background

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationFlow } from "@/components/ui/integration-flow";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 1100, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <IntegrationFlow />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `{ name: string; icon: ReactNode; title?: string; mono?: boolean }[]` | `Okta, Snowflake, Slack, ClickUp, Zendesk` | Integrations that rotate through the pills (5 or more look best). The icon fills a 64 × 64 box; mono logos turn black in the centre |
| label | `string` | `"Integrations like Slack, Okta and Snowflake…"` | Accessible description of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- The scene is exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the pills and cards inside are hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The pills travel along the dashed arc one slot at a time (0.9 s); the one landing in the centre turns light and shows its logo in color
- The centre pill charges up, a beam sweeps over to the Data Analysis hub (1.1 s) and the hub lights up as it arrives
- The coral background blobs drift and breathe slowly on a 16 s loop
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything stands still in the centre state, with the beam drawn in

### Responsive

- Drawn on a 2400 × 1490 stage and scaled to the width of its container, so the layout never reflows
- Keeps its 2400 : 1490 aspect ratio; set a width or max-width via className
- Set --ui-if-bg and --ui-if-fade to change the stage background and the color the bottom fades into
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Integration Grid (Free)

Honeycomb-like wall of integration logos around a bright centre tile with your product mark, fading out toward the edges

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/integration-grid
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-grid.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-grid`

### When to use

- Integration sections and feature cards like “Works with the tools you already use”
- Landing pages that show your product at the centre of an ecosystem

### When not to use

- A real, clickable list of integrations – the tiles are decorative and not links
- More than 22 logos – the grid has 22 outer tiles, extra logos are left out

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationGrid } from "@/components/ui/integration-grid";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 760 }}>
      <IntegrationGrid mark={<img src="/logo.svg" alt="" width={40} height={40} />} />
      <h3>Plays well with your stack</h3>
      <p>Connect the tools your team already relies on.</p>
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| logos | `IntegrationGridLogo[]` | `22 well-known tools` | Logos filled row by row around the centre – each { name, path, color?, darkColor? } with a single 24 × 24 SVG path (e.g. from simple-icons); without color the mark follows the ink color |
| mark | `ReactNode` | `a neutral flower mark` | Content of the larger centre tile – usually your product logo |
| columns | `5 \| 7 \| 9` | `9` | Tiles in the middle row – the rows above and below get two fewer. Fewer columns make the tiles larger |
| label | `string` |  | Accessible description – by default lists the integrations |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image whose label lists every integration; tiles and logos are hidden from screen readers
- Nothing in the scene is interactive

### Motion

- Still by default; on hover a tile turns fully white and its logo grows a little from the centre
- With prefers-reduced-motion the hover lift is switched off

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 1520 : 560 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – every size is in container units
- Tile fills fade toward the edges while the logos keep their full brand colors
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

- Import: `@/components/ui/layer-stack`

### When to use

- Explaining a layered product or platform – each entry is one layer of the stack
- Feature sections that walk through capabilities one by one, with a visual that follows along

### When not to use

- Navigation that changes page content – this is an illustration with its own small state

### Usage

```tsx
import { LayerStack } from "@/components/ui/layer-stack";

export function PlatformSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <LayerStack
        items={[
          { title: "Triggered by events", hint: "Webhooks", icon: "bolt" },
          { title: "Grounded in your data", hint: "Context", icon: "database" },
          { title: "Connected to your apps", hint: "APIs", icon: "plug" },
          { title: "Works with any model", hint: "Routing", icon: "spark" },
          { title: "Traced at every step", hint: "Logs", icon: "pulse" },
        ]}
      />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `LayerStackItem[]` | `five sample layers` | Up to five entries, top layer first – { title, hint?, icon? } with icon one of bolt, database, plug, spark, pulse |
| defaultIndex | `number` | `0` | Entry to start on |
| interval | `number` | `2600` | Time per entry while it plays on its own, in ms |
| onChange | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called when the user picks an entry |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves focus to the chosen entry
- ↑ / ↓: Picks the previous or next entry

### Accessibility

- The list is a vertical tablist with real buttons; the chosen entry has aria-selected
- The stack itself is decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The chosen layer and the ones above it glide up to open a gap; its face, edge and icon turn blue and a soft glow fades in beneath it
- A white card glides behind the chosen entry in the list
- Steps through the entries on its own and pauses while hovered or focused; after a click or key press it stays put
- With prefers-reduced-motion it doesn't play on its own and changes happen instantly

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – text and layers are sized in container units
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Your mark on a white disc in the middle – company logos bounce out of it and settle around it

- Import: `@/components/ui/logo-cluster`

### When to use

- Integration or ecosystem sections – "works with the tools you already use"
- Feature cards that need a lively, friendly picture around your own brand

### When not to use

- Listing your real integrations – the logos are examples
- Places where people need to read or click the logos

### Usage

```tsx
import { LogoCluster } from "@/components/ui/logo-cluster";

export function IntegrationsCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <LogoCluster />
      <h3>Connects with everything</h3>
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` | `"The affectUI mark surrounded by…"` | Accessible description of the illustration |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the bubbles are hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- When the cluster comes into view the middle circle appears, then the logos quickly bounce out of it one after another
- Once they land, the ring turns slowly clockwise while every logo stays upright – paused while off screen
- Hovering a bubble grows it slightly with a springy ease and a softer shadow
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything is in place right away

### Responsive

- Square, scales with the width of its container (max 420px) – every size is in container units
- Light and dark mode via a .dark class or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Swap the mark in the middle for your own logo: replace the MARK path and its viewBox
- Company logos belong to their owners – check you may show them before you ship

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: integration-grid, model-wheel

## Model Wheel (Free)

AI model names on a turning drum – the rows bend away at the edges and each model lands on a soft gray fill

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/model-wheel
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/model-wheel.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/model-wheel`

### When to use

- Feature cards about model choice, routing or "bring your own model"
- Landing pages that list supported AI providers in a calm, moving way

### When not to use

- A real model picker – the wheel can be spun, but it doesn't report a choice
- Long lists – the drum shows about seven rows at a time

### Usage

```tsx
import { ModelWheel } from "@/components/ui/model-wheel";

export function FeatureCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <ModelWheel />
      <h3>Every model, one workspace</h3>
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| models | `{ name, viewBox, color, d }[]` | `8 popular models` | Models on the wheel, each with its brand mark as one SVG path; use at least 7 to keep the drum full |
| hold | `number` | `1500` | Milliseconds a model stays in the middle |
| label | `string` | `"AI models on a turning wheel…"` | Accessible description of the illustration |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the rows are hidden from screen readers
- Hovering holds the wheel, so nothing moves while someone reads it
- Spinning by hand also works with touch; the automatic turn starts again after a short pause

### Motion

- The rows sit on a cylinder: towards the top and bottom they tilt away, shrink and fade
- Every turn runs on a soft spring: the drum gathers speed, overshoots a touch and locks onto the next model like a magnet
- Grab the wheel and drag it up or down to spin it; a quick flick keeps it turning, then it snaps onto the closest model
- The wheel turns downwards; the model in the middle sits on a gray fill that grows or shrinks to its name
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion it doesn't turn by itself, but can still be spun by hand

### Responsive

- Fixed height of seven rows; the width follows its container
- Light and dark mode via a .dark class or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Brand marks belong to their owners – check you may show them before you ship

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: glow-keyboard, chat-composer

## Tab Overload (Free)

Overlapping browser windows where the highlight follows the hovered tab

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/tab-overload
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/tab-overload.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/tab-overload`

### When to use

- A problem card about context switching, research in too many tabs or manual busywork
- Bento grids and feature cards that need a small illustration above the text

### When not to use

- Showing real browser content – the windows only contain placeholder blocks
- Places where the right and bottom edge must stay sharp – the scene fades out there by design

### Usage

```tsx
import { TabOverload } from "@/components/ui/tab-overload";

export function FeatureCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <TabOverload />
      <h3>Card title</h3>
      <p>Short description of the problem or step.</p>
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` | `"Three overlapping browser windows…"` | Accessible description of the illustration |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the windows inside are hidden from screen readers
- The hover highlight is purely decorative, nothing needs to be reached with the keyboard

### Motion

- The placeholder blocks shimmer softly
- The front window is highlighted with colored dots, an outline and a glow; hover a window behind it and the highlight moves over
- With prefers-reduced-motion the shimmer stops and the highlight switches instantly

### Responsive

- Transparent background; the whole scene fades out towards the right and bottom edge with a CSS mask, so it blends into any surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – set a width or max-width via className
- The hover swap uses the CSS :has() selector; in browsers without it the front window simply stays highlighted
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Connected teammates – a cursor drags a new one into the empty slot, the line turns solid and they go online

### When to use

- Feature cards about inviting teammates, collaboration, sharing or multiplayer
- Onboarding steps like “Invite your team” where a friendly, moving scene helps

### When not to use

- Places that need to stay completely still – use prefers-reduced-motion or a static image

### Usage

```tsx
import { TeamInvite } from "@/components/ui/team-invite";

export function FeatureCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 420 }}>
      <TeamInvite
        avatars={[
          { src: "/team/maya.png", name: "Maya" },

    </article>

```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |

| label | `string` |  | Accessible description – by default built from the names |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label built from the names; avatars, lines and cursor are hidden from screen readers
- Nothing in the scene is interactive

### Motion

- A 4.4 s loop with soft ease-in-out: the cursor picks up the third avatar, carries it into the dashed slot, the line draws solid and the green status dot pops in
- Only transforms, opacity and a stroke offset are animated – no layout work
- With prefers-reduced-motion it stays a still frame of the waiting state

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – every size is in container units
- Avatars are square portraits shown in white-ringed circles; photos, 3D faces or illustrations all work
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

- React 19

## Voice Orb (Pro)

The face of a voice assistant – a sphere of dots that breathes, catches sound, collapses into a spinning ring while thinking and ripples when it speaks

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/voice-orb
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/voice-orb.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/voice-orb`

### When to use

- Voice mode of an assistant: one calm object that shows whether the AI listens, thinks or talks
- Hero of an AI product page, an empty state before the first prompt, or a call screen
- Anywhere a spinner would undersell what is happening – the orb says which phase it is

### When not to use

- Inline in a chat thread or next to text – use Thinking Loader or Thinking State, they are made for small sizes
- As decoration that never changes state – a still image costs nothing; the orb draws every frame
- Below about 96px – the dots merge into a blob

### Usage

```tsx
import { VoiceOrb } from "@/components/ui/voice-orb";

export function VoiceMode() {
  const { state, level, toggle } = useVoiceSession(); // "idle" | "listening" | "thinking" | "speaking", 0–1
  return <VoiceOrb state={state} level={level} onPress={toggle} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| state | `"idle" \| "listening" \| "thinking" \| "speaking"` | `"idle"` | What the assistant is doing – the orb melts from one state into the next |
| level | `number` |  | Loudness from 0 to 1 while listening or speaking. Without it the orb makes up a natural-looking level |
| size | `number` | `220` | Edge length in px |
| dots | `number` | `520` | Number of dots – raise it for large sizes |
| accent | `string` | `blue` | Color the moving dots take on; resting dots use the text color |
| label | `boolean \| Partial<Record<state, string>>` | `true` | The line under the orb – false hides it, an object replaces single texts |
| interactive | `boolean` | `true` | Dots give way to the mouse pointer |
| onPress | `() => void` |  | Makes the orb a button, e.g. to start and stop listening |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| style | `CSSProperties` |  | Inline styles on the root – set color here to change the resting dots |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: With onPress: presses the orb

### Accessibility

- The canvas is decorative; the state is in the label, which is announced politely when it changes
- With onPress the orb is a real button named by its label; without it, an image named after the state
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing moves: the orb shows one still frame per state (sphere, raised dots, ring, waves)
- The colors follow the text color and adapt to dark mode on their own

### Motion

- Idle: the sphere turns slowly and breathes
- Listening: dots jump outward with the level and take on the accent color; a soft glow follows the loudness
- Thinking: the sphere collapses into a tilted, fast spinning ring with a light running around it
- Speaking: waves travel from pole to pole with the level
- States are blended, never switched – every dot glides from one shape to the next in about a third of a second
- The animation pauses while the orb is off screen or the tab is in the background

### Responsive

- Fixed square of size px – pass a smaller size on phones; it is sharp on high-density screens
- Touch screens: no pointer effect, the press works as usual
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Changing state or level never restarts the animation – only size and dots rebuild the canvas
- Smooth a raw microphone level a little before passing it, or pass it as is: the orb eases towards it anyway

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: thinking-loader, thinking-state, chat-composer

---

## World Map Continental (Pro)

World map with one highlighted continent and a pastel band along its coastline, switchable between all six

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/world-map
- Section: Illustrations · Maps
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/world-map.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/world-map`

### When to use

- Showing that you serve, operate in or focus on one continent
- Market, coverage or expansion sections on a landing page, where a calm map says more than a list of countries

### When not to use

- Data maps with values per country – this is a decorative illustration, not a chart
- Showing individual countries – each continent is one merged shape without borders, simplified from Natural Earth 1:110m

### Usage

```tsx
import { WorldMap } from "@/components/ui/world-map";

export function MarketSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <WorldMap />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| continent | `"north-america" \| "south-america" \| "europe" \| "africa" \| "asia" \| "oceania"` |  | Highlighted continent (controlled). Pair it with onContinentChange to keep the menu working |
| defaultContinent | `Continent` | `"europe"` | Continent highlighted first when continent is not set |
| onContinentChange | `(continent: Continent) => void` |  | Called when the viewer picks a continent in the menu |
| showSwitcher | `boolean` | `true` | Show the continent menu in the top-left corner |
| label | `string \| ((continent: Continent) => string)` | `"World map with Europe highlighted" …` | Accessible description of the map; by default it follows the current continent |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the menu button: open the continent list. In the list: pick the highlighted continent
- ArrowDown / ArrowUp: On the menu button: open the list. In the list: move through the continents
- Home / End: Jump to the first or last continent
- Escape: Close the list and return focus to the menu button
- Tab: Close the list and move on

### Accessibility

- The map is one image whose label names the highlighted continent; the shapes inside are hidden from screen readers
- The menu button reports the current continent and its expanded state; the list is a listbox with options, the selected one marked with aria-selected

### Motion

- A soft pastel band travels along the coastline of the continent's main landmass in a continuous 14-second loop: a blurred glow that only spreads outwards, with three sharp layers on top – the same band as in the DACH Region map
- Switching continents fades the old highlight back into the gray world while the new one settles in from slightly smaller with its shadow; the band starts anew
- The menu morphs open out of its button, and the hover fill glides between rows
- With prefers-reduced-motion the band stays still, continents swap instantly and the menu opens without the morph

### Responsive

- Transparent background; the solid gray world and the lighter highlighted continent read on light and dark surfaces alike
- Keeps a 540 : 242 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – set a width or max-width via className
- The menu scales down with the illustration (to about 60 %); on small sizes the open list may extend below the map
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Blur Crossfade (Pro)

Swaps content with a soft blur while the box glides smoothly to the size of what comes next

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/blur-crossfade
- Section: Motion · Transitions
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/blur-crossfade.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/blur-crossfade`

### When to use

- Button labels and status text that change in place – Save → Saving… → Saved
- Panels, tips or steps that swap content of different lengths without a jump in the layout

### When not to use

- Navigating between pages or large views – use a route transition instead
- Content that updates many times per second, like counters or live prices

### Usage

```tsx
import { BlurCrossfade } from "@/components/ui/blur-crossfade";

export function SaveButton({ status }) {
  return (
    <button>
      <BlurCrossfade id={status} morph="both" as="span">
        {status === "saving" ? "Saving…" : status === "saved" ? "Saved" : "Save"}
      </BlurCrossfade>
    </button>
  );
}

// Height glides between messages of different length
<BlurCrossfade id={step}>
  <p>{steps[step]}</p>
</BlurCrossfade>
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | `string \| number` |  | Key of the current content – changing it starts the swap |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content for the current id |
| duration | `number` | `420` | Length of the swap and the size morph in ms |
| blur | `number` | `10` | Blur in px at the outer ends of the fade |
| morph | `"height" \| "both" \| "none"` | `"height"` | Which sides glide to the new size; both makes the box as wide as its content |
| as | `"div" \| "span"` | `"div"` | Root element – span inside buttons and other inline content |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the box |

### Accessibility

- Only the current content is exposed – the leaving copy is aria-hidden and inert
- Put aria-live on a surrounding element when the change should be announced, e.g. a status button

### Motion

- The old content blurs, fades and grows slightly as the new one sharpens in from 98 %, while the box glides to the new height (and width)
- Quick changes stay clean: only the latest leaving copy and the current content are ever on screen
- Reduced motion swaps instantly

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
- Content keeps its natural size; the box only clips during the swap, so shadows and focus rings show otherwise

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: text-reveal, gradient-text

---

## Gradient Floor (Pro)

A blurred colour gradient that glows up from the bottom edge – two layers that drift and morph

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/gradient-floor
- Section: Motion · Backgrounds
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/gradient-floor.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/gradient-floor`

### When to use

- Hero sections, AI features or call-to-action blocks that need a warm, living backdrop
- Behind a chat input or a prompt, to make it feel like the start of something

### When not to use

- Behind long body text – the bright floor competes with small type
- Several floors on one screen – each one runs its own animation

### Usage

```tsx
import { GradientFloor } from "@/components/ui/gradient-floor";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    // Give the floor a height, e.g. with a class
    <GradientFloor className="hero">
      <h1>Ideas start to glow</h1>
    </GradientFloor>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content rendered above the floor |
| colors | `[string, string, string]` | `["#FF7700", "#FF0055", "#0073FF"]` | Gradient from the crest down |
| speed | `number` | `3` | Seconds per morph loop; 0 keeps the shape still |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for height or rounded corners |

### Accessibility

- The floor layers are hidden from screen readers; only your children are announced
- Keep text above the bright part of the floor at a readable contrast

### Motion

- Two blurred layers – colour and a white plus-lighter layer – whose peaks and valleys rise and fall against each other
- Both layers drift sideways on the same beat, the light one a little less
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion the floor stays still

### Responsive

- Scales with the width of its container and stays anchored to the bottom edge – give the root a height
- Set the background with --ui-gf-bg (default #fafafa, dark mode #111113)

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: glow-keyboard, grid-background

## Gradient Text (Pro)

Letters cut from a liquid, ever-flowing gradient – the color sweeps across the word the first time it's seen

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/gradient-text
- Section: Motion · Text
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/gradient-text.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/gradient-text`

### When to use

- One word or a short phrase in a hero headline that should carry the brand
- A highlight inside a heading, like a product name or the payoff of a sentence

### When not to use

- Body copy or long passages – a moving gradient makes them harder to read
- Several highlights on one screen – the effect works because it's rare

### Usage

```tsx
import { GradientText } from "@/components/ui/gradient-text";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <h1>
      Interfaces people actually <GradientText>feel.</GradientText>
    </h1>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The text to fill with the gradient |
| colors | `string[]` | `["#dd0674", "#5e3ee0", "#ff5fae", "#7c5cff"]` | Gradient start, end and up to two blob colors; replaces the dark-mode colors too |
| speed | `number` | `8` | Seconds per flow cycle |
| sweep | `boolean` | `true` | Sweep the color in from left to right when the text scrolls into view |
| as | `"span" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "p"` | `"span"` | Element to render |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- The text stays real, selectable text – the gradient copy on top is aria-hidden
- Pick colors with enough contrast against your background; the defaults are tuned for white and near-black

### Motion

- Soft color blobs drift across a two-color base in a slow loop; the sweep wipes the color in once, the first time the text is 60% visible
- Reduced motion shows the finished gradient, standing still

### Responsive

- Font, size and weight come from the parent, so it scales with your headline
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: text-reveal

---

## Grid Background (Free)

A fine line grid that drifts slowly behind your content and fades out towards the edges

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/grid-background
- Section: Motion · Backgrounds
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/grid-background.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/grid-background`

### When to use

- Hero sections and feature headers that need a quiet, technical backdrop
- Empty states or panels that feel too flat on a plain background

### When not to use

- Behind dense text or data tables – the lines compete with the content
- Several moving backgrounds on one screen – keep it to one per view

### Usage

```tsx
import { GridBackground } from "@/components/ui/grid-background";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <GridBackground size={48} direction="diagonal">
      <section style={{ display: "grid", placeItems: "center", minHeight: 480 }}>
        <h1>Build on a steady grid</h1>
      </section>
    </GridBackground>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content rendered above the grid |
| size | `number` | `48` | Cell size in px |
| color | `string` | `rgba(0,0,0,.07)` | Line color; dark mode defaults to rgba(255,255,255,.07) |
| speed | `number` | `3` | Seconds per cell; 0 keeps the grid still |
| direction | `"up" \| "down" \| "left" \| "right" \| "diagonal"` | `"diagonal"` | Drift direction; diagonal runs from top right to bottom left |
| reveal | `boolean` | `true` | Uncover the grid with a circle growing from the center when it first comes into view |
| fade | `number` | `70` | Radius of the edge fade, in % of the distance to the corners |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the container – give it a height or let the content size it |

### Accessibility

- The grid layer is decorative: aria-hidden and pointer-events: none
- Content sits in its own layer above the grid and stays fully interactive

### Motion

- The lines move by exactly one cell per loop, so the drift is seamless; only transform is animated
- The reveal grows a circular mask from the center once, when the grid is 20% in view
- Reduced motion: the grid stays still and appears without the reveal

### Responsive

- Fills its container at any size; the fade follows the container's shape
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Number Ticker (Free)

Odometer-style numbers – every digit rolls to its new value and counts in from zero when it scrolls into view

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/number-ticker
- Section: Motion · Numbers
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/number-ticker.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/number-ticker`

### When to use

- KPIs, prices and counters that change while the user is looking, like dashboards or live stats
- Headline numbers on a landing page that should count in when they scroll into view

### When not to use

- Dense tables with many numbers – rolling digits everywhere becomes noise
- Values that change many times per second; the roll never settles

### Usage

```tsx
import { NumberTicker } from "@/components/ui/number-ticker";

export function RevenueKpi({ revenue }: { revenue: number }) {
  return (
    <p className="text-4xl font-semibold">
      <NumberTicker value={revenue} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 }} />
    </p>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `number` |  | The number to show – change it and the digits roll to the new value |
| format | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | Formatting, e.g. currency, percent, compact notation or fraction digits |
| locale | `string` | `browser locale` | Locale passed to Intl.NumberFormat, e.g. "en-US" or "de-DE" |
| duration | `number` | `900` | Length of a roll in milliseconds |
| delay | `number` | `0` | Wait before the first count-in, in milliseconds |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper – font size, weight and color are inherited |

### Accessibility

- The formatted value is in a visually hidden text inside an aria-live="polite" region, so screen readers hear the final number once
- The rolling digit columns are aria-hidden

### Motion

- Each digit rolls up when the value grows and down when it shrinks; new columns (9,999 → 10,000) slide in
- Counts in from 0 the first time it scrolls into view
- Reduced motion jumps straight to the value

### Responsive

- Inherits font size and weight from its parent and uses tabular numbers, so the width stays steady while rolling
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Shimmer Loader (Free)

Skeleton blocks that share one soft light sweep, plus shimmering text for “Thinking…” states

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/shimmer-loader
- Section: Motion · Loaders
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/shimmer-loader.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/shimmer-loader`

### When to use

- Placeholders while cards, lists or profiles load, shaped like the content that will arrive
- A shimmering status label while an AI answer or a long task is being generated

### When not to use

- Waits under ~300 ms – a flash of skeletons feels slower than showing nothing
- Progress you can measure; a progress bar tells the user how long is left

### Usage

```tsx
import { Skeleton, ShimmerText } from "@/components/ui/shimmer-loader";

export function PostSkeleton() {
  return (
    <div aria-busy="true" className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <Skeleton circle width={36} />
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Skeleton width={120} height={10} />
        <Skeleton width={80} height={8} />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export function Thinking() {
  return <ShimmerText>Generating summary…</ShimmerText>;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skeleton · width | `number \| string` | `"100%"` | Width – numbers are px, strings any CSS length |
| Skeleton · height | `number \| string` | `12` | Height – numbers are px |
| Skeleton · radius | `number \| string` | `6` | Corner radius |
| Skeleton · circle | `boolean` | `false` | Round shape that uses width for both sides, e.g. for avatars |
| Skeleton · className / style | `string / CSSProperties` |  | Extra class or inline styles on the block |
| ShimmerText · children | `ReactNode` |  | The label the highlight runs through |
| ShimmerText · duration | `number` | `2` | Seconds for one pass of the highlight |
| ShimmerText · className | `string` |  | Extra class – font size and weight are inherited |

### Accessibility

- Skeletons are aria-hidden – put aria-busy="true" on the container that is loading
- ShimmerText stays real text, so screen readers read the label normally

### Motion

- The skeleton highlight is pinned to the viewport, so all blocks share one sweep that travels across them together
- Reduced motion shows static placeholders and plain text

### Responsive

- Skeletons fill their container by default; set width for fixed shapes
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Text Reveal (Free)

Text that arrives word by word or letter by letter – each piece rises out of a soft blur as it scrolls into view

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/text-reveal
- Section: Motion · Text
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/text-reveal.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/text-reveal`

### When to use

- Headlines and short intros on landing pages that should arrive as you scroll
- A key sentence you want read in order, like a mission statement or a quote

### When not to use

- Long paragraphs or anything people need to read right away – waiting for words gets tiring
- Text that changes often, like live data – the reveal plays only when it enters the view

### Usage

```tsx
import { TextReveal } from "@/components/ui/text-reveal";

export function Intro() {
  return <TextReveal as="h2" text="Words that arrive one at a time." />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | `string` |  | The text to reveal |
| by | `"word" \| "char"` | `"word"` | Reveal word by word or letter by letter |
| stagger | `number` | `40` | Time between two pieces, in ms |
| delay | `number` | `0` | Wait before the first piece, in ms |
| duration | `number` | `700` | Time each piece takes to arrive, in ms |
| as | `"p" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "span"` | `"p"` | Element to render |
| once | `boolean` | `true` | Reveal only the first time; otherwise it plays again each time it enters the view |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Screen readers get the full sentence from a visually hidden copy; the animated pieces are aria-hidden
- Words never break in the middle, and spaces stay real, so lines wrap like normal text

### Motion

- Each piece fades in out of a blur while it rises a little, one after another, once 30% of the text is visible
- Reduced motion shows the text right away

### Responsive

- Font, size and color come from the parent, so it fits any heading or paragraph
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: gradient-text

## Tilt Card (Pro)

A card that tilts in 3D towards the pointer, with a soft glare that follows it and a smooth spring back

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/tilt-card
- Section: Motion · Hover
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/tilt-card.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/tilt-card`

### When to use

- Showcase cards: membership or pricing cards, product shots, featured items
- A single hero object that should feel tangible on hover

### When not to use

- Grids of many cards – the motion becomes noise when every card tilts
- Cards full of controls or text to read – the moving surface makes them harder to use

### Usage

```tsx
import { TiltCard } from "@/components/ui/tilt-card";

export function MembershipCard() {
  return (
    <TiltCard maxTilt={10} scale={1.02}>
      <div className="membership">
        <span>affectUI Pro</span>
        <span>•••• 4821</span>
      </div>
    </TiltCard>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The card's content – it fills the tilting surface |
| maxTilt | `number` | `10` | Maximum tilt in degrees |
| glare | `boolean` | `true` | Show a soft glare that follows the pointer |
| scale | `number` | `1.02` | Scale while the pointer is over the card |
| perspective | `number` | `900` | Perspective distance in px – smaller is more dramatic |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper; set --ui-tc-radius to match your card's corners |

### Accessibility

- Purely visual: the tilt adds no roles or tab stops, and the glare is aria-hidden
- Keyboard focus on anything inside the card lifts it slightly, so focus is visible in the motion too

### Motion

- Pointer moves are batched with requestAnimationFrame and written to CSS variables; only transform and opacity animate
- On leave the card springs back to rest with a soft overshoot
- Touch pointers don't tilt
- Reduced motion: no tilt or glare, only the shadow changes

### Responsive

- Sizes to its content; the demo card shrinks to the available width
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
